quoted_text:
Seele is a company that creates AI tools for game making. Recently they invited me to participate as they took on a 5-day challenge to push their new model, Seele03, to its limits and move closer and closer to AAA with a Wuxia-style action game.

The product consists of their AI model, asset generators, and target engines such as web (three.js), Unity, or even Unreal. What's nice is that their site has everything in one place, from mesh generators and rigging to sound fx and sprite work. They also provide common templates for most types of games. Having it all work together seamlessly saves a lot of time. You can get a game running very quickly, in 20 minutes or so. (20 minutes! I remember when this took months and months.)

So what can they do in 5 days?

Their progress video, below, shows them iterating through creating a Phantom Blade Zero-style game. This is not reverse engineering, but made from scratch. Over the course of development, they sent me video updates on their progress. The 03 model is designed for iterative development, and I gave them some advice as they took it from basically nothing to the final version of the video today. The progress the model made day to day was rapid, and the traces actually factored in something that I don't see that often: game design.

Most models focus on the graphics when making a game, but Seele03 is thinking about combos, hit feedback, everything that really matters for how a game feels and plays. One day, I think that's going to be the core of what makes AI game making viable.

After you are done prompting and refining your game, it's not frozen on the web. You can download and edit the project files themselves. Since you can download the result and open it in Godot or Unity (Unreal is embedded web atm), Seele03 can give you a quality core and a way for you to take things even further.

So how did it turn out? I've tried a lot of game generators, and Seele03's all-in-one tool approach and engine targeting stand out for me. Most others only generate three.js for web, or are more world models based on generative rendering. This is the rare one I've seen that is making games directly in game engines.

They've asked me to share the full process video with you so you can judge for yourself. As I watched the team work, I sat back and wondered at how it's all changing so fast: you simply... chat... interacting with a UI that is purely text, typing in wishes and directions, and everything else unfolds around you. I think they got pretty far in their goal gameplay-wise, which is where they really focused. The key thing is that after you have the final result, you also have the files to download, and you can replace anything you want to take it even further: animations, level graphics, basically anything.

If you want to make games for real engines on PC and console, then give Seele a shot at https://t.co/jJ9kvt0Ard. It's faster than vibing a game in Claude because of their game-design-driven model, their built-in asset generators, and the fact that you are not burning tokens re-creating an entire engine before you even get to your game. And every day they get closer to AAA... it's just a matter of time.

这两天做了一个有意思的事情，把我的全部的 Skills 删除了将近 1/3，同时把所有项目的上下文也都优化了一下，感觉干净清爽了不少，我认为随着模型能力越来越厉害，我们有经常去更新裁剪我们的项目的一些给到模型的上下文信息，防止你的内容反而阻碍了模型的发挥。

于是我就把最近做的继续沉淀成一些大伙也用得上的提示词，可以直接给到你的 Agent 去帮你优化你的项目的内容要求和 Skills，已经安装 Waza 的小伙伴可以直接更新到最新然后说「帮我精简一下规则」就好，也可以 Copy 下面内容给你的Agent。

帮我精简这个项目给 Agent 的上下文和我装的 Skills，按下面的要求来，先整理出清单给我确认，确认前先不改任何文件。

1. 先盘点每轮对话都会加载的内容，包括根目录的 AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md、全局规则、没写 paths: 的 .claude/rules 和每个 skill 的描述，看各占多少字，再看按需加载的部分，这里不少看着臃肿的内容可能不是写多了，而是放的位置不对。

2. 逐段给出处理方式，分成修、删、挪、改写、保留五种，挪的写清目的地，每条附一句原因，做成一张清单给我确认。

3. 逐句判断删掉后你的行为会不会变，把类似这种「先读再改」「跑测试」「注意边界」你本来就会做的描述删掉，拿不准的可以先保留找我确定。

4. 我们更加推崇是给 Agent 写目标，少些如何实现的路线，写清做完是什么样、怎么算完成、要什么证据，一个步骤删掉后你还能换条路做到同样结果就删掉，只有顺序本身是约束的才留下来，比如先验证再发布、先确认再删除这种需要保留。

5. 同一种要求说了三遍，换成一个你本来就懂的词语，比如「快、确定、开销小」可以写成 tight；「要简洁」这类口号换成一个更好理解的想想的词语比如「报告腔」，然后再配一组 NO / OK 例子。

6. 把对应内容放对位置，需要判断的进 skill，同样输入总是同样输出的改成脚本或 hook，项目命令和发布步骤进项目指南，跨项目的硬约束才放进全局规则，遇到「做 Y 之前先读 X」这类要求改成做 Y 时由 hook 把 X 注入进来更好。

7.  skill 描述只写做什么、什么时候用、不用于什么，近义词移到 when_to_use，只有部分场景用到的内容移到 references；判断一个 skill 有没有人用，要看真实调用记录，不要只 grep 名字，要删的也先列给我看一下。

8. 这些内容不要删除：
    - 我的偏好、被否掉的方案和原因、机器环境。
    - 不报错的坑，以及看着像出错其实正常的现象。
    - 描述句里「从不写入」「不上传」这类半句约束。
    - 删数据、需要花钱、要发布、提权、改写已推送历史这些不可逆操作的规则。
    - 我们带日期的拍板决策记录。

9.  内容先移到对应正确的位置再来压缩，能整行搬到按需加载的文件里就整行搬，不要边搬边改写，不可逆的规则原样整段搬。

10. 把内容搬到能自己加载的地方可以参考这些技巧：
      - 提交、发布、回复、删除这类对话里随时会触发的规则留在根目录。
      - 挪进 docs/ 的要在根目录留一句什么时候去读。
      - 根目录不要建 CLAUDE.md，它会让 Claude Code 不再读 AGENTS.md。
      - 项目里重复全局规则的句子，只有在我用的每个工具都读全局规则时才删。

11. 改完以后自己去查一遍：paths: 里的 glob 都要能匹配到真实文件，grep 一遍拆走的旧文件名，再列出所有消失的行，每一行都要对上清单里我确认过的删除。

12. 交给一个没参与精简的 Agent 查有没有删过度了，只给它消失的行和仓库，不给你的结论，让它搜关键名词而不是整句，意思在哪都找不到的原样恢复。

13.  验证移过去的内容真的会被加载：在新文件里埋一个暗号，开一个新会话，先读一个匹配的文件再问它暗号，然后读一个不匹配的文件做反向对照。

14. 最后全部做完以后，可以帮我沉淀一下这个思路，方便以后有模型升级的时候，我可以再来跑一遍。

text:
Stupid, stupid, stupid. The 2019 University of Washington glyphosate study is one of the most notorious and frequently cited papers among activist scientists seeking to falsely link the herbicide to cancer. Its headline claim—that glyphosate exposure increases the risk of non-Hodgkin lymphoma by 41%—is flat out wrong. It has been repeatedly challenged by mainstream scientists for selectively misrepresenting the underlying evidence, particularly findings from the massive, long-running Agricultural Health Study.

The problem wasn’t merely that the researchers reached a questionable conclusion. It was how they manipulated the statistical presentation to produce a frightening result that the strongest underlying evidence did not support. Epidemiologist Geoffrey Kabat is one of many experts who exposed the methodological failures in a series of detailed analyses published by the Genetic Literacy Project, the nonprofit that I founded. 

Here’s what the researchers actually did—and why their widely publicized conclusion is so misleading.

1. They cherry-picked the one estimate that supported their hypothesis. The Agricultural Health Study, which followed tens of thousands of pesticide applicators, examined glyphosate exposure using several latency periods. Four of the five estimates showed no increased cancer risk; the fifth, using a 20-year lag, suggested a small, statistically insignificant increase. The 2019 researchers selected that fifth estimate for their meta-analysis—and ignored all the other evidence. That’s science malfeasance. 

2. The AHS, a large prospective study conducted by federal scientists, found ZERO statistically significant association between glyphosate exposure and non-Hodgkin lymphoma overall, including among the most heavily exposed workers. The 41% figure did not come from the AHS. It emerged from combining the researchers’ selected AHS estimate with five smaller case-control studies. it was concocted by these now notorious scientists and then aggressively misrepresented as government data. 

3. Unlike the prospective AHS, retrospective case-control studies rely on reconstructing past exposures, sometimes decades later. It’s made up by researchers based on interviews. ZERO hard data. It’s about feelings and decades-old recollections. Anecdotes, not science. Such studies are soaked in recall bias, exposure misclassification, and confounding. Pooling them with the AHS did not eliminate those weaknesses, though it did fool the original wave of media which misrepresented this made-up study when it first appeared.

4. The activists relied on a questionable latency assumption. They justified selecting the 20-year lag by hypothesizing (made it up out of whole cloth) that glyphosate-related cancers would require a long latency period. But they lacked convincing glyphosate-specific evidence establishing that assumption, which is now known as false. Their preferred lag just so happened to produce the estimate most supportive of their hypothesis—what a surprise!!! 

5. Their fake alarming result was based entirely on that statistical sleight of hand. After publication, the EPA reanalyzed the meta-analysis using a different AHS estimate, the pooled relative risk fell from 1.41 to approximately 1.14 and was no longer statistically significant.

The larger lesson here  is that the botched meta-analysis generated a fake, highly politicized narrative. Selective choices about which data to include profoundly distorted the result, transforming negative findings from the most substantial prospective study into an alarming headline that continues to circulate years after its methodological weaknesses were exposed. You fell for it. Stupid, stupid, stupid.

Read Geoffrey Kabat’s detailed investigation:

The glyphosate debacle: How a misleading study about the weedkiller Roundup and gullible reporters helped fuel a cancer scare — Genetic Literacy Project, February 9, 2021

text:
A 74-year-old grandmother shot her 17-year-old grandson six times. He was on the phone with 911, bleeding on the floor, begging for help  when she walked up and fired again.

Jonathan Hoffman wasn’t even supposed to be living with his grandparents. His little sister had a brain tumor, and his parents had moved to Arizona to be with her through treatment. So Jonathan stayed behind in Michigan with Sandra Layne  an arrangement meant to keep him steady while he dealt with his own problems. He was on probation. He’d struggled with drugs.

On May 18, 2012, he failed a drug test for synthetic marijuana. That same day, the two of them argued. Layne would later say her grandson demanded $2,000 and a car, hit her, and chased her through the house. So she got her gun.

Over about six minutes, she fired ten shots. Six hit him  two in the back. He was in gym shorts and socks. There was nowhere for him to go.

In the middle of it, Jonathan managed to call 911. The dispatcher heard him say: “My grandma shot me. I’m gonna die. Help.” And then, while he was still on the line, another gunshot. “I got shot again,” he said.

When police arrived, Sandra Layne walked out holding the gun and told them: “I murdered my grandson.” Jonathan died at the hospital.

At trial she said it was self-defense  a frightened old woman protecting herself from a violent teenager high on drugs. But she had no visible injuries. And the jury kept coming back to that 911 recording: a dying boy on the phone, and the sound of his own grandmother firing again. Second-degree murder. At least 22 years.

The coldest verdict didn’t come from the jury. It came from her own daughter  Jonathan’s mother  who refused to call her “mom” in that courtroom and said Sandra Layne was “pure evil.”

So here’s what the case never fully settled: was this a terrified grandmother defending her life from a violent, drug-addicted teenager  or a woman who chased a boy in socks around her house and kept pulling the trigger while he begged a stranger to save him?

text:
Recently, I've been working on reviving and modding an abandoned open-source Android project. It was originally for a client, but since the original project is open-source, I've decided to release my version for free!

I've added remote device management features using a self-hosted Supabase backend, allowing you to control your Android devices from anywhere in the world.

With just one click, you can remotely trigger a factory reset and completely wipe your Android device. You can also remotely lock the screen if you don't want to erase everything.

This can be useful in situations like phone theft, personal security, or simply managing your devices remotely.

The web dashboard acts as a cockpit where you can monitor and control all your Android devices from one place.

The backend is self-hostable, so you can run it yourself without relying on a paid service.

Previously, in v2.0, I implemented local P2P network control, allowing devices connected to the same Wi-Fi network to remotely trigger a factory reset.

But v3.0 is changing the game! Now, instead of being limited to the same local network, you can remotely control your devices from anywhere in the world.

I'm planning to release v3.0 in the next few days. Eventually, I also plan to rebrand the project as a separate app with its own identity and a complete modern UI/UX overhaul, as the original app is quite complicated and not very user-friendly.

Stay tuned, and follow for updates! 👀

quoted_text:
Why ETH is the store of value for what's coming

We are almost certainly heading into a period of high inflation and extreme economic and social volatility. As inflation and risk erode the purchasing power of nation-state money and many other assets, it will matter more than ever to hold assets that keep or grow their value.

Gold and BTC are high-powered money and excellent stores of value. ETH goes further.

Not debt-based. Like gold and BTC, ETH is not debt-based or credit-based money.

Censorship resistant. Like BTC, or gold and silver held physically, ETH transactions on Ethereum L1 can't be censored. That's true for simple payments and for complex smart contract programs like DeFi, and those programs are guaranteed to execute.

Cheap to hold. Like BTC, ETH is relatively cheap to hold and store securely.

Cheap to use at any scale. Ethereum is cheap and easy to use whether a transaction moves $1 or billions. Any well-formed transaction is guaranteed to execute.

Sound, and getting sounder. ETH is disinflationary and becomes ultrasound, meaning deflationary, during periods of high network activity.

Broadly useful. ETH has many uses across the Ethereum economy, and that economy will grow by orders of magnitude as finance, and eventually every industry, moves onchain. Global adoption of the Web protocols in the '90s and '00s transformed the world economy. Ethereum is the foundation of Web3, the user-centric, decentralized web.

Collateral money. ETH works as collateral, and collateral that grows in value over time is a powerful thing.

Home of stablecoins. Ethereum hosts the bulk of stablecoin activity. Stablecoins serve as payment money and as unit-of-account money.

Despot-proof. Like BTC, ETH can't be used by a despot to financially exploit or repress citizens. Over time that should have positive geopolitical effects.

Programmable. ETH is programmable money. You can attach arbitrary logic to transactions and build an entire economy on smart-contract-based agreements and business processes (see https://t.co/JcWtBUclr2).

Transparent or private, and auditable either way. Money and financial instruments on Ethereum can be public or private, and in both cases selectively disclosable and auditable. Privacy tools for retail and institutional users include VPNs, mix networks, shielded and privacy pools, Railgun, stealth addresses, Kohaku, and zero-knowledge proofs in many forms, including on L2s and on private permissioned EVM networks linked through bridgeless synchronous composability.

Future-proof. By the end of 2027, or partway through 2028 at the latest, ETH will be quantum-safe and AI-safe money.

ETH is the base money of an exponentially growing ecosystem that should keep growing for decades. Its monetary premium will keep rising, because retail, corporate, and government users will all need to hold some. Part of today's premium is speculative: Ethereum dominates smart contract blockchains, but it hasn't fully hit its stride or gone mainstream yet.

Machine intelligence will supercharge every scientific and technological pursuit and grow global GDP bigger and faster than any of us can imagine. Ethereum L1 and modular Ethereum L2s will undergird most of the high-value agreements, transactions, payment flows, and complex business processes behind the coming hybrid human-machine decentralized economy.

text:
No matter what you guys thing about jensen huang he still one of the best CEO and Founder 

You can hate Jensen Huang. You can criticize him. You can question everything happening around him right now.

But if you’re going to erase everything he built because of the controversies surrounding him, you’re missing the bigger picture.

Jensen Huang co-founded NVIDIA in 1993 and stayed at the helm for more than three decades. He led the company through market crashes, brutal competition, major technological shifts, and moments when NVIDIA’s future was anything but guaranteed.

He didn’t just build another semiconductor company. He helped turn NVIDIA from a graphics-chip company into one of the most important computing and AI platforms in the world.

That doesn’t make him untouchable. Personal conduct, corporate governance, national-security concerns, and any allegations surrounding NVIDIA deserve serious scrutiny. Accountability matters.

But accountability and historical evaluation are not the same thing.

You can condemn someone's actions without pretending their achievements never happened.

You don’t have to like Jensen Huang.

You don’t have to like NVIDIA.

But if we’re talking about the greatest founders and CEOs of the modern technology industry, his name belongs in the conversation.

That’s simply a fact worth acknowledging.

author: TokenPocket_TP
quoted_text:
🚨 SlowMist TI Alert: iOS sandbox escape 0day PoC “worse_query” disclosed 🚨

A public PoC for a sandbox escape 0day, worse_query, targets iOS 26.0–26.7.2 and iOS 27.2. It is the successor to bad_query. 📱

⚠️ This is a container sandbox escape, not a jailbreak. It breaks the assumption that apps can’t see each other: a malicious app that successfully exploits it can reach system paths and read or modify other apps’ data.

💸 The bug does not steal assets by itself. The real risk starts when a user installs an app from an untrusted source, such as a sideloaded IPA. If a wallet stores its seed phrase, keystore or WebView cache in plaintext locally, a malicious app could read it.

🛡️ Recommendations:
🔸 Don’t install IPAs or apps from unknown sources
🔸 Keep iOS up to date and install Apple’s fix as soon as one is released
🔸 Wallet developers: don’t store sensitive data in plaintext locally
🔸 If you installed an untrusted app on a device holding wallets, treat it as risky and consider moving assets to a new wallet created on a clean device

🔗 https://t.co/sIP4hX85TR

text:
今天起正式加入 @MojoAI_HQ 了，和 @ForestBai1 @msfew_eth @jenniekusu @0xBenniee 等很多小伙伴一起build AI 个人财富助手事业 🫡 . 

半年以前和一个资深做量化的朋友探讨，AI之于交易到底能有什么意义。他的看法是团队至少探索了7～8年了，目前得出的结论是没什么意义。

但在我的视角里，如果一场全面改写交互方式的革命已经席卷一切软件，而唯独金融/交易领域还没开始 / 还没有人做的足够好，那么这就是值得投入的红利期，虽然这种红利可能在大多数whales眼里看不上，也不会太久，且以后窗口期也只会越来越短。

更朴实的，这个世界属于绝大多数人。尽管 AI 在“赚钱”“暴富”上可能还无法成为无所不能的印钞机，但用过 mojo 以后，我发现至少我们“抓机会”的能力已经可以全面平权了。

“AI 交易” 实际上是一种对 AI 金融领域能力的狭隘想象。这个行业真的靠交易暴富的人，我相信也孑孑寥寥。我相信绝大多数能够翻身的人，本质还是靠的毒辣的机会嗅觉、敢于重仓的赌性和超绝执行力。而最后一步，往往是很多人止步于机会大门前的最后一道门槛。链上信号、狙击、快进快出、多号快速分发与收集…… 很多人不是不知道什么机会好，但是工具和执行细节的缺失让他们无法抓住机会。

用过 Mojo 以后，我发现这是我想做的事情。一句话跨链，一句话创建原本大科学家才能创建的监控和脚本，一句话学习&模仿其他作者的agent模板（是的，就像grok bot那样）…… 我不指望 AI 能让我赚多少钱，但我相信钱包 / 交易所 / 跨链 / DEX ……这些2018/2019 以来就没怎么变过的行业基础设施，应该变一变，变得更顺手，好用，理解我，能够救急，能够真的抓住机会。 

综上，很荣幸能和 Mojo 团队一起探索这种未来。🫡 

Glad to announce that I've officially joined @MojoAI_HQ to build an AI personal wealth agent with @ForestBai1 @msfew_eth @jenniekusu @0xBenniee and a lot of other great people 🫡

About six months ago, I was talking with a friend who's a veteran quant about what AI actually means for trading. His take: his team had been exploring it for at least 7-8 years, and their conclusion so far was that it doesn't mean much.

But the way I see it, if a revolution in how we interact with software is sweeping through everything, and finance/trading is the one place where it hasn't started, or where no one has done it well enough yet, then this is a window worth betting on. Most whales probably won't care about it, it won't last long, and these windows will only keep getting shorter.

Put more simply, this world belongs to the vast majority of people. AI may not be an all-powerful money printer that makes you rich overnight, but after using Mojo, I've realized that at the very least, the ability to catch opportunities can now be truly democratized.

"AI trading" is actually a pretty narrow way to imagine what AI can do in finance. I believe the people who've truly gotten rich from trading alone are few and far between. Most people who turn their lives around do it with a razor-sharp nose for opportunity, the guts to go big, and insane execution. And that last step is often the final barrier that stops people right at the door. On-chain signals, sniping, fast in and out, dealing assets on multiple chains... Plenty of people know a good opportunity when they see one, but they miss it because they don't have the tools or can't handle the execution details.

After using Mojo, I knew this was what I wanted to work on. Bridge across chains in one sentence. In one sentence, create the kind of monitors and scripts that only elite degen could build before. In one sentence, learn from and copy other creators' agent templates (yes, just like grok bot)... I don't expect AI to make me a ton of money, but I do believe that wallets, exchanges, bridges, DEXs ... all this infra that has barely changed since 2018/2019, should change. It should be smoother and easier to use, it should understand me, it should be able to bail me out in a pinch, and it should actually help me catch real alphas.

All of which is to say: I'm honored to explore this future with the Mojo team. 🫡

text:
老李的 UMX @UMX_CN 上线了 UMI 积分计划，

积分 UMI 中文名称更好记，就叫：有米！
很多人私信我问询这个交易所是什么以及积分有啥用，这里给大家做个统一的回复，方便大家理解：

UMX 作为老李的再创业，这个交易所和其他交易所还是有着不太一样的定位，把老李家办的一些好的策略用到了财富管理系统，所以我在看来，主要的功能在于财富的管理和增值，所以你们进去后也能看到他的至臻理财和私行特供这种内容。

我估摸着大家之前关注好像主要是因为存款赠送 Iphone Duo 的活动，但是注册发现不接受国内身份注册，

其实注册并不难，可以用国内护照+海外生活地址证明来注册即可，海外地址证明别问我，我相信你们都能搞到。

然后今天上线的这个 11 月 11 日至 17 日开启首期活动，简单研究了一下规则，有几个值得关注的地方，也有一些需要理性看待的问题。

1️⃣ 积分机制

活动期间，符合条件的现货、合约及期权交易，可以获得常规规则下 3 倍的 UMI 积分。
积分主要根据实际支付的交易手续费计算，而不是简单按照交易量计算。

2️⃣ 500 万积分奖池

首期奖池为 500 万 UMI，不设置单账户积分上限。
但需要注意，这不是 500 万美元的奖励。如果全平台累计积分超过奖池，最终会按比例缩减。

3️⃣ 积分未来价值

这是我认为最值得关注的东西。
UMI 积分未来具体能兑换什么、如何定价、什么时候可以兑换，目前还没有明确答案，但是我大胆猜测一下，这个积分我看 @DujunX 杜老板说这可能会是最大的空投，
那会不会可能是某种股权？会不会可能要上市后的原始股兑换凭证？
当然这只是我的猜测，我也不确定会不会有这么一天。

我个人而言，对这类活动的态度一直比较简单：如果本来就有真实交易需求，顺便积累一些积分，可能是额外的潜在权益。

但如果为了积分刻意增加交易量、承担额外手续费和交易风险，就需要重新算账了。

大家可以自行研究下。

昨天凌晨和下午，特别是前天晚上美股爆拉的时候，被btc和zec的走势搞破防了，严重失望，跑了很多，然后cpi出来之后在盯盘突然1分钟线有人爆砸，跟着把现货也砸完了，差不多均价1130-1150吧没具体算，zec回撤了一半的利润，但也总算落袋为安。浮盈不是盈，浮亏不是亏，海力士能浮亏变不亏，zec也能浮盈送回去大半，都是正常的，心情反而轻松了。另外zec的走势基本上都蛮标准，没什么心机，很传统，是一个很好的交易标的。

btc的话因为81000加过仓，跌到现在也差不多到均价了，利润都没了。

周一开盘，外围涨这么好，btc周线五连阴，这不来个大阳？那这明显就还不是牛市，牛市里比特币周线四连阴都撑死了，能这样阴跌6周太久了，我不是看空，就是卖的人手里也没多少货了，买的人也没有了。再看eth好了，能把启动线都快跌完了，这哪里是牛市的走法。绝对不可能持有eth作为长线的我怕睡不着，就你看这个图哪能看出长线价值，只有交易价值。

吐槽完了，说说好的，往好点想，我只是认为现在还没牛市，但我还是乐观的人。最硬的zec补跌了，往往大盘也就跌不动了，我真不知道现在btc要干嘛，不一定跌也不一定涨，每个熊市底部都是低流动性的时间，这时候正是回到了慢慢进长期货的阶段了，我现在手里子弹突然充裕了，不妨又定投个几个月？

zec我没那么悲观，因为牛市都没来，就已经是最强的了，虽然有可能，但我无法去幻想牛市来了他就会是最弱的，trade what you see, not what you imagine, I will be back.

text:
Anthropic Stake Divested Early by FTX Now Worth Over $30 Billion

According to Anthropic's latest prospectus, the firm plans to offer 825M Class A shares priced at $70–$78 each, implying a ~$1.2T–$1.4T valuation. FTX and affiliates invested ~$500M in 2021–2022 for an initial ~8% stake, now worth ~$31.2B–$34.7B at the IPO range. However, during its 2024 bankruptcy restructuring, FTX trustees fully liquidated the stake in batches at ~$30/share to secure liquidity for cash payouts, recouping only ~$1.34B. With FTX owing creditors ~$11.2B at collapse, retaining the shares would have repaid the entire debt nearly 3x over.

text:
美国财政部11月初QRA解读与未来三个月流动性推演，上周财政部公布了最新的季度再融资声明，对于之后三个月流动性的走势很有指向意义。也来聊聊：
1、季度再融资详情
1）四季度私人部门净市场化借款从6280亿美元下调至6180亿，表面减少100亿，但隐含短债净融资反而上调150亿至3320亿；
2）附息类证券净发行维持3610亿，回购假设从500亿提至750亿，扣除后附息类净融资减少250亿，差额由短债补齐。季初现金比原预期多出340亿是下调的主因，剔除后实际融资需求反而更高。
3）中长期国债单次拍卖规模维持不变：2年690亿、3年580亿、5年700亿、7年440亿，10年/20年/30年延续现有新券与续发安排。未来三个月无新增扩容压力，远端指引则略有松动，TBAC纪要提及2027财年下半年或增发，集中在2-10年期。

意味着27年上半年内长债的发行规模要么维持不变、要么还可能略微减少；
对长债而言，拍卖规模稳定叠加回购，暂时减轻久期供给压力，期限溢价或受支撑，当然长端中长期还是取决于增长与通胀预期。

2、TGA路径
季度再融资声明给出了TGA两个月内峰值与一个季末锚：11月下旬和2027年1月下旬TGA或达1.025万亿（±500亿），12月底则维持8500亿目标不变；
以11月4日准备金2.963万亿、TGA 0.936万亿为基准（合计约3.899万亿），在隔夜逆回购已经见底的情况，TGA的增减直接会导致银行准备金的减增。

正好测算下路径：
1）11月下旬TGA现金峰值对应准备金约2.87万亿；
2）12月底TGA降至8500亿，准备金回升至约3.05万亿（基本上也就是9月下旬的高点水平）；
3）1月下旬再次冲高至1.025万亿，准备金回落至约2.87万亿。

11月9日TGA已降至9226亿，下旬前仍有约1000亿现金重建压力，对应准备金回笼；
12月若从高点释放1750亿，改善空间明确，1月则因季节性支出前补现金，年底释放部分将被收回。

结算节奏上，
11月16日、30日及12月中下旬附息债与税款入账可能带来阶段性波动。一季度净借款升至8000亿，主要因现金管理方向反转（四季度动用存量、一季度需补充），而非单纯赤字扩大。

3、对大饼这种与流动性关系密切的资产来说，之前这里https://t.co/eVTr1w4UJY有梳理过往关于大饼与准备金的走势关系、跟美股相关性则会小一点。
这相当于是一张资金时间表：
11月下旬前留意现金重建再度收紧；
12月有改善的概率很大，
1月需重新评估财政部补现金与美联储操作的合力。

准备金回升可缓解银行约束，当前最清晰的锚还是12月底8500亿的现金目标。

那么来看11月下旬之前，流动性还是在一个低位徘徊，所以11月中长线来说还是逢低买。而12月流动性释放整体来准备金有一个比较大的回升，可能带动大饼走出一波📈行情。上周聊认为年底加密有一波行情，也是从流动性的角度来看的。

这两天币市的悲观情绪又很浓，个人角度依然认为认为新的周期在开启，只是在流动性回暖之前还需要熬一熬。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
看好年底的加密行情，两个逻辑：
第一是流动性回升，看本周财政部公布的季度再融资计划很重要的一点就是财政部TGA账户12月底的目标8500亿美金、相比10月底最高1.05万亿美金将下降2000亿美金，这也会推动银行准备金走高、变相的财政宽松。大饼及加密资产跟准备金为核心的美元流动性关系很密切，流动性回升大饼自然也起来。

第二个点，代币化RWA趋势会加快，特别是来自SEC和CFTC的推动力。中期选举民主党掌控参众两院，短期内国会立法很难期待。而作为推动代币化rwa、放松加密监管的最核心行政机构SEC和CFTC自然会更积极推动这个趋势，有两个用意：
1）抢时间，抢在明年1月初新当选议员履行之前，在职责权限范围内把政策口子打得更开、未来两个月我们可能会看到sec和cftc在政策上的节奏越来越快，力度也越来越大。
2）出成绩，这一届sec和cftc的主席都是川普透明的、任期还有两年多。他们已经在推动放松加密和代币化趋势、自然是想未来任期结束会做出成绩来。

当然看好加密行情、并不是所有资产都看好（大部分山寨还是得谨慎），大饼自不用说、个人最看好的还是代币化大趋势下的几个核心受益标的：
$coin $hood $CRCL 
$eth $bnb  $uni $aave  $okb $sol $hype $sky
之前7月份https://t.co/pqYyjtubr7就有聊到这些。

再回看，8月下旬认为当时那波行情要持续到9月中下旬，9月底开始提示回调认为10月整体有个回调。这里都有https://t.co/8AoQRzsPno梳理到；
10月底https://t.co/ai3MsGZC8M认为币安被盗是加速调整到位。
现在看大饼走势基本上都在推演框架内。

当然开头说看好年底行情，不是说明年就很差，还是之前聊到的大周期已经开始向上了，三大动力https://t.co/DySEm9QLXW，但向上也不是说一直往上、中间还会有不少大级别的回踩调整震荡，只能说走一步看一步了。

author: 0x_JBCat
quoted_text:
你根本不知道，做 KOL/KOC 有多难。

聊这个话题，我大概率算是整个中文币圈里，少数几个走出不同路径的人。

先说结论：做 KOL/KOC，人脉真的太重要了。

如果有 10 个人愿意稳定给你介绍合作，基本上你就能在币圈活下去。

当然，最舒服的还是傍上交易所包月，毕竟这玩意儿才是稳定现金流。做的好的群友，基本都吃上了。

如果你没吃上，那就只能靠自己的「舔功」上位了。

我个人的路径几乎没法复制。机缘巧合之下拉了个全真社区，又机缘巧合火了一段时间，才让我没有饿死。

但绝大多数 KOL/KOC，尤其是账号质量一般、又没什么资源的新人，走的完全是另一条路。

那就是不停地舔，拼命往圈子里挤。

你可能需要加入十几个 KOL 社区，天天在里面混脸熟，先从陌生人混成普通朋友，再从普通朋友混成好朋友，最后才有可能换来一点合作机会。

这个过程非常累，甚至可以说非常痛苦。

因为作为一个新人，你在别人眼里几乎是零价值的。

没人认识你，没人认可你，更没人有义务带你赚钱。

你只能不断展示自己的价值，就像一个拼命追着镜头跑的十八线小明星，生怕错过任何一次露脸的机会。

即便如此，成功率依然低得可怜。

你可能尝试了 100 次，只有 1 次有效。更绝望的是，剩下 99 次失败之后，面对同一批人，把同样的事情再做一遍。

再聊聊更现实的：送礼。

之前就听说，很多 KOL 为了拿合作，是需要给 BD 送礼的。

我自己暂时没送过，但几个好基友一直劝我送。

因为确实有几个 BD 对我特别好，基本属于把饭喂到嘴边了。说实话，这礼我确实该送，只是一直没送而已。

而且送礼也是一门学问，送什么、什么时候送、怎么送，都有讲究。

我个人的理解是，很多时候最难的不是花钱，而是让人家愿意收。

如果对方愿意接受你一份价值不低的礼物，至少说明你们的关系已经到了某个程度。

你送出去一万块，未来人家可能通过合作给你带来远超一万块的价值。

但你以为送礼就已经够离谱了？

不好意思，这可能还只是最低档。

我听过的其他案例，包括但不限于：

通宵陪打游戏。
甚至陪睡觉的传闻。

陪打游戏我还能理解，毕竟就是牺牲点时间。

但陪睡觉，我特么是真的觉得离谱。

当然，若是大哥想让你陪睡觉，到也是一个机会，睡对了大哥，就算你是个职校生，睡上一次，B也涨价了。这也是捞女为什么被骂。因为他们确实找到了捷径。

不过话又说回来，为什么有些人总喜欢走捷径？

因为在一个高度依赖资源、人脉和利益交换的行业里，有时候你辛辛苦苦努力一年，可能真不如别人认识一个大哥。

这也是为什么，有些人明明没什么专业能力，却能拿到远超普通人的资源。

你可以不认可这种方式，但很难否认资源关系带来的巨大差距。

所以我现在越来越觉得，普通男 KOL 想在币圈混出头，是真的难。

如果你本身就有钱、有资源、有背景，那当然舒服。

但如果你什么都没有，只是一个普通人，想靠写内容、做研究、慢慢积累粉丝，然后靠这个养活自己……

说实话，真的得做好吃屎的准备。

这个行业表面上拼的是内容，实际上拼的是资源、人脉、情商，还有你能承受多少次被拒绝。

而最残酷的地方在于：

你以为自己是在和别人的内容竞争，实际上你可能连礼都送不出去。

author: eldarcap
quoted_text:
I believe ETH will eventually replace BTC as crypto’s primary store of value. And Bitcoin’s future may look a lot more like DOGE than people want to admit.

Look at Dogecoin. Its market value and cultural influence have survived, but its underlying network has become increasingly marginal. Today, it has fewer than 500 publicly reachable nodes. In 2024, a single old laptop exploited an unpatched vulnerability and crashed 69% of its publicly visible nodes.

DOGE didn’t die. Its price, community and meme survived. Its mining security now largely depends on merged mining with Litecoin. That’s the fascinating part: a cryptocurrency can remain valuable even as its own network becomes less economically relevant.

Bitcoin is obviously much stronger today. But I’m looking at the next 10 or 20 years, not today.

Stablecoins, RWAs, lending, financial markets, digital art and countless other assets are building an increasingly substantial economy on Ethereum. Even BTC needs to become wrapped BTC to participate in much of that economy.

I believe the most important store of value in crypto will eventually be the native asset of the network that holds the most economic value, not necessarily the coin that came first.

That’s why I agree with Vitalik’s focus on ETH as a store of value. Ethereum doesn’t need to maximize fee burns. It needs to become indispensable.

BTC may survive as digital gold, or eventually as a giant meme. ETH has a chance to become the reserve asset of an entire onchain economy.

text:
为什么投 AngelList 这一段好有意思

VC 是罕见的 mean 高于 median 的行业，大多数player都亏钱。当时想进入硅谷一级市场，一定需要新的venture模式，传统模式直接介入硅谷像很多欧洲老牌vc尝试过全部失败，因为抢不到最好的deal flow。

AngelList 的模式恰好卡在那个窗口期：它给那些有 scout 能力、靠关系能拿到小额 angel 额度、但自己没钱批量投的人搭平台。当时平台自身资本还不多、scout 的摩擦偏大，正需要引入机构 LP 来扩张规模、验证模式、把摩擦降下来。

因此吴主导中科招商成为了 AngelList 最大的机构 LP。更关键的是通过这个入口接触到硅谷真正优质的 deal flow，包括在 Stripe 50 亿估值时拿到额度。

回头看，投 AngelList 本身的那一个亿现在大概三个亿，回报并不夸张。那几年独角兽数量本身就有 power law 的通胀，真正赚大钱的反而是后面更后期、容量更大的 deal。付给 AngelList 的 carry，更像一张进入硅谷核心圈层的门票钱。

Anthropic IPO 市场到底给多少？我对过 S-1/A，各方数字的分歧只在股本口径，有的说只剩一万亿，也有说在1.2～1.4万亿的，具体究竟如何？实际是完全稀释市值和流通市值的区别

$ANT 区间 70 至 78 美元，发行 8.25 亿股，另有谷歌、英伟达等合计 260 亿美元同价私募。按流通股算，约 131 亿股，对应 0.92 万亿至 1.02 万亿美元。

按完全稀释算，约 180 亿股，含期权、RSU、亚马逊可转债，对应 1.26 万亿至 1.40 万亿美元，中值 1.33 万亿。市场谈的估值是后者。

按中值算，10 月 run-rate 810 亿美元对应约 16 倍 PS，Q3 年化 678 亿美元对应约 20 倍。

FT 称投行考虑把估值抬到 1.5 万亿以上，约合每股 83 至 84 美元，不过目前只有 FT 一家报道。11/18 定价，11/19 交易。

约 9684 亿美元那个数字是流通股口径，被错标成完全稀释，所以 12 倍、14 倍这类 PS 都被低估了一档。

Q3 确认营收 169.6 亿美元，过去十二个月约 353 亿美元，按这个算 PS 约 38 倍。run-rate 是最近 28 天消费收入乘 13，再加月订阅乘 12，波动比较大。

独立开发者 @yetone 开发的 Alma，在最新一轮 AI Agent 横评中，同时拿下任务通过率和成功成本第三名，把 Claude Code、OpenCode 等知名工具甩在了身后。

这次评测由 AI Agent 基础设施公司 Runta 发起。在当前的榜单快照中，Alma 的任务通过率为 72.7%，仅次于 Codex CLI 的 77.9% 和 Pi 的 72.8%。Claude Code 则为 70.0%。

Alma 不仅通过率更高，完成任务也更省钱。它每成功完成一道题平均花费约 0.80 美元，Claude Code 为 0.94 美元，成本低约 16%。

这次 FrontierHarness v1.1 专门研究一个问题：同样的大模型，换一套 Agent 执行框架，表现究竟能差多少？

评测覆盖 21 组 Harness 配置、5 款大模型和 62 项任务，每项重复 4 次，计划运行 26,040 次，规模达到上一版的 72 倍。所有工具都在统一的云端环境中运行，比较任务成功率、Token 成本和执行速度。

Alma 是一款主打本地运行、长期记忆的 AI Agent，能直接读取和修改代码、执行终端命令、搜索网页，还支持 Skills 和 MCP。它可以自由切换底层模型，不依赖某一家模型厂商。

最近，Alma 还整合了 Herdr。Claude Code、Codex、Pi 等编程 Agent 可以继续在 Herdr 中运行，Alma 则把它们集中到一个聊天界面，查看执行过程、回复问题和批准操作。用户可以通过 iPhone 远程管理电脑上的多个 Agent。

目前评测尚未结束，排名仍会变化。参测模型也仅限 GLM、DeepSeek、Kimi、Muse 这几款开源模型，没有覆盖 GPT 和 Claude 系列闭源模型。

According to Anthropic's latest prospectus, the firm plans to offer 825M Class A shares priced at $70–$78 each, implying a ~$1.2T–$1.4T valuation. Why ETH is the store of value for what's coming

We are almost certainly heading into a period of high inflation and extreme economic and social volatility. As inflation and risk erode the purchasing power of nation-state money and many other assets, it will matter more than ever to hold assets that keep or grow their value.

Gold and BTC are high-powered money and excellent stores of value. ETH goes further.

Not debt-based. Like gold and BTC, ETH is not debt-based or credit-based money.

Censorship resistant. Like BTC, or gold and silver held physically, ETH transactions on Ethereum L1 can't be censored. That's true for simple payments and for complex smart contract programs like DeFi, and those programs are guaranteed to execute.

Cheap to hold. Like BTC, ETH is relatively cheap to hold and store securely.

Cheap to use at any scale. Ethereum is cheap and easy to use whether a transaction moves $1 or billions. Any well-formed transaction is guaranteed to execute.

Sound, and getting sounder. ETH is disinflationary and becomes ultrasound, meaning deflationary, during periods of high network activity.

Broadly useful. ETH has many uses across the Ethereum economy, and that economy will grow by orders of magnitude as finance, and eventually every industry, moves onchain. Global adoption of the Web protocols in the '90s and '00s transformed the world economy. Ethereum is the foundation of Web3, the user-centric, decentralized web.

Collateral money. ETH works as collateral, and collateral that grows in value over time is a powerful thing.

Home of stablecoins. Ethereum hosts the bulk of stablecoin activity. Stablecoins serve as payment money and as unit-of-account money.

Despot-proof. Like BTC, ETH can't be used by a despot to financially exploit or repress citizens. Over time that should have positive geopolitical effects.

Programmable. ETH is programmable money. You can attach arbitrary logic to transactions and build an entire economy on smart-contract-based agreements and business processes (see https://t.co/JcWtBUclr2).

Transparent or private, and auditable either way. Money and financial instruments on Ethereum can be public or private, and in both cases selectively disclosable and auditable. Privacy tools for retail and institutional users include VPNs, mix networks, shielded and privacy pools, Railgun, stealth addresses, Kohaku, and zero-knowledge proofs in many forms, including on L2s and on private permissioned EVM networks linked through bridgeless synchronous composability.

Future-proof. By the end of 2027, or partway through 2028 at the latest, ETH will be quantum-safe and AI-safe money.

ETH is the base money of an exponentially growing ecosystem that should keep growing for decades. Its monetary premium will keep rising, because retail, corporate, and government users will all need to hold some. Part of today's premium is speculative: Ethereum dominates smart contract blockchains, but it hasn't fully hit its stride or gone mainstream yet.

Machine intelligence will supercharge every scientific and technological pursuit and grow global GDP bigger and faster than any of us can imagine. Ethereum L1 and modular Ethereum L2s will undergird most of the high-value agreements, transactions, payment flows, and complex business processes behind the coming hybrid human-machine decentralized economy.

Goals

• Follow a goal live: every round, every team, and what each agent last said.
• Research goals can return a dataset with exact totals, pinned to IPFS, and the write-up's figures must match it.
• Agents re-read every source they cite before they hand in, and flag any that don't hold up.
• Each research batch starts with five items and pauses if the brief isn't working.

Desktop App for Mac/Windows
• New: every agent you hold, in your Mac menu bar or Windows tray, at https://t.co/9QX9KrfZDJ.
• Setup runs your agent in a secure box that can't see your files, and starts it the moment its seat is approved.
• Lend a seat from the app, and seats lent on imdLend stay in your list.
• The app tells you when an agent hits its Claude or Codex limit, and when it's back.

Workers
• New imd rpc setup: one Alchemy key gives your worker its own RPC on Ethereum, Base and Robinhood Chain.
• New imd venice key: run Venice models for the jobs that ask for them.
• imd doctor checks each runtime's sandbox and tells you why the network paused your machine.
• In Telegram, /agent 410 tells you how agent 410 is doing, and a bug report becomes an issue with a draft fix.
• If https://t.co/fRnb1K501K's domain goes down, agents reach the network by a backup address, and delivered files stay up on https://t.co/kTqmWJpy2Z.

Explorer
• Simplified nav: Swarm, Tokens and Sites, then Create, Docs and your wallet.
• Each token gets a launchpad-style page that trades in ETH and shows only the tax its hook really takes.
• Pause or resume your agent from its page with one signature, no gas.
• Rewards adds a Sellable view that claims only what's worth $1 or more.
• Connect the same way on every page: any browser wallet, Rabby, Coinbase Smart Wallet, or your wallet's own browser on a phone.
• The front page renders in a fifth of the CPU time, and a 2,500-item goal loads 0.5 MB instead of 16.3 MB.

IMD Website 
• https://t.co/tTmryBD4TG is one file your agent follows to hire IMD or run a worker, and it installs in Hermes.
• New docs: Hire Swarm, Join Swarm and Get $IMD on one page, under a flock that flies into the IMD mark.
• The home page terminal shows the running goal and what each seat last said.
• The seats market reads the whole OpenSea book, with the week's sales in one live line.

Oracle
• Ask 2 to 8 questions in one order, read at the same block, for 0.5 IMD each.
• A new recipe prices an NFT collection from its Seaport and Blur sales.
• Contracts can pin the exact question they ask, and take only its answer.
• Panels take turns across the whole fleet, and a request for one quick answer goes to the fastest third.

Launches and Sites
• Launch fees on Ethereum and Robinhood Chain now feed the burn: IMD is burned, ETH buys IMD to burn.
• A company with no token can launch as contracts only, now on Base too.
• New sites get their own address on https://t.co/RnlbYJYrYt, or go on your own domain through ENS or DNSLink.
• Contracts can buy jobs, launches and workflows through the Intake, and read the files of a job they bought.

Privacy and Security
• Tasks run in a sandbox on Mac and Linux: they write only in their own folder and can't read your files, keys or settings.
• A brief that tries to read the agent's machine, reach a private address or dump raw command output is refused before anyone pays.

This update also includes:
• Fixes nine ways a job could fail or get stuck.
• Fixes an issue where a cancelled job could still open a launch or take a site's name.
• Fixes an issue where a goal item could hang for hours on a cited page.

author: jevgenijs
quoted_text:
I am still looking for more AI infra supply side that wants to get paid by agents.

Last week we integrated @BoundlessHQ for unstoppable inference & @e2b for unstoppable sandboxes.

We are missing other critical infra such as model routers or cloud platforms like Cloudflare and Vercel. Of course the dream would be to get an EC2 box or an EKS cluster with a single API call from your agent.

The missing component that we hear from larger providers many time is identity, so it's a good thing we just added identity support to the Machine Payments Protocol.

Normally your agent would call a paid API, get a 402 back, and then need to re-submit its call with a signed payment in the header.

For identity, we simply introduce an additional roundtrip, where the API can say "I also need you to prove ownership of this email", or "I need to find your wallet in my database first", or "I need to check this 3p API whether you're a good or bad person".

We are looking for early "heavy hitter" partners who want to unlock getting paid with agents for their most critical products.

Please DM me if you want early access and want to collaborate on shaping not just payments but also identity for agents.

author: 0xdizai
quoted_text:
你根本不知道，做 KOL/KOC 有多难。

聊这个话题，我大概率算是整个中文币圈里，少数几个走出不同路径的人。

先说结论：做 KOL/KOC，人脉真的太重要了。

如果有 10 个人愿意稳定给你介绍合作，基本上你就能在币圈活下去。

当然，最舒服的还是傍上交易所包月，毕竟这玩意儿才是稳定现金流。做的好的群友，基本都吃上了。

如果你没吃上，那就只能靠自己的「舔功」上位了。

我个人的路径几乎没法复制。机缘巧合之下拉了个全真社区，又机缘巧合火了一段时间，才让我没有饿死。

但绝大多数 KOL/KOC，尤其是账号质量一般、又没什么资源的新人，走的完全是另一条路。

那就是不停地舔，拼命往圈子里挤。

你可能需要加入十几个 KOL 社区，天天在里面混脸熟，先从陌生人混成普通朋友，再从普通朋友混成好朋友，最后才有可能换来一点合作机会。

这个过程非常累，甚至可以说非常痛苦。

因为作为一个新人，你在别人眼里几乎是零价值的。

没人认识你，没人认可你，更没人有义务带你赚钱。

你只能不断展示自己的价值，就像一个拼命追着镜头跑的十八线小明星，生怕错过任何一次露脸的机会。

即便如此，成功率依然低得可怜。

你可能尝试了 100 次，只有 1 次有效。更绝望的是，剩下 99 次失败之后，面对同一批人，把同样的事情再做一遍。

再聊聊更现实的：送礼。

之前就听说，很多 KOL 为了拿合作，是需要给 BD 送礼的。

我自己暂时没送过，但几个好基友一直劝我送。

因为确实有几个 BD 对我特别好，基本属于把饭喂到嘴边了。说实话，这礼我确实该送，只是一直没送而已。

而且送礼也是一门学问，送什么、什么时候送、怎么送，都有讲究。

我个人的理解是，很多时候最难的不是花钱，而是让人家愿意收。

如果对方愿意接受你一份价值不低的礼物，至少说明你们的关系已经到了某个程度。

你送出去一万块，未来人家可能通过合作给你带来远超一万块的价值。

但你以为送礼就已经够离谱了？

不好意思，这可能还只是最低档。

我听过的其他案例，包括但不限于：

通宵陪打游戏。
甚至陪睡觉的传闻。

陪打游戏我还能理解，毕竟就是牺牲点时间。

但陪睡觉，我特么是真的觉得离谱。

当然，若是大哥想让你陪睡觉，到也是一个机会，睡对了大哥，就算你是个职校生，睡上一次，B也涨价了。这也是捞女为什么被骂。因为他们确实找到了捷径。

不过话又说回来，为什么有些人总喜欢走捷径？

因为在一个高度依赖资源、人脉和利益交换的行业里，有时候你辛辛苦苦努力一年，可能真不如别人认识一个大哥。

这也是为什么，有些人明明没什么专业能力，却能拿到远超普通人的资源。

你可以不认可这种方式，但很难否认资源关系带来的巨大差距。

所以我现在越来越觉得，普通男 KOL 想在币圈混出头，是真的难。

如果你本身就有钱、有资源、有背景，那当然舒服。

但如果你什么都没有，只是一个普通人，想靠写内容、做研究、慢慢积累粉丝，然后靠这个养活自己……

说实话，真的得做好吃屎的准备。

这个行业表面上拼的是内容，实际上拼的是资源、人脉、情商，还有你能承受多少次被拒绝。

而最残酷的地方在于：

你以为自己是在和别人的内容竞争，实际上你可能连礼都送不出去。

text:
The US selloff is a TECH crash, not a market crash.

From its Oct 6 record high to its Nov 5 close, the S&P 500 fell -5.9%.

But remove tech stocks and the Mag 7, and the S&P 500 would actually be UP +6%.

Tech and the Mag 7 are just ~78 of the S&P 500’s 503 stocks.

Yet they make up ~53% of the index, and they are down -16% over the same period.

That means tech and the Mag 7 alone subtracted ~9 percentage points from the index.

In other words, they accounted for MORE than 100% of the S&P 500’s decline.

In October, 9 of the 11 S&P 500 sectors rose:

- Energy: +13.8%
- Consumer Staples: +10.9%
- Utilities: +10.1%
- Health Care: +9.7%
- Materials: +8.2%
- Consumer Discretionary: +6.0%
- Financials: +5.8%
- Real Estate: +5.5%
- Industrials: +0.2%
- Technology: -8.2%
- Communication Services: -9.9%

The only 2 sectors that fell are home to the AI trade.

Truly a tale of two markets.

反思！沃什时代的美联储，新政策框架让市场反而更加敏感！

沃什希望的是减少政策上过多的前瞻性指引，让政策回归锚定数据，这本身短期让宏观数据的权重更高，

但是部分理事，依旧延用此前Fed管用的预期管理方式，大胆且明确的表达自己对通胀、对经济、对利率的观点，但是因为与沃什主张政策有冲突，让讲话对市场的刺激也变得更加敏感！

从昨天沃勒讲话之后，陆续洛根、施密德、鲍曼与保尔森多位理事对经济与利率发表讲话，引发市场对未来Fed加息政策的定价与预期调整

截止目前，12月加息25BP概率88.6%，加息50BP概率11.4%，2027年1月加息概率进入61.1%，已经开始初步定价

也就是说，这连续的鹰派观点讲话，不仅锁定了12月加息的概率，更是让市场开始预期12月加息50BP或者1月连续加息，对风险市场更不利的是恐怕会有加息周期回归的预期出现！

未来真的要出现连续性加息吗？

这里要考虑到Fed政策的“反身性”，按照这个逻辑来看，当数据、Fed理事预期引导等多重因素下让市场开始为12月后续的持续加息做定价的时候，反而会反向削弱未来加息的可能性

以目前为例，12月加息被锁定后加息预期外溢至50BP或者1月连续加息，而金融市场提前交易预期进行估值回调，但是随着金融条件足够收紧，12月加息之后其实后续继续加息的可能性大大减少！

同时，如果期间Brent价格可以回归90美元下方，其实对12月加息甚至未来更多的加息都是有一定的削弱性的！

以此为核心逻辑，这也是我为何本周多次提出，从本周开始到12月9日议息会议前，市场一旦继续回调，就是给了抄底买入的机会！ @MSX_CN

The past two weeks in tokenized stocks (Oct 26–Nov 8):

• Issuance up 19% to $3.79B
• DEX volume: $3.14B, down 26.1%
• $504M in net new issuance
• Holder positions up 17k to 457.9k

The trend continues: the market grows fast, but the trading volume is declining.

@Binance’s bStocks still lead the issuance, growing from $1.07B to $1.42B (+33%) over the past 2 weeks. @RobinhoodCrypto now leads trading: $1.51B of DEX volume over the two weeks (48%) vs $1.01B for bStocks, whose weekly volume fell for a third week in a row.

The biggest additions to supply were all bStocks tokens: Alphabet (+$84M), SpaceX (+$69M), Intel (+$38M), SanDisk (+$35M) and QQQ (+$33M).

TSV settled the first trades under the SEC’s tokenized-stock exemption

DRW Cumberland bought issuer-sponsored tokenized Canton Strategic Holdings (CNTN) shares from Five North on @CantonNetwork. No trade size was disclosed.

Full story: https://t.co/gUFZqCIMOx

That’s a wrap for this edition of the Tokenized Stocks Digest, covering the data and biggest stories from the past two weeks.

text:
英伟达全球 18% 的营收来自新加坡客户，但真正运到新加坡的产品，只对应全球营收的 2%。

《金融时报》今天的一篇调查，揭开了新加坡如何成为中国 AI 芯片贸易的关键中转枢纽。

一个典型案例是 Megaspeed。这家新加坡公司是英伟达认证的云服务合作伙伴，资产负债表规模在一年间从 3300 万美元暴涨至 30 亿美元，阿里巴巴是其最大客户。如今，美、新两国正在调查它是否涉及违规转移受限芯片，公司则否认存在违法行为。

更值得注意的是，新加坡的角色不只是物流中转站。采购合同可以签在新加坡，服务器可以部署在第三国，最终算力却可能由中国企业使用。

这也是美国芯片出口管制越来越棘手的地方：过去要追踪一块芯片去了哪里，现在还得弄清楚谁买了它、谁控制它，以及谁最终在使用它。

芯片有国界，算力服务却可以跨境。美国试图封锁的是供应链的终点，但全球 AI 产业正在把这个终点变得越来越模糊。

Why ETH is the store of value for what's coming

We are almost certainly heading into a period of high inflation and extreme economic and social volatility. As inflation and risk erode the purchasing power of nation-state money and many other assets, it will matter more than ever to hold assets that keep or grow their value.

Gold and BTC are high-powered money and excellent stores of value. ETH goes further.

Not debt-based. Like gold and BTC, ETH is not debt-based or credit-based money.

Censorship resistant. Like BTC, or gold and silver held physically, ETH transactions on Ethereum L1 can't be censored. That's true for simple payments and for complex smart contract programs like DeFi, and those programs are guaranteed to execute.

Cheap to hold. Like BTC, ETH is relatively cheap to hold and store securely.

Cheap to use at any scale. Ethereum is cheap and easy to use whether a transaction moves $1 or billions. Any well-formed transaction is guaranteed to execute.

Sound, and getting sounder. ETH is disinflationary and becomes ultrasound, meaning deflationary, during periods of high network activity.

Broadly useful. ETH has many uses across the Ethereum economy, and that economy will grow by orders of magnitude as finance, and eventually every industry, moves onchain. Global adoption of the Web protocols in the '90s and '00s transformed the world economy. Ethereum is the foundation of Web3, the user-centric, decentralized web.

Collateral money. ETH works as collateral, and collateral that grows in value over time is a powerful thing.

Home of stablecoins. Ethereum hosts the bulk of stablecoin activity. Stablecoins serve as payment money and as unit-of-account money.

Despot-proof. Like BTC, ETH can't be used by a despot to financially exploit or repress citizens. Over time that should have positive geopolitical effects.

Programmable. ETH is programmable money. You can attach arbitrary logic to transactions and build an entire economy on smart-contract-based agreements and business processes (see https://t.co/JcWtBUclr2).

Transparent or private, and auditable either way. Money and financial instruments on Ethereum can be public or private, and in both cases selectively disclosable and auditable. Privacy tools for retail and institutional users include VPNs, mix networks, shielded and privacy pools, Railgun, stealth addresses, Kohaku, and zero-knowledge proofs in many forms, including on L2s and on private permissioned EVM networks linked through bridgeless synchronous composability.

Future-proof. By the end of 2027, or partway through 2028 at the latest, ETH will be quantum-safe and AI-safe money.

ETH is the base money of an exponentially growing ecosystem that should keep growing for decades. Its monetary premium will keep rising, because retail, corporate, and government users will all need to hold some. Part of today's premium is speculative: Ethereum dominates smart contract blockchains, but it hasn't fully hit its stride or gone mainstream yet.

Machine intelligence will supercharge every scientific and technological pursuit and grow global GDP bigger and faster than any of us can imagine. Ethereum L1 and modular Ethereum L2s will undergird most of the high-value agreements, transactions, payment flows, and complex business processes behind the coming hybrid human-machine decentralized economy.
author: eldarcap
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

一枚芯片绕过禁令，叫监管漏洞。24 万枚芯片都能绕过去，恐怕就不能只用「漏洞」来解释了。

The Information 独家调查披露，前 Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang 被指协助将约 24 万枚受美国出口限制的英伟达芯片运入中国，主要是 H100 和 H200。

其中一部分经过上海世纪立通，最终进入为阿里巴巴、腾讯提供算力的数据中心。

更微妙的是，世纪立通与 Huang 的家族存在关联，同时还是英伟达认证的「优选云合作伙伴」，能够通过官方合作渠道获取芯片。世纪立通否认与 Huang 存在业务往来，并强调自身经营合法合规。

美国试图通过出口管制切断中国获取先进算力的渠道，却可能无意中抬高了「渠道」本身的商业价值。

芯片还是那些芯片，需求也没有消失。变化的是交易路径，从直接采购，变成跨境公司、分销商、云服务商之间的层层流转。

禁令越严，合法供应越受限制，掌握复杂采购网络和跨境资源的人就可能获得越高的议价权。

华盛顿想让芯片变得难以获得，却可能让一群懂得怎么获得芯片的中间人，变得越来越值钱。

这或许才是出口管制最吊诡的地方，它试图消灭一条供应链，却可能刺激另一条供应链生长。

text:
On Nov 2, SEC staff updated the FAQ for the Application of the Federal Securities Laws to Certain Types of Crypto Assets. They say “a crypto system is ‘decentralized’ if it functions and operates autonomously with no person, entity, or group of persons or entities having operational, economic, or voting control of the crypto system.”

The staff looks for anyone who can act alone, outside the network's governance: to limit access, change how upgrades get voted on, pick who runs nodes, change the code or reverse transactions.

Here's how THORChain works on each point.

Operational - Funds sit in vaults run by groups of nodes, and every transaction needs a supermajority of nodes to authorize it. No single node can move funds or undo a swap. If the protocol detects an insolvency, it will automatically halt a whole chain, to protect the network. It can't target a single user. Operational mimirs exist to protect the network from attack or failure. These require a minimum of 3 node votes, but 4 nodes can then vote to reverse, 5 can counter the 4, and so on.

Economic - Fees are automatically charged on all swaps and automatically distributed on the network to the various stakeholders. Changes to fees, tokenomics, etc. are called economic mimirs and need 2/3 of active nodes.

Voting - Anyone can run a node if they bond enough RUNE to be churned into the network. No person picks the nodes. Parameters change only through on-chain node votes. Same with a protocol upgrade. No team or company can change a parameter on its own. Every node vote is recorded on-chain, and anyone can check it.

美国把中国大学拉进出口黑名单，却没能拦住英伟达最先进的 AI 芯片流入校园。

路透社独家报道，根据最新采购记录，一所与解放军关系密切、早已被美国列入出口管制实体清单的中国大学，上个月仍成功采购了英伟达 H200 AI 芯片。

这件事的关键不只是中国大学买到了什么，而是美国已经明确禁止向特定机构出口先进技术，却依然没能完全切断它们获取算力的渠道。

出口管制可以限制英伟达卖给谁，却很难保证芯片在经过经销商、第三方采购和跨境流通之后，最终落到谁手里。

这也是华盛顿越来越难解决的矛盾：芯片是可以追踪的商品，但算力正在成为一种难以封锁的全球性资源。

美国可以不断扩大黑名单，但只要全球芯片流通网络仍然存在，纸面上的禁令与现实中的供应链之间，就始终可能存在缝隙。

author: hmalviya9
quoted_text:
what if we had memecoins with an expiry date?

so many of these coins die within a few minutes anyways.

can we actually put that deadline into the contract?

ethereum already has a token standard for this.

it's called ERC-7818. 

it allows devs to create tokens with a defined validity period. once that period ends, those tokens become unusable and cannot be transferred.

imagine launching 1M tokens with a lifespan of 7 days.

people buy them, trade them, build memes around them.

but everyone knows when the party ends.

buying on day 6 doesn't give you another 7 days. you're buying the remaining time.

that's where the psychology gets interesting.

every buyer has to think about two things: how much attention this meme can attract, and how much time it has left.

i'm surprised this isn't a bigger conversation on CT.

even more surprised that devs aren't exploring a narrative around it.

a weekend memecoin. a seven-day meme competition. a token built around a live event.

you could build seasons where tokens expire, while the memes, collectibles and community history survive. those mechanics would need additional development.

but there is a catch.

expiry doesn't refund anyone. and if the token has no use or final payout, everyone is trying to find another buyer before the same deadline.

tokens can also expire inside liquidity pools, so devs need to design how trading ends and what happens to the remaining liquidity.

the countdown alone isn't enough. what people can do before it reaches zero is where the actual design begins.

memecoins which are gonna die anyways.

at least with these, the funeral date is public.

EthenaのPT限定のPendle Market、Pendleを資金調達マーケットに変えたってことでこれは凄いな。

YTの買い手が居ないと本来PTの利回りが出ないが、YTをEthenaチーム自体が買う。

✅️ 構造の解釈
◉リテールにPTを買ってもらう
→ リテールがPTを買う際、まずは原資産の購入が必要(個人投資家はUSDeのプライマリに参加できない)
→ 実質的に資金調達に該当該当

◉Ethena LabsがYTを買う
→ PT利回りが上がり(PT価格が下落)、固定金利での投資家が参入
→ 実質的に"利払い"をする行為に該当

YTを購入することで、実質利払いをし、資金調達につなげる。

✅️ Pendleを使う意味
● プラットフォームとしての強さ：固定金利のStablecoinとして出すならPendleを使う必要は無いが、PendleにはマジでPTクジラが沢山いるから集客力は担保できる。
● セキュリティの高さ：システム的にYTの購入にEthena Labs以外からアクセス出来ないようにPermissionをつけるだけなので、セキュリティはPendleそのまま。

実はPendleを使ったマーケティングとして、これまでもチームがYTを爆買いすることで、PT利回りを上げて原資産発行量を増やすのはよく行われていた。それを表立ってやり始めたということ。

更にMorphoのマーケットを使ってPTループをさせることで、恐らく投資家は最大12倍レバレッジをかけることができる。
Ethena Labs的には、$10kの投資家に$120k分投資させることにつながる。YTの利払いをし、MorphoのCutated Vaultsの投資家にリスクを押し付けることで。

DeFiの深い流動性をTradFiの資金調達に使うのはめっちゃ流行ってるなと思うがその1つの事例

text:
If a token can’t generate +EV for its protocol, it’s useless.

That’s why $OXO is built to turn token trading fees into more capital people can borrow on @paboxoxyz.

Paboxo lets users borrow USDG against supported tokenized stocks and Uniswap liquidity positions. OXO aims to help fund those loans.

The planned setup for launch works like this:

• The Paboxo team supplies 80% of the launch funding, with eligible public backers supplying 20%.

• After launch costs, the funds buy OXO inventory and support three AI trading agents. Their capital stays committed to trading. The team and backers can't withdraw it after launch aka perma-locked

• Paboxo splits the OXO-related fees it actually receives: 50% for lending liquidity and 50% for treasury and operations. Other recipients keep their own fee shares.

• Paboxo converts the lending portion into $USDG if needed and deposits it into its Earn vault, adding money available for eligible loans.

For example, $10,000 in fees received by Paboxo means $5,000 toward lending and $5,000 toward operations, before conversion and execution costs.

The difference is where the money goes.

Some DeFi models use product revenue to buy back tokens. OXO plans to use income from token trading to help fund the lending product and scale further.

Protocol-owned liquidity already exists elsewhere. OXO's particular approach connects committed trading capital with fee income that can build lending reserves.

With sustained trading activity and fees reaching the vault, that lending base can grow over time. Repaid loans make the capital available again, while the operating share can support new markets and integrations.

That gives OXO a clear role in Paboxo’s expansion and differ greatly from others DeFi token, helping more people access liquidity from their tokenized assets as the product grows.

The numbers: media-verified AI incidents jumped from ~2,700 (2024) to over 4,600 (just Jan–Aug 2026). Its roadmap: interoperability for safety tests, third-party verification of developer claims, confidential incident hotlines, strict agent permissioning, and open-source toolkits for regulators everywhere.

author: BlockBeatsAsia
quoted_text:
ZEC 单日暴跌近 20%，Hyperliquid 84.4% 的百万美元级多头地址陷入浮亏，巨鲸合计被套约 2374 万美元。

Hyperliquid 上 zcash:native 从昨夜高点 1,199.20 美元一路跌至今日午后低点 965.79 美元，区间跌幅约 19.5%，截至发稿暂报 987 美元，24 小时跌幅约 14.7%。

据统计，全市场 32 个持仓价值超过 100 万美元的 ZEC 多头地址中，已有 27 个陷入浮亏，占比 84.4%，合计浮亏约 2,374 万美元。

这 27 个地址合计持有约 12.26 万枚 ZEC，价值约 1.21 亿美元，占上述巨鲸多仓的 90.2%，相当于 Hyperliquid ZEC 永续合约总未平仓量的 29.5%。32 个地址的加权建仓均价为 1,127.26 美元，较当前价格高出约 12.5%。

其中，地址 0xc36a 浮亏最严重，持有约 1.35 万枚 ZEC 多仓，建仓均价 1,229.96 美元，目前浮亏约 327 万美元，清算价为 894.23 美元。

此外，地址 0x8f74 今晨被强平全部 567 枚 ZEC 多仓，亏损约 11.25 万美元；地址 0xb200 过去 24 小时内更是连续三次被强平，累计涉及 324 枚 ZEC。

最近，我收到了几份涉及我的材料，已经整理提交给法务部门。里面有人在索取、传递我的个人隐私信息，也有人对我的生活作出带有侮辱性的猜测，讨论怎样找到可以用来攻击我的材料，但是她自己也说了没有找到，因为我根本没有做过那样的事情。

说不害怕是假的，这几天我状态非常差，靠一口气吊着，比起那些难听的话和造谣，我更担心自己会不会影响到家人。

我知道，不可能让所有人都喜欢自己。不喜欢我也没关系，划走我的主页就好了。我没有想到，这份不喜欢，还会延伸到我的生活里。

text:
Why ETH is the store of value for what's coming

We are almost certainly heading into a period of high inflation and extreme economic and social volatility. As inflation and risk erode the purchasing power of nation-state money and many other assets, it will matter more than ever to hold assets that keep or grow their value.

Gold and BTC are high-powered money and excellent stores of value. ETH goes further.

Not debt-based. Like gold and BTC, ETH is not debt-based or credit-based money.

Censorship resistant. Like BTC, or gold and silver held physically, ETH transactions on Ethereum L1 can't be censored. That's true for simple payments and for complex smart contract programs like DeFi, and those programs are guaranteed to execute.

Cheap to hold. Like BTC, ETH is relatively cheap to hold and store securely.

Cheap to use at any scale. Ethereum is cheap and easy to use whether a transaction moves $1 or billions. Any well-formed transaction is guaranteed to execute.

Sound, and getting sounder. ETH is disinflationary and becomes ultrasound, meaning deflationary, during periods of high network activity.

Broadly useful. ETH has many uses across the Ethereum economy, and that economy will grow by orders of magnitude as finance, and eventually every industry, moves onchain. Global adoption of the Web protocols in the '90s and '00s transformed the world economy. Ethereum is the foundation of Web3, the user-centric, decentralized web.

Collateral money. ETH works as collateral, and collateral that grows in value over time is a powerful thing.

Home of stablecoins. Ethereum hosts the bulk of stablecoin activity. Stablecoins serve as payment money and as unit-of-account money.

Despot-proof. Like BTC, ETH can't be used by a despot to financially exploit or repress citizens. Over time that should have positive geopolitical effects.

Programmable. ETH is programmable money. You can attach arbitrary logic to transactions and build an entire economy on smart-contract-based agreements and business processes (see https://t.co/JcWtBUclr2).

Transparent or private, and auditable either way. Money and financial instruments on Ethereum can be public or private, and in both cases selectively disclosable and auditable. Privacy tools for retail and institutional users include VPNs, mix networks, shielded and privacy pools, Railgun, stealth addresses, Kohaku, and zero-knowledge proofs in many forms, including on L2s and on private permissioned EVM networks linked through bridgeless synchronous composability.

Future-proof. By the end of 2027, or partway through 2028 at the latest, ETH will be quantum-safe and AI-safe money.

ETH is the base money of an exponentially growing ecosystem that should keep growing for decades. Its monetary premium will keep rising, because retail, corporate, and government users will all need to hold some. Part of today's premium is speculative: Ethereum dominates smart contract blockchains, but it hasn't fully hit its stride or gone mainstream yet.

Machine intelligence will supercharge every scientific and technological pursuit and grow global GDP bigger and faster than any of us can imagine. Ethereum L1 and modular Ethereum L2s will undergird most of the high-value agreements, transactions, payment flows, and complex business processes behind the coming hybrid human-machine decentralized economy.
author: binji_x
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
Can you pump a subnet’s alpha to mint more gamma? No.

Gamma is now live on Bittensor. It’s a dollar-valued credit you mint by burning a subnet’s alpha, and subnets can accept it as payment for their services.

So the obvious question: can you pump a subnet’s alpha price and mint more gamma? No, and the reason is a neat bit of design.

When you burn alpha, it’s valued at the LOWER of two prices:
- Spot: the pool price right now
- Gamma price: a slow-moving reference price each subnet tracks

The gamma price drops to spot instantly. When spot rises, it only closes half the gap every 600 blocks (~2 hours), and it can at most double in that time. Falls count right away. Rises have to last before they count.

Both prices are read before your mint’s own trade, so pumping in the same block, or over a few blocks, gets you nothing extra.

TAO/USD is guarded the same way. It drops at once but rises by at most ~2% an hour, and if the oracle’s price is over an hour old, minting stops.

The formula:
gamma = alpha burned × min(spot, gamma price) × 

TAO/USDPrices that fall fast and rise slowly mean only lasting demand turns into gamma.

Full breakdown 👇
https://t.co/4aQDaQ2b7j

However, the devil was that it was sneakily enabled by default in the Ledger SDK since their ledgerhq/context-module v1.16... So right after the lib update - every transaction you sign with a Ledger device started sending to https://t.co/wtXKaYbqGf the network, the contract or recipient address, device model and firmware, app versions and whether you signed blind.

I'd argue that privacy should be the default, @Ledger 💪

Happy to see more and more people becoming aware of the privacy implications and picking Ambire for our ongoing privacy focus.

Catching things like this 👀 is part of the job for us!

text:
Ledger doesn't store the transaction data sent for this Clear Signing lookup. By default, the signing SDK sends Ledger's servers the transaction details needed to find the right descriptor, so you can read what you're approving on your signer's Secure Screen. Integrators can also handle that lookup themselves.

Donjon's explanation: https://t.co/2nNvve8Xgg
author: Ledger
quoted_text:
This is part of how Clear Signing works. ERC-7730 descriptors, which turn raw calldata into readable fields, are too large to fit on a Ledger signer, and most integrators don’t want to bundle the full metadata set. 

So the default context module in our signing kit resolves them from Ledger’s servers at signing time. That requires sending the transaction details needed to find the right descriptor. Ledger doesn’t store that data.

It runs in the developer library that wallet apps use to talk to a Ledger signer, not in device firmware.
Integrators control it and can supply their own context module to resolve metadata themselves: https://t.co/VaR4ehwAhk

How the context module works: https://t.co/NCJYcilFcr
The descriptor registry is public: https://t.co/P1lUdMW92l

text:
What stood out to me was the experiment design and validation (using independent datasets and methods) that Claude did.

The different ways the result was checked (in Claude’s own words):

- Calibrating first. Before looking at mitochondria at all, it confirmed that protein melting temperature tracks living temperature across 13 species. It also confirmed this within the same protein families (human vs worm, fly, fish, yeast).

- Testing that melting temperature is built into the protein itself. Proteins from a heat-loving bacterium, produced inside E. coli, kept their high melting points. So it’s written into the protein, not lent by its surroundings.

- Replicating across labs and species. It used 25 separate conditions from 4 independent labs and 6 species. No single condition came anywhere near the predicted effect, including fly cells, one of the cell lines where hot mitochondria was claimed.

- Separating built-in stability from surroundings. It analysed broken-open cells (built-in stability) apart from intact cells (stability helped by the surroundings). Both came out far below the prediction.

- Matched “sister” proteins. It compared 47 pairs from the same family, one copy working in mitochondria and one outside, after checking where each actually lives. There was no difference.

- An independent method: reading heat tolerance from sequence. An AI model, trained only on bacteria, predicts heat tolerance from a protein’s sequence. It was first checked against a known answer: human proteins should read “hotter” than worm, fly, fish and yeast proteins, and they did. Then, in all 5 species tested, mitochondrial proteins read slightly cooler, not hotter.

- Proteins nearest the supposed heat source. If heat were confined to the inner membrane (where the heat is made), those proteins should show the strongest adaptation. They didn’t.

- Robustness checks.
Two different definitions of “mitochondrial protein” gave the same answer.
Correcting for protein length changed nothing.
Including proteins that never melted didn’t change the conclusion.
Uncertainty was propagated properly, accounting for shared proteins and for doubt about the calibration itself. The chance that the calibration is weak enough to hide a 10 °C effect came out at 1.5% or less.

- An adversarial review by a second AI (OpenAI Codex). It found real bugs and weak spots: ID mix-ups, mis-paired proteins, merged replicates and overconfident error bars. Each one was fixed or stated as a limitation, and the headline claim was narrowed as a result.

- A prior-work search. It searched the literature to confirm the test was new. The closest earlier work, from the theory’s own proponents, had seen a roughly 2 °C difference and read it as support. This analysis showed that 2 °C is 5–10 times too small.

- Writing down what would prove it wrong. It designed a decisive experiment (heat cells with the mitochondria switched on vs off) and recorded the predictions in advance.

text:
Privacy and verification are two completely different problems.

And I think this is one of the more underrated parts of @termix_ai AACP architecture.

Most people hear TEE and ZK and assume they're solving the same thing.

Not exactly.

❯ TEE (Trusted Execution Environment)

Runs computations inside a hardware-isolated environment, helping protect sensitive data and execution from the surrounding system.

Think private inputs, API keys and confidential workloads.

❯ ZK (Zero-Knowledge Proofs)

Allows a verifier to check a cryptographic proof that a specific computation was executed correctly, without having to rerun the entire computation.

Think verifiable execution rather than simply trusting someone's claim.

Here's where AACP gets interesting.

Its whitepaper outlines four verification levels:

L0 → Manual verification
L1 → TEE-based verification
L2 → zkVM-based verification
L3 → TEE + zkVM

The combination is what caught my attention.
TEE can help protect the environment where work happens, while zkVM proofs can provide cryptographic evidence about the execution.

Two different approaches addressing different trust assumptions.

Of course, neither magically guarantees that every AI-generated answer is correct.

But building different verification options into the protocol makes a lot more sense than treating every task the same way.

Privacy protects the process.

Proofs help verify the execution.

That's the distinction worth understanding.

Dems won big in the midterms and even Vance blames the Iran war for the loss, so Hegseth is the obvious fall guy. Massie (R) will force an impeachment vote in the House next week, and odds jumped from ~30% to ~50%.

My take:
• Trump today: “I have every intention to keep him.” Voluntary resignation <5%.
• Leadership will likely move to table it, i.e. kill it before it’s even debated. GOP still controls the lame-duck House, but only ~4 defections or no-shows sink the tabling motion. Many Republicans just lost their seats and owe Trump nothing, so impeachment passing is a real risk (~30%).
• Even if impeached, removal needs 67 senators. Not happening.

I’m on No for Dec 31.

text:
Our direct experience with Nvidia, never shared before:

22 months ago, we published the below analysis raising concerns that Nvidia's AI chips were potentially being routed to China through Singapore.

Less than 24 hours later, Nvidia's Head of PR contacted us, directly addressing our analysis. Their message to us is included below.

At the time, in the previous 3 quarters, $17.4 billion of Nvidia's revenue came from Singapore versus $11.6 billion from China.

Furthermore, at the time, the US had ~5,375 data centers, China had 448, and Singapore had just 99. The numbers just did not add up. You can read our full analysis below.

Nvidia's PR team sent us the following message:

"The revenue associated with Singapore does not indicate diversion to China. Our public filings report 'bill to' not 'ship to' locations of our customers. Many of our customers have business entities in Singapore and use those entities for products destined for the US and the West. We insist that our partners comply with all applicable laws, and if we receive any information to the contrary, act accordingly. Our last 10-Q noted: 'most shipments associated with Singapore revenue were to locations other than Singapore and shipments to Singapore were insignificant.'"

Fast forward to today.

According to new reports, Nvidia, $NVDA, CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy helped facilitate at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to Chinese companies through a network spanning China and Singapore.

The reported shipments date back to 2023 and involved ~240,000 advanced Nvidia AI chips.

These allegations remain under investigation, and it is not yet established whether the shipments were connected to the revenue discrepancies we highlighted 22 months ago.

Nvidia maintains that it has no reason to believe US national security or company secrets were compromised.

But the overlap between these new allegations and the questions we raised in January 2025, along with Nvidia's response to us at the time, is noteworthy.

We stand by our view that Jensen Huang is likely to remain CEO of Nvidia and will continue to be an integral figure in the AI Revolution.

We expect more on this soon.

quoted_text:
WIDTH is introducing DeFi Shield, lightweight compliance tooling for DeFi protocols with an operating team, mainly in trading and lending. It puts wallet risk screening (KYT), alerts, case review and an audit trail into one workflow, so that when a regulator asks, the team has evidence of reasonable steps and a complete record behind them.

Most DeFi users connect through self-custody wallets, leaving no identity data on file for conventional onboarding due diligence, while a team with control or sufficient influence over a protocol still carries the compliance obligations. Regulatory inquiries tend to centre on two points: whether the team acted on high-risk addresses, and whether it can show a record.

DeFi Shield addresses both. It screens the wallets that interact with a protocol through continuous monitoring and an optional pre-transaction API check, returning a risk level, a score, the rules triggered and a recommended action. Every alert and disposition goes into an append-only log that cannot be altered, with exportable address-level, case-level and periodic reports. AI drafts alert assessments, recommendations, report narratives and, where needed, suspicious transaction report text for compliance staff to review, and decisions such as freezing assets, suspending service or reporting to regulators stay with the team.

The 90-second product brief below shows how screening, the audit trail and reporting work.

想认真问大家一个问题 👇

之前分享过，我们做的预测 Agent Rhizome 在打榜 FutureX 上拿过第 1、3、7 名。最近在考虑把它做成 DeepSeek Harness 或 Codex 的插件，想听听大家的真实想法。

用起来大概是这样。

你只需要问一句：

「DeepSeek V5 会在春节前发布吗？」

Rhizome 会先参考历史发布规律，建立一个初始概率，再去搜索官方动态、代码改动、媒体爆料、预测市场等信源。

每获得一条新证据，就更新一次概率。多个子分析师会独立评估，出现分歧再进行裁决。

最后给你一个类似这样的回答：

「45%。目前最大的不确定性是……如果 12 月出现灰度测试，概率可能升至 75%。」

但说实话，我还不确定预测是不是一个太小众的需求。

所以想直接问问大家：

1️⃣ 如果做成插件，你会安装吗？

2️⃣ 最近有没有什么事情，是你特别想知道「它到底会不会发生」的？

3️⃣ 你希望预测 Agent 提供什么功能？

过去两个月，我们一直在闷声干一件事：教 AI 预测未来。

今天可以摊牌了 🎉 

在 FutureX，一个专门考察"预测还没发生的事"的实时榜单上，我们的长程预测 agent 拿下：

🥇 第 1 名（基座 Kimi K3） @Kimi_Moonshot
🥉 第 3 名（基座 DeepSeek V4 Pro）@deepseek_ai
7️⃣ 第 7 名（基座 MiniMax M3）@MiniMax_AI

同一套框架，换三个模型当"大脑"，全部进前十。

感谢团队成员 @Bruce_Lee1207 一起努力的付出 。

先回答一个你们一定会问的问题：现在榜单满天飞，FutureX 凭什么值得认真对待？
1️⃣ 出品方是 ByteDance Seed 联合 Stanford、Princeton、复旦，学界业界联合出品，论文在 arXiv 公开；
2️⃣ 它可能是唯一一个"打榜"在逻辑上不成立的榜单：题目全是尚未发生的真实事件，agent 先交预测，官方等事件落地后按真实结果判分。答案在出题时根本不存在，所以没有题库可背，没有答案分布可过拟合，想提分只有一条路：真的更会预测；
3️⃣ 同台的是谁：OpenAI、Google、xAI 的 Deep Research 系 agent 都被系统评测过，https://t.co/Jsf4FPzkDp 登顶时还专门发了官方博客。

再说我们的 agent 在做什么。你可以把它想象成一个不知疲倦的分析师：

🔍 自己上网检索，多信源交叉验证
🧠 把证据沉淀成"信念"，有新信息就更新判断
🎲 最后给的不是一句"可能吧"，而是一个校准过的概率
⚖️ 多个子分析师意见相左时，还有裁决机制出面对齐
  ......

为什么执着于预测？因为预测未来是智能最诚实的试金石，它逼着模型把检索、推理、常识、对不确定性的拿捏全部亮出来，一点都藏不住。

这只是开始。方法细节，后续成绩和最后的产品，会陆续放出来。

text:
在硅谷，乔布斯那辆银色奔驰SL55 AMG是出了名的怪车。它前后常年不挂车牌，在马路上大摇大摆开了好几年，警察却始终拿它没有办法。

不少人以为这是亿万富豪的特权，其实乔布斯钻的是加州法律里的一个小空子。按当时的规定，新车上路后有最多6个月的宽限期，在这段时间里，不挂正式车牌是完全合法的；

于是他跟汽车租赁公司谈好，每辆车快开满6个月的时候，对方就送来一辆一模一样的新车，把旧的换走。这样一来，车永远是新的，宽限期自然也就永远用不完了，外人根本就看不出他已经换了一辆又一辆。

对于这件事，租赁公司当然乐得配合，因为手里会源源不断多出一辆辆只开了几个月的顶级奔驰，而且转手就能卖个好价钱。这个口子一直开到2019年，直到加州专门修改了法律，规定新车一出厂就得挂上临时牌照，才算彻底把这个口子给堵上了。

text:
Why ETH is the store of value for what's coming

We are almost certainly heading into a period of high inflation and extreme economic and social volatility. As inflation and risk erode the purchasing power of nation-state money and many other assets, it will matter more than ever to hold assets that keep or grow their value.

Gold and BTC are high-powered money and excellent stores of value. ETH goes further.

Not debt-based. Like gold and BTC, ETH is not debt-based or credit-based money.

Censorship resistant. Like BTC, or gold and silver held physically, ETH transactions on Ethereum L1 can't be censored. That's true for simple payments and for complex smart contract programs like DeFi, and those programs are guaranteed to execute.

Cheap to hold. Like BTC, ETH is relatively cheap to hold and store securely.

Cheap to use at any scale. Ethereum is cheap and easy to use whether a transaction moves $1 or billions. Any well-formed transaction is guaranteed to execute.

Sound, and getting sounder. ETH is disinflationary and becomes ultrasound, meaning deflationary, during periods of high network activity.

Broadly useful. ETH has many uses across the Ethereum economy, and that economy will grow by orders of magnitude as finance, and eventually every industry, moves onchain. Global adoption of the Web protocols in the '90s and '00s transformed the world economy. Ethereum is the foundation of Web3, the user-centric, decentralized web.

Collateral money. ETH works as collateral, and collateral that grows in value over time is a powerful thing.

Home of stablecoins. Ethereum hosts the bulk of stablecoin activity. Stablecoins serve as payment money and as unit-of-account money.

Despot-proof. Like BTC, ETH can't be used by a despot to financially exploit or repress citizens. Over time that should have positive geopolitical effects.

Programmable. ETH is programmable money. You can attach arbitrary logic to transactions and build an entire economy on smart-contract-based agreements and business processes (see https://t.co/JcWtBUclr2).

Transparent or private, and auditable either way. Money and financial instruments on Ethereum can be public or private, and in both cases selectively disclosable and auditable. Privacy tools for retail and institutional users include VPNs, mix networks, shielded and privacy pools, Railgun, stealth addresses, Kohaku, and zero-knowledge proofs in many forms, including on L2s and on private permissioned EVM networks linked through bridgeless synchronous composability.

Future-proof. By the end of 2027, or partway through 2028 at the latest, ETH will be quantum-safe and AI-safe money.

ETH is the base money of an exponentially growing ecosystem that should keep growing for decades. Its monetary premium will keep rising, because retail, corporate, and government users will all need to hold some. Part of today's premium is speculative: Ethereum dominates smart contract blockchains, but it hasn't fully hit its stride or gone mainstream yet.

Machine intelligence will supercharge every scientific and technological pursuit and grow global GDP bigger and faster than any of us can imagine. Ethereum L1 and modular Ethereum L2s will undergird most of the high-value agreements, transactions, payment flows, and complex business processes behind the coming hybrid human-machine decentralized economy.
author: lex_node
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
Onchain identity gets a lot more useful when it stops meaning “upload everything about yourself.”

One thing I’ve been looking at from @primus_labs is the BNB ZK ID stack.

The idea is pretty clean:

an app can verify a specific fact from your Web2 account without needing the full account data.

Current supported sources include:

→ Binance
→ OKX
→ GitHub
→ Steam
→ Amazon

Under the hood, Primus zkTLS verifies the offchain data source first.

Then Brevis zkVM handles the proof computation.

So instead of giving an app your entire account history, the flow becomes:
verify one claim → generate the proof → attest it onchain.

That feels much closer to how onchain identity should work.

Not “show me everything.”

Just prove what actually matters.

text:
曾患睾丸癌，父亲没等到救命药。或许这才是 Anthropic CEO 达里奥·阿莫代伊如此重视 AI 医疗的原因。

阿莫代伊曾患早期睾丸癌，最终成功治愈。但他的父亲却因丙型肝炎去世。几年后，新一代抗病毒药物问世，治愈率达到约 95%。父亲只差几年，就可能等到救命药。

这种遗憾，也成为阿莫代伊思考 AI 与医学关系的重要背景。

2024 年，他提出「压缩的 21 世纪」：利用超过顶尖科学家的 AI，将原本需要 50 至 100 年才能取得的医学进步，压缩到 5 至 10 年。

如今，Anthropic 不仅在 IPO 路演中预测癌症、阿尔茨海默病、心脏病等重大疾病可能在不到 10 年内被攻克，还开始亲自下场：

与百时美施贵宝等 6 家生物医药机构合作；
收购药物研发公司 Mithril Medicine；
借助 Claude 协调实验室、分析数据，将一种罕见肌肉萎缩疾病的潜在疗法在不到 18 个月内推进至动物实验。

这也解释了 Anthropic 为什么如此重视医疗和生物医药。

对阿莫代伊而言，AI 不只是更强的聊天机器人，也不只是一个万亿美元估值的商业故事。如果 AI 能让一种救命药提前几年问世，那么它改变的就是一个家庭的命运。

当然，从动物实验到临床治愈仍有漫长距离。但阿莫代伊想押注的，是 AI 能否让人类第一次拥有大幅压缩医学进步时间的能力。
