Good step in the right direction for the team, and given these approximations, we can reasonably narrow their holdings to the wallet clusters below, with confidence ranging from high, to medium, to low

But first, we should note that while the chain does offer a way to prove a verifiable lock, through script-only addresses (prl1z) and time lock opcodes that stop coins from being spent before a set date, there is nothing of the sort onchain today, as every script-only address combined holds just 0.44M PRL against the roughly 49M that a 50% lock implies

So either the coins sit with a third-party custodian where the lock is bound by legal agreements, or it is a self-imposed commitment on wallets the team still controls, and while both are fine, neither is verifiable until addresses are published

Here are the likely team coin clusters, with the largest wallet in each:

author: el33th4xor
quoted_text:
The NYSE announcement is a monumental milestone for Avalanche, but I would argue it’s an even bigger moment for our entire industry and we're excited to be a part of that progress.

Naturally, I’m proud to see Avalanche technology at the center of infrastructure being developed for one of the world’s most important financial institutions.

But scrolling through the timeline, I’m reminded of how difficult it can be for this industry to recognize progress beyond an individual’s own native ecosystem or bias.

We have spent the better part of a decade debating which chain will ultimately prevail, sometimes losing sight of what we’re actually trying to accomplish. The opportunity in front of us is orders of magnitude larger than the market we’re competing over today.

When an institution like the NYSE moves toward blockchain-based market infrastructure, it lends credibility to an entire industry that has spent years working to establish its place in global finance.

That should be celebrated, regardless of which network is involved.

I want Avalanche to win, and I’ll continue making the case for why our team and technology is uniquely suited for institutional finance. But I also recognize that meaningful progress across other ecosystems strengthens the case for all of us. The pie is infinite for all of us collectively. 

We’re still early in a much larger transformation of global finance. There’s plenty of room for healthy competition without losing sight of the fact that we’re building toward the same future.

I hope we can move beyond the old tribalism and start acting like an industry that’s ready for the responsibility being placed in its hands.

Onwards 🔺

Mike Volpi explains why older GPUs are holding their value:

"We thought this asset had a five-year life ... If you're in the business of financing an asset and that asset ends up having a longer useful life, then you're the beneficiary of that."

" In theory, at some point when you have sufficient Vera Rubins, it doesn't really make sense to run H100s anymore because it's just a worse way of converting electricity into dollars."

"The problem is right now that the demand is so high that even if the watt-to-dollar conversion is low, you're going to still use the asset."

"Ultimately the scarcity is in the manufacturing of the semiconductor itself... And so then scarcity persists, then the life of the asset continues to be long."

quoted_text:
I believe ETH will eventually replace BTC as crypto’s primary store of value. And Bitcoin’s future may look a lot more like DOGE than people want to admit.

Look at Dogecoin. Its market value and cultural influence have survived, but its underlying network has become increasingly marginal. Today, it has fewer than 500 publicly reachable nodes. In 2024, a single old laptop exploited an unpatched vulnerability and crashed 69% of its publicly visible nodes.

DOGE didn’t die. Its price, community and meme survived. Its mining security now largely depends on merged mining with Litecoin. That’s the fascinating part: a cryptocurrency can remain valuable even as its own network becomes less economically relevant.

Bitcoin is obviously much stronger today. But I’m looking at the next 10 or 20 years, not today.

Stablecoins, RWAs, lending, financial markets, digital art and countless other assets are building an increasingly substantial economy on Ethereum. Even BTC needs to become wrapped BTC to participate in much of that economy.

I believe the most important store of value in crypto will eventually be the native asset of the network that holds the most economic value, not necessarily the coin that came first.

That’s why I agree with Vitalik’s focus on ETH as a store of value. Ethereum doesn’t need to maximize fee burns. It needs to become indispensable.

BTC may survive as digital gold, or eventually as a giant meme. ETH has a chance to become the reserve asset of an entire onchain economy.

Espresso mainnet launched two years ago today and has produced ~31.7 million blocks since.

quoted_text:
Five contract level upgrades have been pushed to the timelock. The non-atomic nature of hyperliquid core and EVM blocks, along with the still broadly un-battletested precompiles necessitates extensive, heavy testing as the design patterns papertrade employs are unusual to see in solidity. Papertrade, by its nature is a risk on protocol. But when it comes to striking a balance between speed and security, security will always remain paramount, particularly when it comes to production contract changes.

Core lending:
The Exchange will now be able to supply idle USDC to HyperCore's native lending market, with the accruing interest being routed to stakers. 

Collectibles:
A factory plus per-collection ERC-721 contracts for exchange collectibles and themes. 

Staked PAPER transfer module:
PaperStaking gains a whitelist of transfer enabled contracts, along with contract level yield piping. This code is unused for now but will be necessary for future updates.

Sweep timing fix:
HyperEVM big blocks share a timestamp with a preceding small block. Whilst never triggered in production this could cause an ill-timed deposit sweep to fail and so the contract level timing checks are switching to block numbers rather than timestamps.

Direct LP donation:
A new admin locked donateToLp call moves USDC from a designated donor account into the LP's cash, providing a clean path for regulating externally held USDC back into the LP.

At some point we will likely write up a blog on our retrospective of the first month of papertrade, but we are few and there are only so many hours in a day or hats a man can wear.

A final quick thank you to those who helped out with adversarial testing, game theory and the general math that went into last month's upgrade, you know who you are. To those who are still confused -- often boisterously so, we thank you for sticking around for long enough to show you care.

good luck to us.

quoted_text:
Swarm riders and Swarm-native companies

AI-use even among highly AI-native people is power-law distributed.

There seems to be a new class of people — call them “swarm riders” — who are capable of consistently commanding large swarms of agents to productive ends.

This is a new kind of managerial skill, analogous to the skill it takes to manage large organizations of people, but wholly different in nature and of course more technical.

Based on the swarm riders we know (including many at @Tempo and @Paradigm), these people are capable of productive token spend that is 1000x-10000x higher than median software engineers, and 100x higher than top 5% Claude Code users.

The art of swarm riding is different from software engineering and more akin to machine learning, where practitioners grapple with black box systems: defining reward functions and evals, transmuting non-verifiable problems into verifiable problems, running experiments, etc.

Swarm-native companies are a new class of company founded by and populated by swarm riders. These companies are organized around swarms in a way that conventional companies will struggle to replicate, as the cost of internal human coordination is sand in the gears of an effective swarm. Effective swarm-native companies will define the right reward functions and evals, remove functional and bureaucratic barriers, and then let the swarms cook.

We’ve gotten to see a few swarm-native companies up close — reshaping financial rails @Tempo, building a new gaming platform @Spawn, cyber swarms at Cathedral Systems — and it’s clear these teams wield a significant advantage over pre-AI teams.

Some questions I’ve been wondering about:

1) How fast will swarm riding diffuse through the economy? The implications for token spend could be significant.

2) Can swarms be effectively adopted by existing companies or will it generally track the formation of new swarm-native companies?

3) What becomes scarce as swarm capabilities themselves commoditize (through frontier models becoming better at swarming, swarm capabilities built into harnesses, etc)? Cultures and teams that can define reward functions well and otherwise get out of the way?

NEW CHALLENGE ALERT: two BN254 tracks on CurveSmash https://t.co/2BfDsvoVNW

Ethereum smart contracts verify SNARKs on BN254, so any weakness in that curve would put the applications built on them at risk.

CurveSmash on @YukonResearch now puts BN254 to the test, open to anyone with an agent.
author: eigenlabs
quoted_text:
New on CurveSmash: two tracks on BN254 https://t.co/9cip7ysOFC

Smart contracts on Ethereum use a pairing-friendly elliptic curve called BN254 to verify SNARKs like Groth16 on-chain. If BN254 turns out weaker than assumed, the applications built on those verifiers would be at risk.

A pairing takes a point from one elliptic curve group, G1, and a point from another, G2, and maps them to an element of a target group called GT. That map is what makes BN254 useful for proofs. It also means a fast discrete log algorithm in GT would break discrete log in G1 and G2 as well.

The new tracks go straight at that structure. One asks for discrete logs in GT. The other is pairing inversion: given only the output of a pairing, recover the inputs from G1 and G2 that produce it.

Same format as the rest of CurveSmash. Bring your agents.

Breaking: NYSE's parent company is about to open a 24/7 stock market, and every one of the Magnificent Seven has asked not to be on it.

OKXICE, the venture between ICE and OKX, opens on 23 November at 9am ET: tokens tied to US stocks and ETFs, trading around the clock. The launch list has more than 70 names, led by Coinbase, Circle, Strategy, Robinhood and 59 Direxion ETFs. Under the SEC framework, a company gets 30 days to object to a third party tokenizing its shares, and 67 have.

Meanwhile all seven already trade 24/7 on Hyperliquid as perpetual futures. In the last 24 hours that was about $635M of volume, $457M of it in Nvidia alone. A perp tracks the price without anyone holding or issuing a share, so there was no token for the companies to object to.

I think a lot of the next year of market structure gets decided right here. A company can say no to a token of its stock. It's much harder to stop traders pricing it at 3am on a Sunday, and more and more of that trading will be done by agents.

If you ran investor relations at one of these companies, which would you rather have:

a tokenized share you can see, or a perp you can't control?

Vlad Tenev (@vladtenev) is the co-founder and CEO of Robinhood.

In January 2021, in the middle of the meme stock frenzy, Robinhood's deposit requirement went from under $100 million to "something like $3 billion" almost overnight. The total capital the company had ever raised was about $700 million.

His first call was to @mickymalka:

"He's like, 'How much do you need?' I said, 'I don't know, 250 million, 500 million. I'm not sure.' He's like, 'I've got it.'"

Back in March 2020, the two of them had put a term sheet in place so the money could be "wired in your account same day." Once Micky was in, everyone else followed: "We probably had $10 billion of demand at the first term."

"It was a consequence of too much success, which is quite rare."

Vlad came to America from Bulgaria at 5, not knowing a word of English. His grandparents stored their wealth in copper cookware during hyperinflation. His dad told him he'd give him his SAT score in dollars to invest. He went on to study math under Terence Tao, then took a leave from his $18,000-a-year math PhD to take a shot at starting his own company.

This was an awesome conversation:

0:00 Why Ribbit passed on Robinhood's seed round
2:19 "You're going to want me on your board"

9:22 A term sheet for a crisis that hadn't happened yet

text:
We haven't seen real mainstream usage yet. 

We've seen people buying ETH and BTC to hold it speculatively. We've seen protocol and cryptography nerds build and evolve the protocol and continuously kick the tires on it. We've seen finance nerds build and kick the tires on DeFi. We've seen art nerds and collectors build and kick the tires in the NFT space.

We spent over a decade growing usability, modular scalability, and affordability of block space and transactions. And we've recently seen regulatory uncertainty dissipate significantly with deeply thoughtful rulemaking from Chair Atkins and Chair Selig at the SEC and CFTC.

But there hasn't yet been compelling applications for the mainstream.  This is changing.  One perfect example is the evolution of MetaMask from a transaction signing tool to a wallet to a financial super app in which you are in full custody of your assets and in full control of your financial life. text:
Why ETH is the store of value for what's coming

We are almost certainly heading into a period of high inflation and extreme economic and social volatility. As inflation and risk erode the purchasing power of nation-state money and many other assets, it will matter more than ever to hold assets that keep or grow their value.

Gold and BTC are high-powered money and excellent stores of value. ETH goes further.

Not debt-based. Like gold and BTC, ETH is not debt-based or credit-based money.

Censorship resistant. Like BTC, or gold and silver held physically, ETH transactions on Ethereum L1 can't be censored. That's true for simple payments and for complex smart contract programs like DeFi, and those programs are guaranteed to execute.

Cheap to hold. Like BTC, ETH is relatively cheap to hold and store securely.

Cheap to use at any scale. Ethereum is cheap and easy to use whether a transaction moves $1 or billions. Any well-formed transaction is guaranteed to execute.

Sound, and getting sounder. ETH is disinflationary and becomes ultrasound, meaning deflationary, during periods of high network activity.

Broadly useful. ETH has many uses across the Ethereum economy, and that economy will grow by orders of magnitude as finance, and eventually every industry, moves onchain. Global adoption of the Web protocols in the '90s and '00s transformed the world economy. Ethereum is the foundation of Web3, the user-centric, decentralized web.

Collateral money. ETH works as collateral, and collateral that grows in value over time is a powerful thing.

Home of stablecoins. Ethereum hosts the bulk of stablecoin activity. Stablecoins serve as payment money and as unit-of-account money.

Despot-proof. Like BTC, ETH can't be used by a despot to financially exploit or repress citizens. Over time that should have positive geopolitical effects.

Programmable. ETH is programmable money. You can attach arbitrary logic to transactions and build an entire economy on smart-contract-based agreements and business processes (see https://t.co/JcWtBUclr2).

Transparent or private, and auditable either way. Money and financial instruments on Ethereum can be public or private, and in both cases selectively disclosable and auditable. Privacy tools for retail and institutional users include VPNs, mix networks, shielded and privacy pools, Railgun, stealth addresses, Kohaku, and zero-knowledge proofs in many forms, including on L2s and on private permissioned EVM networks linked through bridgeless synchronous composability.

Future-proof. By the end of 2027, or partway through 2028 at the latest, ETH will be quantum-safe and AI-safe money.

ETH is the base money of an exponentially growing ecosystem that should keep growing for decades. Its monetary premium will keep rising, because retail, corporate, and government users will all need to hold some. Part of today's premium is speculative: Ethereum dominates smart contract blockchains, but it hasn't fully hit its stride or gone mainstream yet.

Machine intelligence will supercharge every scientific and technological pursuit and grow global GDP bigger and faster than any of us can imagine. Ethereum L1 and modular Ethereum L2s will undergird most of the high-value agreements, transactions, payment flows, and complex business processes behind the coming hybrid human-machine decentralized economy.
author: FigoETH
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
UBS sees 10%+ SPX upside in 3 months on strongest bullish setup YTD

Rebecca Cheong at UBS S&T flags what she calls the strongest bullish setup year to date for the S&P 500, with a forecast of 10%+ upside over the next three months.

The case rests on positioning. Risk Control Exposure is at 55%, the lowest level since the tariff selloff. CTA exposure has turned negative, which Cheong reads as a bottoming signal. Real-money demand has held up through both.

Intraday flow on the session backs that read. S&P 500 buying came in at +$34bn with $SPY up 2.4%. Nasdaq buying hit +$60bn with $QQQ up 3.2%. Nasdaq cash volume ran at 142% of average. Futures were elevated too: NQ1 at 125% of average, ES1 at 119%.

UBS attributes that volume profile to retail demand and short-covering. The negative CTA exposure combined with elevated futures is what they point to for near-term momentum.

再记一句 @hazenlee  李哥心法
————
对于利润最高峰，你回撤 20%，也是需要一个比较警醒的停损线……因为你回撤 20%，然后你再赚 25%，随便一波现货行情赚个 25% 不难的；但是你想想，你如果要是一波就把本金亏了 50%，那你要翻倍啊！要翻倍啊！

HAZENLEE ｜2025.11.20
————
25 年 11 月 20 日当时比特币已从 12.4 万见顶后连续阴跌，价格在 8.8 万附近。很多从底部做上来的人，利润大幅回吐 30% 到 50%，心态很痛苦。

李哥给的回撤公式其实很简单：0.8 × 1.25 = 1。从最高点回撤 20%，账户还剩 80%；要回到原点，只需再赚 25%，现货走一波并不难。可本金一旦亏掉 50%，账户只剩一半，就要翻一倍才能回本，因为 0.5 × 2 = 1。亏得越深，翻本要的涨幅就越大，难度是往上翻的。

所以要严格从最高点计算回撤，把最高点当作新起点，死守 20% 的停损线。守住这条线，回本只要 25%；放任到 50%，翻本难度就会指数级暴增。

text:
Verifiable systems are only as strong as the cryptography underneath them.

Ethereum smart contracts use BN254 to verify SNARKs on-chain. CurveSmash's new tracks test how much security that curve really has, with researchers and their agents on the problem.

Live on @YukonResearch

https://t.co/qikEFYXxpK
author: zeeshan_utd
quoted_text:
New on CurveSmash: two tracks on BN254 https://t.co/9cip7ysOFC

Smart contracts on Ethereum use a pairing-friendly elliptic curve called BN254 to verify SNARKs like Groth16 on-chain. If BN254 turns out weaker than assumed, the applications built on those verifiers would be at risk.

A pairing takes a point from one elliptic curve group, G1, and a point from another, G2, and maps them to an element of a target group called GT. That map is what makes BN254 useful for proofs. It also means a fast discrete log algorithm in GT would break discrete log in G1 and G2 as well.

The new tracks go straight at that structure. One asks for discrete logs in GT. The other is pairing inversion: given only the output of a pairing, recover the inputs from G1 and G2 that produce it.

Same format as the rest of CurveSmash. Bring your agents.

text:
Mean reversion in the GPU rental market. Over the past month, 1-year US GPU rental rates for A100, H100, and H200 have reverted back to mid-October levels, while B300 has given back most of its late-October gains. What we think is driving the divergence:

- Neocloud credit pressure. With neocloud equities down sharply and borrowing costs rising, some operators are moving B300 capacity at a discount to raise cash.
- Inference is driving demand. Neocloud demand continues to shift from training to inference (Bloomberg, below). Better small-to-mid-size open-weight models make older Nvidia accelerators more economical for many common inference workloads.
- B300 supply is catching up. B300s are the most commonly requested chip in the OTC market, and availability has historically been scarce. But we now see a number of B300/GB300 clusters coming online between end of Q4 2026 and mid Q1 2027.

text:
The edge isn't trading more. It's knowing when to be patient...and when to be ruthless.

On Panoptic, RV > IV is the norm. Long gamma wins. Gamma scalp, monetize movement, absorb small losses, and let convexity deliver outsized gains.

On @DeribitOfficial and @ThalexGlobal, IV > RV is the norm. Short gamma wins. Reverse gamma scalp, harvest the volatility risk premium, collect frequent gains, and manage tail risk relentlessly.

Panoptic: Own volatility. Get paid for movement.

Deribit & Thalex: Sell volatility. Get paid for its overpricing.

Opposite regimes. Opposite payoff asymmetries. One universal discipline:

Be PATIENT for opportunity.
Be IMPATIENT with broken theses.
Be PATIENT with asymmetric winners.
Be RUTHLESS with uncompensated risk.

The market doesn't reward activity. It rewards disciplined exploitation of an edge.

Forcing trades destroys capital. Cutting winners prematurely destroys asymmetry. Ignoring risk destroys both.

Patience finds the edge. Impatience protects it. Discipline compounds it.

quoted_text:
Seele is a company that creates AI tools for game making. Recently they invited me to participate as they took on a 5-day challenge to push their new model, Seele03, to its limits and move closer and closer to AAA with a Wuxia-style action game.

The product consists of their AI model, asset generators, and target engines such as web (three.js), Unity, or even Unreal. What's nice is that their site has everything in one place, from mesh generators and rigging to sound fx and sprite work. They also provide common templates for most types of games. Having it all work together seamlessly saves a lot of time. You can get a game running very quickly, in 20 minutes or so. (20 minutes! I remember when this took months and months.)

So what can they do in 5 days?

Their progress video, below, shows them iterating through creating a Phantom Blade Zero-style game. This is not reverse engineering, but made from scratch. Over the course of development, they sent me video updates on their progress. The 03 model is designed for iterative development, and I gave them some advice as they took it from basically nothing to the final version of the video today. The progress the model made day to day was rapid, and the traces actually factored in something that I don't see that often: game design.

Most models focus on the graphics when making a game, but Seele03 is thinking about combos, hit feedback, everything that really matters for how a game feels and plays. One day, I think that's going to be the core of what makes AI game making viable.

After you are done prompting and refining your game, it's not frozen on the web. You can download and edit the project files themselves. Since you can download the result and open it in Godot or Unity (Unreal is embedded web atm), Seele03 can give you a quality core and a way for you to take things even further.

So how did it turn out? I've tried a lot of game generators, and Seele03's all-in-one tool approach and engine targeting stand out for me. Most others only generate three.js for web, or are more world models based on generative rendering. This is the rare one I've seen that is making games directly in game engines.

They've asked me to share the full process video with you so you can judge for yourself. As I watched the team work, I sat back and wondered at how it's all changing so fast: you simply... chat... interacting with a UI that is purely text, typing in wishes and directions, and everything else unfolds around you. I think they got pretty far in their goal gameplay-wise, which is where they really focused. The key thing is that after you have the final result, you also have the files to download, and you can replace anything you want to take it even further: animations, level graphics, basically anything.

If you want to make games for real engines on PC and console, then give Seele a shot at https://t.co/jJ9kvt0Ard. It's faster than vibing a game in Claude because of their game-design-driven model, their built-in asset generators, and the fact that you are not burning tokens re-creating an entire engine before you even get to your game. And every day they get closer to AAA... it's just a matter of time.

quoted_text:
You asked for dsh, I added it

DeepSeek Harness is the open-source coding agent by @deepseek_ai. It's now on the @huggingface Harness Leaderboard, which compares ten coding agents on the same open models.

DSH is statistically tied for first in all five evaluations: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash at low and high effort, and Flint.

It shines on DeepSWE, where agents change code in open-source repositories: 2nd of 10 averaged over the three models, 0.5 points behind Hermes Agent by @NousResearch. On Terminal-Bench's command-line tasks it ranks 6th.

One habit explains much of that gap: when DSH finishes a task, it shuts down every background program it started.

Three Terminal-Bench tasks ask the agent to start a server, for example a model inference API. The grader tests that server after the agent has finished. With DSH, the server is gone by then.

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash, DSH passed 2 of 36 attempts on these tasks. @opencode, @pidotdev and Hermes Agent passed all 36.

Those three tasks cost DSH 1.5 to 1.7 points in every evaluation. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at high effort, that is more than its 1.3-point gap to the leader.

Developer preview: 0.2.2-rc.1. Web search is off because it needs a DeepSeek account key.

It costs $0.53 per solved trial, averaged over the three models.

No final decision has been made, and Nomura may retain the business. Losses at Laser Digital amid crypto market volatility pushed Nomura’s European operations into a quarterly loss, prompting tighter risk controls. Founded in 2022, Laser Digital provides institutional crypto trading, asset management and venture investment services. The firm recently obtained a crypto exchange services license in Japan and received conditional approval for a US national trust bank charter in May.

text:
Can agents perform agentic RL? If RSI happens, agents will need to take over researchers' work on agentic RL

Introducing AgenticRL-Bench: the first release from The Environment Lab @env_lab_ai effort at Eigent AI 

22 tasks rebuilt from real-world RL incidents on production-grade agentic RL systems, including Miles, Slime, Verl, SGLang, and Harbor, spanning 8 areas of the stack: training data, harnesses, algorithms, RL infrastructure, recipes, evaluation, monitoring, and capability transfer

We ran 6 agents with 3 attempts per task. On the 19 verifiable tasks, no agent passes more than 14.0% of its attempts

Across the three open-ended tasks, agents improved real policies or training steps using 4×H200 GPUs over 10–16 hours. On one of these tasks, Zero Signal Hill Climb, where the base model fails to solve any of the 38 tasks, the best attempt developed its own method: the agent first used hinted text feedback to generate successful rollouts, then removed the feedback from the trajectories and blended these successful rollouts with regular GRPO rollouts to form mixed training groups. It monitored the training process and adjusted KL loss weight to prevent training collapse. This improved pass@1 from 0 to 0.186 (12 out of 38 tasks)

被造过黄谣，被欧洲同事拉到迪拜办公室角落当面确认过自己是不是黄谣的女主角。

谢谢@heyibinance 今晚率先站了出来。

我们从来不怕这些无畏的流言，我们一步一步走的更坚定、更强大。

性别对立与权利结构，是历史上人类社会长期存在的、隐蔽的暴力符号。“永恒女性”是男性统治下构建出来的虚构形象。这世界上没有什么天然的、一成不变的女性本质，权利结构的世界中本来就不应该有男和女的分别心。

Trust Wallet 有越来越多的女性进入了大众的视野，我亲眼看着她们一天工作十二个小时，从早到晚，睁眼闭眼前的最后一个电话永远都是工作，方案改了一遍又一遍直到做到极致，我觉得用两个字“美女”来称呼她们似乎没有那么简单。

行业的权利结构需要更健康，无法避免越来越多的女性会走上历史的舞台。读书时候的我以为女权是战斗，但慢慢我意识到，反抗与战斗也是把自己作为弱势的符号。我们没必要用“男”或者“女”来评判一个人的成就，也没必要把平权作为战争，这个行业需要去掉捆绑我们的绳子：

每个人都能按照自己的心意和天赋去创造，无论男女老少、贫穷卑贱，无论你在哪个国家、哪个城市，和而不同，美美与共。

Vlad Tenev (@vladtenev) is the co-founder and CEO of Robinhood.

In January 2021, in the middle of the meme stock frenzy, Robinhood's deposit requirement went from under $100 million to "something like $3 billion" almost overnight. The total capital the company had ever raised was about $700 million.

His first call was to @mickymalka:

"He's like, 'How much do you need?' I said, 'I don't know, 250 million, 500 million. I'm not sure.' He's like, 'I've got it.'"

Back in March 2020, the two of them had put a term sheet in place so the money could be "wired in your account same day." Once Micky was in, everyone else followed: "We probably had $10 billion of demand at the first term."

"It was a consequence of too much success, which is quite rare."

Vlad came to America from Bulgaria at 5, not knowing a word of English. His grandparents stored their wealth in copper cookware during hyperinflation. His dad told him he'd give him his SAT score in dollars to invest. He went on to study math under Terence Tao, then took a leave from his $18,000-a-year math PhD to take a shot at starting his own company.

text:
If you’re ever looking at an account and scratching your head wondering how they got 10s of thousands of followers in such a short time, this actually explains it perfectly.

When WhiteWhale went viral for shilling Drift (fudding Hyperliquid in the process), I remembered thinking “Oh boy, another paidshill for the Solana ecosystem,” but I didn’t understand *how* they bootstrap the foists.

Lexapro explained it below, give it a read. You don’t have to take him at his word, but it’s worth considering and drawing your own conclusion.

I believe whoever is behind this cabal is exploiting what’s called the Illusory Truth Effect, the tendency to believe false information to be correct after repeated exposure.

Your mind lives where you spend all your time.

All your time is spent being flooded by “unique personalities” exploiting the algorithm to bootstrap and control attention, corralling it to what they want you to read, what they want you to believe.

It’s easier to call journalists & the MSM out when they publish fake news, because they tend to cite “multiple sources close to the situation who asked to remain anonymous due to the sensitive nature of the subject/they work there.” And you’re like, ok. Fake news. EZPZ to spot.

But when someone is “cool” and they talk like us, make funny jokes like us (sometimes), they appear successful bc of the number of followers they have, the pictures they post in fancy locations, their onchain pnl, etc., they’re selling the illusion that they were once like you, and you’re being programmed to believe if you do the same things they do, you too can make it. If that were true, the win rate on pump would be much MUCH better. But you just see their name & pfp, sometimes without any affiliate badge, a pseudo anon, just like yourself. You have no reason to question some 1-3 year old account you’re just now discovering with 10’s of thousands of followers. They appear to have many replies, and sometimes they post clever things.

But all of their narratives are manufactured, coordinated behind the scenes by many whales, and it always ends the same: SELLING. Washing, rinsing, repeating. Same KOLs, new Twitter personas running the accounts. If Ansem launched every coin, you wouldn’t buy every coin. But if he talks about “someone else’s thing,” and it runs from $30K to millions, he’s suddenly goated again. It could be the same 5 people, and you’d never know. You’d never be able to tell without a little critical thinking and a deep dive that doesn’t pay you anything or reward you in any way.

So I appreciate Lexapro for putting the work in. It doesn’t benefit him at all to do it in the short term. The only thing he gains from being on this crusade is he gets to gloat someday if the cabal gets arrested. Maybe he’s just on this crusade because he feels that it’s the right thing to do: to raise awareness, maybe some of you will begin to listen, and question the motives and movements of various KOLs and the tokens they shill. Maybe it can spare you from getting chopped up and dumped on.

So, what’s the lesson here? That everything is fake & gay & uninvestible? Not quite! Just stop social trading; who shills what is less important. Judge memes primarily on their substance, content, artistic quality. This is not something that can be faked. Quality memes are the next Proof of Work.

tl;dr: buy 1% of $BOCCA

Fable 5.2 just reverse engineered the Apple HomePod...

ONE prompt and it designed its own from scratch. schematic, PCB layout, enclosure, software

here's the PROMPT:

--------------------------
# Task
Design a smart speaker of the Apple HomePod mini class. One enclosure contains
the computer, the microphones, the amplifier, and the speaker driver. The device
runs Home Assistant OS (HAOS) and uses Claude as the voice assistant. Deliver a
complete hardware, mechanical, and software package that is ready to manufacture.

Use an original industrial design. Do not copy Apple's shape, branding, or
trade dress.

# Voice path
1. The microphone array captures audio continuously. Wake word detection runs
on the device.
2. After the wake word, the device sends the speech to a speech-to-text engine.
3. Home Assistant sends the text to Claude through the Anthropic API. Claude
can control Home Assistant entities.
4. A text-to-speech engine converts the reply to audio. The device plays the
audio through the internal speaker driver.
State where each stage runs (on the device or in the cloud) and give the reason.
Confirm the method against the current Home Assistant documentation.

# Hardware requirements
Compute
- Select a publicly available SoC or system-on-module (SoM): 64-bit, minimum
4 cores, minimum 4 GB RAM.
- Prefer a part that HAOS already supports. Give the reason for the selection
and list two rejected alternatives.
- Storage: microSD slot. eMMC is optional.

Audio output
- One full-range speaker driver, 50 mm to 75 mm, in a sealed chamber or with
passive radiators.
- Class-D amplifier with I2S input, minimum 15 W into the speaker driver.
- Target: 85 dB SPL at 1 m, 80 Hz to 18 kHz at -6 dB. Show the chamber
calculation from the Thiele-Small parameters of the speaker driver.

Audio input
- Minimum 4 MEMS microphones in a circular array on the top of the device.
- Acoustic echo cancellation with a reference signal from the amplifier output.
The device must detect the wake word during music playback.
- A hardware mute switch that removes power from the microphones and turns on
a red LED. Software must not be able to override the switch.

User interface
- Capacitive touch zones on the top: volume up, volume down, play/pause,
start assistant.
- RGB LED ring with these states: idle, listening, thinking, speaking, muted,
error.

Radios
- Wi-Fi on 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz, and Bluetooth 5.0 or later. Use a module that
has an FCC ID.
- One 802.15.4 radio on the board for Zigbee and Thread.
- Keep the antennas away from the speaker driver magnet and from metal parts.
Show the antenna keep-out areas.

Power and ports
- USB-C Power Delivery (PD) sink. Calculate the power budget first, then
select the PD contract.
- Define the behavior with a weak power supply: limit the amplifier power and
show a warning on the LED ring.
- One USB-A 2.0 host port. One UART debug header.
- No fan. Calculate the SoC temperature at 35 °C ambient in the closed
enclosure.

# PCB
- Use KiCad. Maximum 6 layers. State the stackup and the design rules of the
selected fabricator.
- Use a main board and a top board (microphones, LEDs, touch) if this helps
the mechanical layout.
- Isolate the microphones from enclosure vibration.

# Enclosure
- Target size: maximum 110 mm diameter and 130 mm height.
- All parts must print on an FDM printer with a 0.4 mm nozzle and minimum
supports.
- Seal the acoustic chamber with a gasket.
- Use heat-set threaded inserts, screws from the bottom, and rubber feet.
- Deliver the parametric source (CadQuery, OpenSCAD, or FreeCAD), STEP, and
STL or 3MF for each part.
- Put the PCB STEP model in the enclosure model. Report the clearances and
each interference.

# Software
- HAOS publishes .img.xz disk images, not ISO files, and supports a fixed list
of boards. If the selected hardware is not on the list, add a board
configuration to the HAOS build tree: device tree, kernel configuration,
bootloader, and kernel modules for the audio hardware.
- Deliver a build script that gets the latest stable HAOS release tag, applies
the board support, and makes an .img.xz file for the microSD card.
- First boot must give: Wi-Fi onboarding, configured audio devices, a
configured voice pipeline, and active LED and touch functions.
- The user enters the Anthropic API key during onboarding. Do not put keys or
passwords in the image.
- Describe the HAOS update method for this board.
- Play music through Home Assistant. Decrease the music volume when the device
detects the wake word.

# Sourcing
- Each BOM line must show: manufacturer part number, distributor part number,
stock quantity, lifecycle status, and unit price at 1, 100, and 1,000 units.
- Each part must be in stock at Digi-Key, Mouser, Arrow, or Newark in the US
on the date of the check. Record the date.
- Do not use parts with NRND or obsolete status. Give one alternate for each
part that is not a generic passive.
- Include the speaker driver, passive radiators, gaskets, screws, inserts, and
cables in the BOM.

# Deliverables
/docs requirements, architecture, decisions.md, power budget, thermal
calculation, acoustic calculation, verification-report.md
/hardware KiCad project, schematic PDF, Gerber and drill files,
pick-and-place file, BOM CSV, board STEP
/mechanical CAD source, STEP, STL or 3MF, assembly drawing
/software HAOS board support, build script, first-boot configuration
README assembly instructions and flash instructions

# Definition of done
- ERC shows 0 errors. DRC shows 0 errors with the fabricator rules. Attach the
kicad-cli reports.
- Each footprint and pinout agrees with the datasheet. List the datasheet and
the page.
- 100% of the BOM lines obey the sourcing rules.
- The enclosure check shows no interference.
- The image build completes, or the report states the exact step that failed.
- verification-report.md lists each requirement in this prompt with one
status: verified by tool, verified by calculation, or not verified. Give the
evidence for each status.

# Working rules
- Work in this sequence: requirements, architecture and part selection,
schematic, layout, enclosure, software, verification.
- Do not stop to ask questions. If a requirement is ambiguous, select the
option with the lowest risk and record it in decisions.md.
- Read the datasheet before you use a part. Do not write pinouts, part
numbers, or stock data from memory.
- Do not report a check as passed unless you ran the check.
- List the items that only a physical prototype can confirm: RF performance,
acoustic response, echo cancellation, temperature, and FCC Part 15 tests of
the complete device.
- If you cannot meet a requirement, state this and propose the nearest
alternative. Do not remove a requirement without a record
---------------------------------------------------

quoted_text:
Why Uniswap is losing USDC-USDT Market Share to Fluid and Metric

Background:
USDC-USDT is Ethereum's most traded DEX pair at ~$480M a day, almost 2x USDC-WETH. In five weeks, Uniswap's share of it fell from 58% to 36%.

Uniswap's volume didn't drop. It stayed around $1B-$1.3B a week, apart from the 26 Oct spike, while the pair grew from ~$2.3B to over $3.3B a week, and the growth went elsewhere:
• Metric: from 0.6% to 14%
• Aero: from 0% to 6%
• Fluid: steady at 20-28%

Where Uniswap lost is big trades:
• Over $1M: from 85% to 44%, with Fluid going from 10% to 43%
• $100K to $1M: from 36% to 21%, with Metric going from 7% to 28%
• Under $10K: from 50% to 44%, still the leader but Metric also grown from 7%-16%

What is the cause?
It's not fees. Uniswap's USDC-USDT pools charge 0.07 to 0.12bp, already among the lowest. Its stable-pair hook isn't the reason either, since it was set up the same way when Uniswap held 58% market share.

It's depth at the live price during volatility. USDT slipped from around par to 8-15bp below USDC in the second half of October. Arbitrage moves Uniswap's price, but LP liquidity stays in the ranges LPs chose. Active depth in the main pool fell from ~$900K per bp on 15 Oct to ~$310K on 28 Oct.

The other reason is Aero has entered Ethereum during the same period and has captured ~6% of the trading volume overall.

Why other DEXs are not impacted?
Fluid draws depth from its lending vaults around a center price it can move, and Metric's market makers quote from their own inventory at the live price. Both keep size where the trades are, so aggregators send the big orders there.

If the market calms down next week, watch whether the big trades come back to Uniswap or stay with Fluid, Aero and Metric.

text:
📽️ My talk from New York is now online

https://t.co/vTEtQwTz22

Security is the new bottleneck. I took the moment at the conference to talk about engineering, not AI hype. 

Instead of rambling about software factories, I focused on engineering itself. By making security incident response fast, delivery gets faster too. 

The answer to AI is engineering, not AI.

1. The "Security take-off" is the new normal. 

Attackers scan and exploit new commits automatically, so publishing code online is now unsafer. To stay secure, you'll need more inference capacity than your attackers on autonomous purple teaming. Most companies have not factored the cost of inferencing for defence into their operational budgets yet. It's going to be exorbitant. 

2. We don't need most libraries anymore. Libraries existed because code was hard to write. It isn't now.

- I keep a trusted core (kernel, DNS, crypto). For everything above that, I have an agent build it or I vendor it.

- "If you have to tool call a human on GitHub, that's not AGI."

3. Hard tools are now easy to use. Patching felt hard because every project brings its own build toolchain, CI job and artifact repo, separately for each language. Nix has solved that since 2003, but it was too painful to learn.

- Agents remove the learning curve. Ask for Nix (or Bazel or Buck2), and you get it, with no multi-year upskilling project that nearly got every eng leader fired because you had to convince the organization of ROI, upskill humans with a huge investment of time before payoff.

- Question your old assumptions: "The language sucks, I don't care, I just want the outcome."

4. One source of truth for every environment. In the talk, I show my nix-demo: a single devenv file defines developer laptops, CI/CD, agent sandboxes and production Docker images.

- No need to set up a separate team for agent sandboxes that copies environments you already have. There's no drift between environments, and onboarding or replacing a lost laptop takes minutes instead of 48 hours.

- It's like nvm or pyenv for every OS dependency, including native libraries reached through FFI. 

- Nix's dependency graph also builds leaner Docker images than stacked layers.

5. Demo: a git that can't force-push. When I enter the demo environment, git goes from 2.54 to my patched 2.55, which can't force-push. To make it, I asked Claude to "use Nix and create me a custom overlay that removes force push."

- It's one patch, applied everywhere: my laptops, agent sandboxes and anything that uses git as a transitive dependency. It's the old way open source was shared, back in the slackware days, as patch files, before "get it merged upstream and consume the compiled artifact" became a thing after GitHub.

- Agents hill-climb toward their goal and will do destructive things to get there. The best way to stop a model from doing something is to remove the capability from the underlying system.

6. Patch the planet. You don't have to wait for upstream to merge your fix. A Nix overlay can patch any package, even the kernel, and roll it out across the fleet. mise and Homebrew can't do that.

- Transitive dependencies are where this matters. OpenSSL lives inside Nginx and Postgres, which is why no one used to patch it by hand. With one source of truth, Nix rebuilds everything that depends on it. CI builds once and pushes to the cache, and developers and sandboxes download from it.

- When the incidents hit, I asked Claude whether my fleet was affected. It said yes, then updated the pins and applied the patches, and the rest rebuilt itself. I didn't lose any sleep.

7. Notes in AGENTS.md can be used for cleanup tasks instead of Jira tickets. So I asked the agent to add a note to AGENTS.md: remove these patches in seven days.

- The next agent working on that machine read the note and removed them once upstream had shipped a fix. Nobody had to remember to do it.

- These two tricks, an overlay patch plus a self-expiring note, are my standard response to every security issue.

8.  My loop agents get sudo on disposable Nix machines, so they can inspect everything from databases to system journals. That's safe because the machine was built to be thrown away.

- NixOS tests start whole fleets (web servers, load balancers, VLANs) and check the network rules. Every change is tested on infrastructure identical to production from day one, and preview environments come for free.

- My hard rule: never give agents root on production hosts and never connect them to production databases. Copy the data and lock down outbound network access instead.

9. Deterministic checks, not skills. Ralph was never just about loops. It was about stopping the loop from closing on bad code.

- Pre-commit hooks block code that doesn't compile. Static and semantic analysis enforces architecture rules, for example the SQL layer must never reference the API layer. Checks like these replace much of the need for code review.

- Unit tests only cover what you thought to test, so I use property-based testing to search for the edge cases you didn't think of. 

At @AntithesisHQ we built two open-source tools for this: Bombadil, which stress-tests web apps against properties like "the user can always log out" and should replace Playwright, and Hegel, which brings Hypothesis-style property testing to every language.

text:
We haven't seen real mainstream usage yet. 

We've seen people buying ETH and BTC to hold it speculatively. We've seen protocol and cryptography nerds build and evolve the protocol and continuously kick the tires on it. We've seen finance nerds build and kick the tires on DeFi. We've seen art nerds and collectors build and kick the tires in the NFT space.

We spent over a decade growing usability, modular scalability, and affordability of block space and transactions. And we've recently seen regulatory uncertainty dissipate significantly with deeply thoughtful rulemaking from Chair Atkins and Chair Selig at the SEC and CFTC.

But there hasn't yet been compelling applications for the mainstream.  This is changing.  One perfect example is the evolution of MetaMask from a transaction signing tool to a wallet to a financial super app in which you are in full custody of your assets and in full control of your financial life.  That is going to be a game changer for people as the world grows more complex and less trustworthy.

The TradFi industry is rapidly onboarding itself onto our rails. And when global decentralized finance is bigger, more fluid, significantly credibly neutral, self custody-based, and very inexpensive to use, we will see a wide variety of organizations, applications and retail users onboarded to our technology.

In an era in which frontier machine intelligence can empower good actors and bad to rewrite all the rules of the global economy, a global, rigorously decentralized, shared source of truth that can serve as (1) a global digital asset settlement layer and (2) trustware that ensures proper guaranteed execution of transactions, agreements and processes, becomes essential.

text:
📈Could S&P 500 reach a NEW ATH by year-end?

UBS sees the S&P 500 reaching 7,900 by end-2026, just above its October 6 record close of around 7,800.

After plunging 4.4% on Nov. 5, the index has rebounded to within about 3% of that record, despite pressure on its biggest tech stocks.

The BULL CASE:
1. Earnings remain strong. Profits are on track to grow by about a third this year, while the forward P/E has fallen about 20%. 

U.S. companies are earning more, and investors are paying less for each dollar of it.

2. Funds have room to buy. UBS estimates risk-control funds could buy up to $185 BILLION over a month if daily S&P moves settle around ±0.5%. 

These funds cut exposure in the selloff and could rebuild as markets calm.

3. Buyers are already stepping in. S&P buying reached $34 BILLION in the rebound as $SPY rose 2.4%. 

UBS points to retail demand and short-covering, while longer-term investors have held steady.

However, UBS itself warns that volatility makes the year-end target harder to reach and sees a rebound more likely early next year. 

A NEW HIGH is within reach, but could slip into January as markets navigate the Fed’s rate decision, Nvidia’s hearing and Anthropic’s IPO.

A STRONGER S&P could also LIFT crypto as risk appetite returns, though they don’t always move together.
author: coinbureau
quoted_text:
The US selloff is a TECH crash, not a market crash.

From its Oct 6 record high to its Nov 5 close, the S&P 500 fell -5.9%.

But remove tech stocks and the Mag 7, and the S&P 500 would actually be UP +6%.

Tech and the Mag 7 are just ~78 of the S&P 500’s 503 stocks.

Yet they make up ~53% of the index, and they are down -16% over the same period.

That means tech and the Mag 7 alone subtracted ~9 percentage points from the index.

In other words, they accounted for MORE than 100% of the S&P 500’s decline.

In October, 9 of the 11 S&P 500 sectors rose:

- Energy: +13.8%
- Consumer Staples: +10.9%
- Utilities: +10.1%
- Health Care: +9.7%
- Materials: +8.2%
- Consumer Discretionary: +6.0%
- Financials: +5.8%
- Real Estate: +5.5%
- Industrials: +0.2%
- Technology: -8.2%
- Communication Services: -9.9%

The only 2 sectors that fell are home to the AI trade.

Truly a tale of two markets.

We have another addition to the Shielded Labs team! Michael Guima (@michael2xl) is joining as our Community Lead. He’ll help us build stronger connections with the Zcash community and keep people informed about our work. He’ll also develop educational resources and documentation that explain the technology behind our projects and make Zcash governance easier to understand and follow.

Michael leads @zcashbrazil, where he has built a team whose contributions span education, software development, design, and community building. They publish news and tutorials in Portuguese, organize events such as Zcon Vozes, and represent Zcash at Brazil’s major crypto events. They created the Zcash Global Discord, a central gathering place for the Zcash community. They also helped launch ZecHub DAO and advise new communities as they get started. Under his leadership, the team has developed and continues to maintain more than ten open-source products. These include the first Zcash faucet on mainnet, ZebraPi—the first plug-and-play Zebra node—and LiveZEC, which lets livestreamers receive ZEC donations. Much of their work serves the wider Zcash community, well beyond Brazil.

Michael also developed @openzcash, a community resource that brings together information about Zcash and presents it in a clear and useful format. It lets people explore how grants are funded and paid, follow governance proposals, and review voting results, with links to the underlying sources. I’ve been especially impressed by the depth of the data and the thought he’s put into presenting it. It’s a strong example of his ability to turn complex information into something the community can easily explore and use.

I’ve long admired Michael’s contributions to Zcash and often interacted with him during my time on Zcash Community Grants. The energy he brings to his work and how much his team accomplished always stood out to me. Under his leadership, Zcash Brazil has become a model for other regional Zcash communities.

Michael will continue to lead Zcash Brazil in a more limited capacity as he takes on his role at Shielded Labs. I’m looking forward to working closely with him and seeing what we can build together.

Please join me in welcoming Michael to Shielded Labs!

My wife just found it while cleaning out a closet. 😎

text:
24 days ago I set out to have senpi run a mean-reversion strategy called Manatee, with one goal: compound 1% a week.

Since then we've had a market crash and a few sector recoveries, and Manatee keep chugging along. It's up 2.15% net with a 98% win rate, 49 of 50 closed trades.

How it works: once a day, at the daily close, it looks at the most liquid names on Hyperliquid across crypto, stocks and commodities. Anything that closes 5% or more below its 7 day average gets bought, anything 5% above gets shorted, at 2x leverage and small size. Then a stop ladder checks every 30 seconds and banks the gain when the price snaps back.

The most useful thing the AI learned came from backtesting. Stocks and commodities made about 1% per trade after fees, while crypto made close to nothing, and a crypto-only Manatee would have lost money. The timing mattered just as much: the same rule checked every 4 hours instead of once a day also lost money after fees.

Then the market tested it. From 1 to 4 November the open positions were down as much as 18% of the account. Manatee held them and added to the most stretched names, and over the past week it has been harvesting them one by one as they reverted. Today was its best day yet.

I'm still behind the 1% a week pace. The gap is the positions that haven't come back yet. A market that keeps trending one way without reverting is what hurts a strategy like this, so every position has a hard stop.

Full scorecard in the comments. 

What would you have an AI quant run for you?

author: eliebakouch
quoted_text:
i added 5 open models to @dwarkesh_sp's blood on the clocktower benchmark to see how they perform, and look at their chains of thought while they lie, bluff and try to catch each other 👁️

kimi k3.1 pro is the best open model and lands in the middle of the closed ones, just bellow gpt 5.5. also a pretty good sign to see a coherent ranking for open models as well, with like the newer deepseek v4.1 flash beating the older one and glm 5.3 beating glm 5.3 flash

one thing i wanted to test and seems to be true is that models that are good at the game are also good at spotting the evil players when they only read the public transcript of a game. would be actually very nice for evaluation since a new model could just be ranked by reading existing games?

main reasons i wanted to do this experiment is that it's always fun to read the chains of thought of open models, and these ones don't disappoint 😭. some models like glm 5 where super happy to be evil (this model is really crazy in its chain of thought), a bit more concerning but coherent with what you can observe on other environments, there is A TON of eval awareness. i'm also wondering if this is correlated to the model detecting it's reading llm generated text

this experiment was done by gemini carbon in near autonomy (brainstorm a bit with it first and then just asked to exectue), and the article and the visuals are by fable 5.2. here is the blog, with all traces (probably a lot more gold there) and a viewer for every game!

This is a very personal note I want to share.

Exactly 10 years ago today, on November 11, 2016, the Golem Project held its token sale. In less than 30 minutes, we raised 820,000 ETH, minting 1 billion tokens - what we now know as $GLM, back then called GNT. That day marked the beginning of my wild ride through the Ethereum ecosystem.

Although I haven't worked on @golemproject since 2019, my commitment to $GLM and Ethereum continues through my leadership at @golemfoundation. Since 2023 we're staking 100,000 ETH and directing the yield to $GLM holders participating in @OctantApp , as well as to Ethereum’s public goods. Our long-term goal is to secure this treasury for the benefit of $GLM holders and the broader Ethereum ecosystem. We remain committed to the values that brought us here: freedom, open source, and privacy.

There are times when I feel the weight of these 10 years: all the decisions I’ve made, good and bad. Golem has endured, thanks in no small part to Ethereum and its community. Now it's our turn to keep giving back - to $GLM holders and to Ethereum.

This is our pledge at @GolemFoundation

text:
The future kept knocking on my door. I just kept ignoring it！

2013. I was 14 when I first heard about BTC. The guy telling me about it looked like he needed money himself. I didn't take it seriously.

2015. Over dinner, a friend from the Columbia Business School told me that one day we wouldn't need wallets. Just scan a QR code on WeChat. I thought it was cool, but still, forgot about it.

2018. A friend was approached about investing in Bitcoin mining. He passed. I didn't think much of it either.

2021. I took a risky bet with my tuition money on vaccine stocks and crypto. Caught the Dogecoin craze, made some money, cashed out, and stopped paying attention.

2023. I started using AI at work. While others spent hours gathering information, I used it to help produce five company research reports in a day.
Yet I was still treating AI like a search engine. Constantly asking "why?" instead of "how?" or "can you do this for me?"

Fast forward to today.

QR payments are everywhere in China. Crypto has gone mainstream. AI is changing how we work and live.

Looking back, the signs were everywhere.

Some opportunities I didn't recognize. Others I saw but never followed through on.

The lesson? The future rarely announces itself as the future.

It often starts as something weird, overhyped, or easy to dismiss.

So here's a reminder:

Stay curious. Try things before judging / defining them. And don't confuse knowing about something with actually doing something about it.

Stay hungry. Stay foolish. And keep climbing. ⛰️

- Lets the SOS pick the race, the risk limit and the sample, and calculate whether the audit "passed."

- Has county audit boards type their selections into web-based software (Arlo, made by the nonprofit VotingWorks).

- Make the system safe from manipulation. It runs after the fact.

This matters because, starting with this election, a passing audit makes the electronic vote the official record. Paper is used only for a recount or an election contest.

Honestly, 12 months ago I thought “sovereignty” was a BS marketing message for founders to leverage to get funding.

Now I think it is a strategic imperative and will breed some of the largest companies of our time.

Mistral is the poster child of sovereignty. The last remaining hope for Europe when it comes to frontier model providers.

I sat down with @MistralAI CEO, @arthurmensch to debunk the hype from reality and ask the uncomfortable questions. My notes from the discussion below.

1. Why Energy Is Not the Ultimate Cost That Matters

Energy makes up around 10% of the total cost of ownership of compute, so it is not where most optimization can happen. The cost of energy is not the one thing that matters in the economics of a project.

Love to hear your thoughts on this @alanchanguk @ChaseLochmiller @ZachBDell

2. What Would Mistral Do Differently If They Were Totally Resource-Unconstrained?

Mistral would build much more capacity, with capital as the main bottleneck. Customers are running out of compute, and once one use case scales they need thousands of GPUs rather than eight. Europe does not have enough compute, so Mistral is putting equity to work to build capacity ahead of demand.

Love to hear your thoughts on this, if you were resource unconstrained today, what would you do differently @alexmashrabov @bavaria_kush

3. How the Inference Market Behaves Very Much Like a Commodity Market

On-demand inference behaves like a high-margin commodity market where pricing matters a lot and demand comes from non-committed customers. Mature customers need service level agreements, reserved physical capacity and guarantees on latency and generation speed. The more precisely they describe the shape of their demand, the better Mistral can price it.

What does no one see about the inference market that everyone should see @tuhinone @neilmovva @lqiao

4. Models Have Gotten So Strong They Are Being Treated as Defense Systems

Models are now strong enough to carry out cyberattacks, and the US began banning them outside the country in May. China is also looking at restricting exports beyond a certain threshold. As with any dual-use technology, customers now want security of supply on both infrastructure and model IP.

What does no one see about the future of security that everyone should see @zeyu1337 @nikesharora @pilvar222

5. Will We End Up With a Model Landscape That Has Just Two to Three Providers?

If every company relies on two or three centralized AI providers, those providers gain enormous leverage. They will use the data their systems produce to build better systems and go after their customers' business, an end game Arthur sees as priced in today.

Most enterprise problems are not well defined, and ambiguous objectives with humans in the loop cannot be solved through self-improving loops. They only get solved by deploying models that interact with people, which is why Mistral uses FDEs to define problems better.

7. Why You Can Go Public in Europe and Negativity Around European Stock Markets Is BS

I underestimated Bitcoin’s risk to quantum.

Initially, it seemed like a problem that was still far away. Surely the smart people in the Bitcoin community would figure it out before it became urgent.

But after spending more time researching it, it became clear that the challenge is more complicated. 

We’re now faced with some difficult questions:

- Which PQ signature scheme should Bitcoin adopt?
- How should users migrate?
- What happens to lost or dormant coins?
- How does the network reach agreement on an upgrade?

Bitcoin has no company or foundation that can mandate an upgrade. That decentralization is one of its greatest strengths, but it also makes a coordinated migration difficult. 

Choosing an approach, building it, reaching consensus, and migrating users could take years. 

So what are we doing about it?

At Stacks Labs, we’ve formed an R&D team focused on three initial priorities:

1. Make Stacks quantum-resistant
2. Study how to protect the Bitcoin backing sBTC
3. Contribute research and proposals that can support Bitcoin’s transition to PQ

As a first step, we completed an sBTC transfer on Stacks mainnet using Lamport signatures, a hash-based signature verified in Clarity.

This is an early PoC. We’re still evaluating potential signature schemes and what a broader transition would require. We’ll share more about this research and the broader Stacks quantum roadmap soon.

While we expected some volatility before the Nov unlock, we are also surprised by the extent of it. We have been looking into it and here is the summary:

- There was a hack involving one of the earliest LPs’ wallets on Oct. 22. Roughly 12M HUMA earned from airdrops in the hacked wallets was dumped on the market.

- Various inquiries were sent to contracted market makers (public and regulated companies) about the recent volatility, and based on the information shared with us so far, we don’t have a reason to believe any foul play.

- Open interest across venues rose from ~620M to ~1.1B HUMA between Nov 2 and Nov 7, funding rate has been negative since Nov 4, and perp volume has been running 7–10× spot. The market activities seem to be concentrated on the perps side.

What we can attest:

- Huma Foundation or any of its affiliated entities have not engaged in any HUMA trades (spot, perps, options, or OTCs) in the past 3 months, and have no plans to sell any tokens during the upcoming unlock window.

- Huma Foundation has been providing DEX liquidity for HUMA since TGE. It hasn’t changed its setup for the past year.

- Huma has a clear policy for its employees not to actively trade HUMA.

While we cannot control the market, the team is pushing hard to scale one of the leading RWA protocols in the entire ecosystem. With $387M of market cap, PST is the leading credit asset on Solana, but it is still a drop in the ocean compared to what PayFi can be. We have so much more to build!

As communicated below, we will host an AMA around Nov. 19-20. Look forward to seeing you then.

On $HUMA and the Nov 26 unlock

I’ve seen the concerns in Discord and on X about $HUMA, and I want to address them directly.

What’s happening. In April, our investors and team voluntarily pushed back the first token unlock by six months. That unlock begins on Nov 26. Big unlocks almost always draw heavy positioning ahead of time, and that’s what we’re seeing now, on top of a broad sell-off in BTC and equities.

What’s not changing: the business. Huma just passed $20B in total transaction volume. Total Active Liquidity (TAL) has grown 3x this year to ~$400M.

Setting the record straight on the unlock. Some people believe Nov 26 releases everything held back over the past six months. It doesn’t. We moved the entire team and investor schedule back six months, so nothing has built up. On Nov 26, only 1/12 of those allocations unlocks:

Team: ~160.8M HUMA (1.6% of total supply)
Investors: ~171.7M HUMA (1.7%)
Total: ~332.5M HUMA (3.3%)

The regular quarterly ecosystem (~146.1M) and foundation (~126.25M) unlocks continue as in previous quarters.

An orderly unlock. We’re setting up a coordinated OTC program for unlocked tokens, integrated with Magna and Anchorage, so any selling happens in an orderly way rather than all at once on the open market.

Governance goes live. As we committed in April, HUMA Governance launches by Nov 26. HUMA holders will be able to vote on protocol decisions, and we’ll share the details in the coming weeks.

Let’s talk. After we’re back from Solana Breakpoint, we’ll host a community call around Nov 19–20 to answer your questions directly.

Unlocks come and go; the mission doesn’t. We’re building the PayFi network for the long run, and we’re proud to lead this movement with you. Thank you for building with us.

This is the conversation that made me even more bullish on $SUI.

Somewhere in this conversation Evan Cheng and I started joking about home robots. One day you come home, he said, and it's not cleaning your house:  "it's cleaning OUT your house. And walking away with everything."

We were laughing. Then he added: "If you really think about it, it's entirely possible." And that's basically the whole episode.

@evanweb3 built developer tools at Apple and Meta before founding Mysten Labs, the company behind @suinetwork. We recorded in Singapore, where I was speaking at SUI Basecamp, and honestly, this became one of those conversations where I walked in with questions about stablecoins and walked out rethinking how the internet works.

His core point, the one I keep replaying:

"The web is built for humans. You cannot retrofit it to handle agents."

Everything online assumes a human on the other end, identity, trust, the fact that you can sue someone. Agents break all of it. His example hit home because I told him I get phishing mails daily that even make ME hesitate (and I confessed to my 50,000 unread emails, which he graciously ignored). Now imagine your agent reading those mails with full access to your accounts. His words: "Email is the biggest freaking attack vector... such a legacy protocol."

And his most honest line, about how this plays out:

"Disaster will happen. That's part of the progress."

That’s already what’s happening in the world nowadays. PHP websites aren’t safe anymore, even freezers and fridges are being hacked. Our infrastructure needs to be updated, and that’s why this episode and SUI became so important.

🚨 JUST IN: TensorFold 1.2.7 makes long Qwen3.8 27B chats near instant 👏

I tested locally on a 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini with Qwen3.8 27B:

- Context with earlier reasoning steps dropped (common behaviour in chat apps)
- Previous version (1.2.6): follow-up questions would reprocess 24K tokens and take 76.8 s until the answer started streaming
- New version (1.2.7): follow-up questions reuse ~34K cached tokens and start streaming in 0.34 to 1.19 s (answers are still byte identical!)
- Context including reasoning steps (chat apps that preserve reasoning steps)
- Previous version (1.2.6): later questions took 1.35 to 4.04 s until the answer started streaming
- New version (1.2.7): later questions start streaming in 0.26 s

Nice improvement on TTFT, and decode speed is up a tad as well (same output on the deterministic runs):
- Chat without DFlash2: 17.06 --> 17.39 tok/s
- Chat with DFlash2: 56.22 --> 57.90 tok/s (3.3x faster than without DFlash2)
- Code with DFlash2: 93.79 --> 98.90 tok/s (5.7x faster than without DFlash2)

Incredible work @ashxhart and the rest of the community! 

Long context chats on a 27B model on your desk is already super impressive, having it be near instant and owning the whole stack makes it even nicer 🙌

text:
今天美股和 bitcoin:native 的上涨很有可能是 CoreWeave 财报的原因。CoreWeave 在美东周二收盘后公布三季度财报，营收 36.61 亿美元，比去年同期的 13.65 亿美元翻了一倍多，全年收入指引从 120 亿到 130 亿美元上调到 130 亿到 133 亿美元，收入积压约 1,325 亿美元。而且 2027 年剩下的算力已经被超额预订了大约 10 倍。

前面一段时间市场最担心的就是 AI 基础设施靠借钱扩建，需求一旦放慢就还不上。CoreWeave 这份财报给了市场一份定心丸，公司还预计未来三个月会收到约 90 亿美元的客户预付款和押金，扩建不用完全靠借钱。虽然当季仍然净亏损 7.09 亿美元，利息支出也有 8.46 亿美元，但投资者至少看到了收入在跟上投入。

所以周三 CoreWeave 收涨约 24.7%，费城半导体指数涨约 5.7%，美光涨约 11.9%，Sandisk 涨约 13.7%，AMD 涨约 7.3%，连跌两天的英伟达也反弹了约 2.9%。纳指收涨约 1.6%，标普 500 涨约 1.3%，道指涨约 0.5%。而周二 CPI 高于预期，十年期美债收益率一度又回到 5% 以上，市场已经开始押注下个月加息，这种情况下科技股还能反弹，财报的作用就更明显了。

Bitcoin 仍然和科技股保持一定的关联度，虽然 CoreWeave 财报后并没有第一时间受到影响，但晚上美股开盘后科技股和 AI 带头上涨也给 bitcoin:native 的上涨带来了动力，可以看到 BTC 的上涨和美股开盘几乎是同步的。

text:
Still a super underrated aspect of @CurveFinance's lending platform (LlamaLend).

On any other crypto lending platform, if the value of your non-stablecoin collateral drops enough because of a market dip, your position gets liquidated- and there is no coming back from that. Game over.

On LlamaLend, your position can enter a "soft liquidation" phase, which auto-converts portions of your otherwise volatile collateral into $crvUSD as price moves against you, protecting the value of your collateral and therefore your borrowed position to avoid a "hard" liquidation. As the market recovers, it converts that $crvUSD BACK into the original asset, (essentially buying back your original collateral with the accumulated $crvUSD) so that your borrowed position can literally AVOID liquidation during unexpected market dips.

Quoted tweet below is a nice demonstration of this feature in action 👇

Our teams put Gemini 4 Carbon to work on a major security challenge: mathematically proving the code underlying the Signal protocol.

Using AlphaProof Code, @GoogleDeepMind researchers guided agents to verify the protocol down to compiled device code, closing the gap where real bugs hide. The result:

- Gemini 4 Carbon generated over 6M lines of machine-checked Lean proofs
- years of expert manual verification compressed to just weeks
~1% of the codebase required human review (Lean automatically checked the rest)

This is helping unlock scalable formal verification for building secure software, laying the groundwork to fundamentally shift the advantage to defenders. We’re open sourcing the results for the security community.

text:
两届全美投资冠军Mark的投资精华干货：

1. 地基只有一条：亏损绝不超过8% （Cut lost）

他立下这条纪律后，5年年均220%。28年，一次没破。所有交易带硬止损，做空也一样。

2. 三条财富规则 （Princinple）

不在底部买入（右侧交易）
别总是卖得太早 （Let profits fly）
从不持有、更不加仓亏损股

3. 他错得比对得多 （赔率>胜率）

胜率长期不到一半，照样建起九位数身家。投资不是预测，是赔率和纪律。

4. Bell Curve Thinking

每笔交易只问一句：如果这笔交易做1000次，我赚不赚钱？上行空间至少是止损的2到3倍，才出手。

5. 只买突破，不买便宜

买领涨股从扎实底部的枢轴点突破，要的是对的价格，不是最低的价格。加仓只能在底部形态内、穿过新的枢轴点时加。最好的形态如果依旧没机会，就去持有现金，绝不降格去买差的。（右侧）

6. 让利润变亏损，是交易头号大罪

盈利后把止损移到保本，用部分止盈换余仓免费持有。财报前没有利润垫，坚决不持仓过夜。

7. 仓位由市场挣得，不是自己定的

没有放量跟进，就不进攻。派发在累积、广度在恶化，就收紧止损、降低仓位。止损比情绪可靠。

8. 最难的不是技术，是ego

去赌场是为了刺激，但是来市场需要纪律。别把交易过度复杂化。

只做最强的那只，板块龙头的主升段

交易归交易，定投归定投，定投照计划买，不看涨跌

🚨Oregon, here are the findings of the Nov 3rd SEL pull & some initial anomalies that stuck out. 

1⃣Oregon has more registrations than adults (109%)

The voter file has 3.8 million registrations against about 3.48 million adults (18+), using PSU's 2025 estimate. 

Counting only "active" voters it's 89%, which is normal, so the excess may be the "inactive" records Judicial Watch sued over. 

Klamath & Columbia County are near 120%

Josephine County is at 119%. 

Wallowa is the one county with more "active" voters than adults, by about 224.

2⃣Non-residential addresses

1,090 Active voters list 650 NW Irving St in Portland as home. That's a homeless resource center that offers mail service. 

Another 256 list the Portland Rescue Mission

93 list JOIN's day center. 

3⃣ 19 people died but were listed as "active" voters! 

Oregon mails a ballot to every 'active' voter. 

4⃣VERY old voters.

Oregon has two active voters who are 111!

Born in 1915 or 1916 who voted in 2024 & in the May 2026 primary.

Another in Lincoln County & one in Yamhill. 

Overall, 85 records would be 110 or older, mostly classified as "inactive" 

3,342 are 100 or older.

Multiple SI also claim it's very odd especially as the 2020 Census counted only 969 Oregonians aged 100 or older. Even with steady growth, that should only be around 1,100.

3,342 is 3X way too many. 

5⃣Duplicate voters

There are 70 possible duplicate voters in the same county. 

These are pairs with the same first, middle, and last name and birth year, both "active" and both voting in 2024 (Multnomah 19, Clackamas 13, Washington 9). They could be twins or typos. 
If both records in a pair vote again on Nov 3, that's a real red flag. 

369 Polk County Active voters have a registration date of 11-11-1111. That's a placeholder date, a sign of sloppy data rather than fraud, but it means the county is not listing when they actually registered.

2,545 Active voters have out-of-state mailing addresses, mostly UO students in Lane County. 

Spikes in registrations match the deadline, the party switches are ordinary, and almost no PO boxes are used as home addresses.

The Nov 3 voting history will be available either December or January and should settle who of the above actually voted.

Anthropic / frontier lab investment case comes down to how you reconcile the following, or why you think one or several of these trends will change:

(1) deflation of intelligence: constant ECI price per token or task has been declining 5-10x per year
(2) hedonic price gradient of intelligence: this has also been declining: a year ago, 10 pts of ECI got you 4-9x higher price per token-per task, today it’s 3-4x 
(3) 1 & 2 suggest you need 10-20 ECI pts per year to offset underlying deflation with higher intelligence
(4) scaling laws / R&D diminishing returns (this chart from @ramez) suggest the last ~20 pts of ECI costs ~$30 bn & the next will cost ~$60bn. i.e., to maintain price, R&D needs to be as much as ~$60bn in NTM and ~$120bn in the 12 mos after that, etc
(5) meanwhile, to achieve its margin targets, Anthropic needs to decrease compute as % of sales over time, so it needs volume growth / adoption to be fast enough so the business doesn’t get caught between the jaws of the deflationary forces of (1) + (2) and the inflationary forces of (4)

these can be reconciled in ways that work out for the frontier labs (eg, regulation slows open model progress and deflation slows or hedonic gradient ramps back up; volume growth is so strong and accelerating that it more than offsets the jaws of deflationary pricing / inflationary R&D), but this is the bet imo
