text:
While zcash:native has become one of the most popular assets of the cycle, there has been very little coverage of its actual market structure or onchain flows. We’d like to fix that by providing more ZEC coverage going forward.

We’ll start with a breakdown of the selloff over the last 48 hours or so.

ZEC fell 16% in two hours on 11/10/2026, from $1,193 to $1,001. In the hour before the break, the only steady seller was on Coinbase’s spot book, where takers sold a net 3.0K ZEC from 14:30 UTC while perp traders on Binance, OKX, and Hyperliquid were still net buyers. 

The break itself began at 15:29:58 UTC, when a single Hyperliquid account that had built a 12.5K ZEC long in the hour after CPI closed the entire position at market in two seconds, just as BTC was rolling over. Over the next ninety minutes perps did most of the damage, with net taker selling of 74K ZEC on Binance, 42K on OKX, 31K on Hyperliquid, and 13K on Bybit, against roughly 27K across all spot venues, about half of it on Coinbase.

Hyperliquid’s trade-level data also shows what kind of selling it was. Between 14:30 and 17:00 UTC, takers closing longs (109K ZEC) outweighed takers opening shorts (50K) by more than two to one, and forced liquidations came to only 6.9K ZEC, so this was longs heading for the exit rather than a liquidation cascade or a wave of new shorts.

To see where that supply came from, we traced every large deposit into Coinbase and Coinbase Prime back to the origin of the coins. Only about 12K ZEC arrived across 11/09 and 11/10, which is less than what was sold on Coinbase during the drop, so most of the selling came from inventory that was already sitting on the venue. Of what arrived the day before, the largest piece was a single 3,058 zcash:native deposit routed through a multisig created two hours earlier, 1.3K had just been withdrawn from Hyperliquid, 0.8K came over from other exchanges, and 2.4K was earlier Coinbase withdrawals coming straight back. Almost none of it was unshielded, none of it was miner supply, and none of it was old coins.

Despite the front page ad of the WSJ, the Grayscale ETF holders were not net sellers either. ZCSH traded 2.46M shares on the day and closed at a small premium, it recorded zero creations or redemptions, and the 1,861 ZEC that settled into Coinbase Prime that morning was delivery on Monday’s redemption. 

The larger onchain move came after the drop. By 18:00 UTC on 11/11, another 16.3K ZEC had been deposited to Coinbase, and 9.8K of it came from three wallets that withdrew from Coinbase Prime in November and December 2025 and had not moved since. 

Those wallets still hold roughly 19K ZEC, and Binance took in a further 8.6K of large deposits over the same hours, so the supply reaching exchanges has grown since the selloff rather than faded

text: “This is the first time in a long time (since the merge/staking/1559) that the network devs and the asset holders can rally on something together. pqai27 is good for Ethereum and good for ETH. “
author: binji_x
quoted_text:
Some thoughts on this:

> Its time to be ambitious again. 
> The Merge 2.0 energy. 

> A system can be attacked in two ways: through its code, or through the people and keys that control it. Becoming post-quantum and post-AI hardens the code while Ethereum's decentralization has already hardened the people side, the side that literally can't be bolted on later. Ethereum has a structural advantage here compared to most other networks that hold value (not just other blockchains!) 

> As AI-assisted attacks make the web less safe, most systems will centralize further. Ethereum will not. It is a bet that you can stay safe in that world without handing anyone else the keys, a place where you can stay safe while still being free.

> This is the first time in a long time (since the merge/staking/1559) that the network devs and the asset holders can rally on something together. pqai27 is good for Ethereum and good for ETH. 

--- 

Wait, a quick ELI15 on pq and pai before we continue: 

What does "post-quantum" mean? 

Future quantum computers could break some of the cryptography that most of the internet relies on today, including blockchains. PQ/Post-quantum means switching to cryptography that holds up against them. The US government moved its target to 2030, and Google is aiming for 2029. This Ethlabs proposal for Ethereum, is trying to get there in 2027. 

What does "post-AI" mean?

 AI is getting very good at two things that matter for security.  

1. Maths. AI is solving long-standing open maths problems by the hundreds, and the security of our cryptography is itself an open maths problem. A break is unlikely, but unlike quantum, nobody can put a date on it. 

2. Bugs. AI now finds software vulnerabilities at scale. OpenAI's internal model found and patched ~1000 in Linux alone. Every piece of software is vulnerable to this scrutiny, even from attackers. 

Post-AI means Ethereum can hold up against both. Its planned cryptography is built on hash functions, which rely on as few assumptions as possible, so there's as little as possible for AI (or quantum) to break. And its clients get hardened against AI bug hunters through formal verification (mathematically proving the code does what it should) and its already robust client diversity (Ethereum runs on several independent clients, so a bug in one need not take the network down).

ok now back to the takes..
 
---

> Ethereum is already where the world trusts onchain value most, it has 11 years without downtime, 46% of all stablecoins, and nearly half of all tokenized assets. pqai27 further future-proofs that trust for the decades ahead and extends it to many others that the network is yet to meet.

> BEWARE: You will get many teams claiming to be PQ with centralized setups that sufficient amounts of blackmail can rug (social risk is real! see: Binance hack). 

> Ethereum will be PQ while remaining decentralized, aka there is no one you can blackmail to shut it down. Ethereum is special in this way.

> Ethereum should not just survive the AI age, it should become one of the foundations that makes the AI age safe to live in. 

> We might finally have a narrative that feels like we can all band together again, this is a perfect storm with SOV. 

Ok its 3am here, more tomorrow.

We think pqai27, as we call it, can be a catalyst for Ethereum protocol development to align behind ambitious goals and continue to improve the security of our network, so that Ethereum’s apps and users may continue to enjoy its value.

In short: We think Ethereum should double down on its unique value proposition of being the most secure place to issue, hold and use the world’s assets, and achieve its post-quantum and post-AI transition over the next year.

This comes on the heels of massive, AI-accelerated progress behind the pieces required to move forward with this transition. Getting there will take work, and we at Ethlabs are committed to seeing it through.

There are no free lunches. Reprioritising post-quantum and post-AI security means deprioritising proposals that are dear to us, such as quick slots. The silver lining is that the work behind pq continues to add utility to the network, such as with new, pq-ready accounts leveraging Frame transactions.

> As AI-assisted attacks make the web less safe, most systems will centralize further. Ethereum will not. It is a bet that you can stay safe in that world without handing anyone else the keys, a place where you can stay safe while still being free.

> This is the first time in a long time (since the merge/staking/1559) that the network devs and the asset holders can rally on something together. pqai27 is good for Ethereum and good for ETH. 

--- 

Wait, a quick ELI15 on pq and pai before we continue: 

What does "post-quantum" mean? 

Future quantum computers could break some of the cryptography that most of the internet relies on today, including blockchains. PQ/Post-quantum means switching to cryptography that holds up against them. The US government moved its target to 2030, and Google is aiming for 2029. This Ethlabs proposal for Ethereum, is trying to get there in 2027. 

What does "post-AI" mean?

 AI is getting very good at two things that matter for security.  

1. Maths. AI is solving long-standing open maths problems by the hundreds, and the security of our cryptography is itself an open maths problem. A break is unlikely, but unlike quantum, nobody can put a date on it. 

2. Bugs. AI now finds software vulnerabilities at scale. OpenAI's internal model found and patched ~1000 in Linux alone. Every piece of software is vulnerable to this scrutiny, even from attackers. 

Post-AI means Ethereum can hold up against both. Its planned cryptography is built on hash functions, which rely on as few assumptions as possible, so there's as little as possible for AI (or quantum) to break. And its clients get hardened against AI bug hunters through formal verification (mathematically proving the code does what it should) and its already robust client diversity (Ethereum runs on several independent clients, so a bug in one need not take the network down).

ok now back to the takes..
 
---

> Ethereum is already where the world trusts onchain value most, it has 11 years without downtime, 46% of all stablecoins, and nearly half of all tokenized assets. pqai27 further future-proofs that trust for the decades ahead and extends it to many others that the network is yet to meet.

> BEWARE: You will get many teams claiming to be PQ with centralized setups that sufficient amounts of blackmail can rug (social risk is real! see: Binance hack). 

> Ethereum will be PQ while remaining decentralized, aka there is no one you can blackmail to shut it down. Ethereum is special in this way.

> Ethereum should not just survive the AI age, it should become one of the foundations that makes the AI age safe to live in. 

> We might finally have a narrative that feels like we can all band together again, this is a perfect storm with SOV.

text:
OKXICE将于11月23日推出代币化证券交易平台，借此聊聊代币化进程中的阻力以及OKXICE为什么要这么做？10月初okx与ice的合资公司宣布采用在SEC创新豁免机制下推出代币化交易平台，之后看到不少美股的知名公司反对，很多人就说代币化趋势要搁浅了。其实并不是这样，聊聊我的理解。

OKXICE选择的SEC美国交易场所豁免路径，这种机制明确赋予发行公司反对权。它如果要采用这套方案，那么收到一些美股公司的反对也不奇怪。其实很多反对的美股上市公司并不是完全反对代币化进程，只是有一些他们不能理解的分歧在里面。

已经公开解释过的公司中，AAOI的说法很有代表性：不清楚这种安排会怎样影响股价、流动性和波动率；担心投资者误以为公司参与或认可该产品；没有看到足够明确、能够抵消这些不确定性的公司或股东利益。
而摩根大通的表态则更克制：仍然看好代币化潜力，但现阶段不参与这个场所，继续评估其他机会

其实可以理解，代币化平台获得的收益比较直接，股票发行公司的收益要绕一层才能兑现。平台可以扩大交易品种、获得客户与交易收入；
上市公司则需要证明，更广泛的交易入口确实改善了投资者覆盖、流动性或资本成本。在早期这些公司看不到这种优势也可以理解。

那为什么OKXICE还要选择“创新豁免”这条路径。我理解是因为它们想获得的业务能力，比“为境外用户提供美股价格敞口”更广。ICE在3月宣布与OKX建立战略关系时，已经把方向说得比较清楚：结合OKX的全球客户渠道、区块链基础设施，以及ICE的市场技术与机构网络，并探索向美国客户提供相关市场服务。

核心其实是争取美国市场里的链上交易入口。
如果主要目标只是做境外股票挂钩产品，确实可以考虑其他法律结构。例如coinbase和robinhood现在的模式、完全不需要股票发行公司是否同意、直接就推出了把股票代币化、但是他们两家的代币化只能面向非美用户推出。

如Robinhood，当前Robinhood Chain产品文件明确写明，Stock Tokens是由Robinhood Assets（Jersey）Limited发行的代币化债务证券，提供底层股票的经济敞口，但不赋予投资者对底层股票发行人的法律或受益权利；产品也不得向美国人士销售

Coinbase的情况更接近第三方托管权益结构。其官方介绍称，代币由真实股份一比一支持，通过受监管托管与信托安排持有，并在Base上流通；发行采用Regulation S安排，不向美国人士开放。

看到了么？robinhood和coinbase现在的代币化产品都不向美国用户开放。而OKXICE想要的恰恰是直接切入美国本土，向美国境内的零售与机构客户提供代币化产品，而这是另一个需要独立解决的市场。

其实这也是监管与行业之间公开争论的问题。之前Coinbase就向SEC提出过类似的质疑：既然传统证券转让、DTCC代币化等安排不要求发行公司逐一批准，为什么新的链上交易路径要增加发行公司否决权？

站在SEC的角度，之前其主席Atkins也明确表态这项临时豁免的定位是为通向后续长期规则的过渡安排，那意味着现在采用这种机制虽然当下会面临一些阻力、但是一旦SEC推出了长期规则那么就会自动获得在未来长期规则下的优先权。所以如果终点是美国境内的链上股票市场，那么通知发行公司是OKXICE选择这条路径必须支付的制度成本。

从产业发展看，这轮反对对美国股票AMM路线构成了实际阻力，但都是产业趋势发展过程中的阶段性阻力，并不会让RWA代币化趋势。

当下以及未来一段时间都将是几种路径继续并行：
1）境外产品先满足全球投资者的访问和组合需求，如robinhood和coinbase模式；
2）DTC等机构推进既有证券权益的流转效率；
3）发行公司主导的产品改善股东服务；
4）OKXICE正在推动的模式， TSV验证链上股票交易能否在保护投资者的同时获得足够流动性、那么未来也会有越来越多的美股上市公司会拥抱这种趋势。

text:
I was wrong about agent sandboxes.

In my article I said pattern 1, where the agent runs on your infra and only calls a sandbox for tools, doesn't work at scale. I moved everything to pattern 2 and put the whole agent inside a VM.

At the time that made sense but today I'd pick pattern 1.

For your own personal agent, a coding agent, or a small project, isolating the whole agent in a VM is still a great default. I would keep doing it.

At real multi-tenant scale it falls apart.

There will be more agents than humans. Every human gets one computer. Giving every agent its own VM running 24/7 means billions of CPU-hungry machines, and we're already short on compute.

Most of what an agent does doesn't need a machine at all. It thinks, calls APIs, reads pages, and waits. Nobody needs a 4 CPU VM sitting idle so an agent can run a simple JS script once an hour.

What I'd build now:
> the agent loop runs on shared infra that scales
> it gets a sandbox only when it has to run untrusted code
> sandboxes spin up in seconds and die right after
> zero state on the machine, everything lives outside it

VMs are a tool the agent calls, but they shouldn't be where it lives.

text:
Haïti, Bukele dicte le tempo

Nayib Bukele est en vedette. Dans les rues de Port-au-Prince et dans des villes de province, on chante son nom. Des foules dansent en évoquant son action. C’est assez rare pour un engouement qui ne date que de quelques semaines. 

« Bukele ap mete nou sou 'compas' ». La phrase est sortie spontanément de la bouche d’une jeune sexagénaire, mardi 10 novembre 2026. 

La dame a repris, souvenir ancien, une expression à la mode au début des années 80, popularisée par Antoine Rossiny Jean-Baptiste dit Ti Manno, chanteur du DP Express, dans l’une des chansons gravées sur le fameux album David. 

Pendant des mois, l’expression « Sou compas » a été mise à toutes les sauces. La graphie créole du compas, nom de la musique dansante la plus populaire en Haïti, n’était pas encore fixée.

Oui. Le président Nayib Bukele du Salvador met tous les Haïtiens sou konpa. Il dicte le tempo à coups de tweets, de messages en créole postés sur ses réseaux sociaux.

Mais la phrase « Bukele ap mete nou sou compas » a été particulièrement inspirée par la vidéo de l’attaque menée par hélicoptère contre le domicile du chef de gang Lanmò San jou, postée mardi 10 novembre 2026. 

La vidéo de quelques secondes est spectaculaire, saisissante et inimaginable après des années de faiblesse, de tergiversations et d’échecs des forces de l’ordre haïtiennes et des missions de l’ONU.

Des hélicoptères d’attaque, on en voit sillonner le ciel de Port-au-Prince depuis des mois. On en avait déjà vu en action contre les groupes criminels, mais jusqu’à présent on ignorait les cibles. 

Cette fois, l’attaque a été annoncée et l’assaut filmé, du décollage à l’impact, jusqu’à la course effrénée des bandits qui cherchaient à échapper au déluge de feu venu du ciel.

Le président Nayib Bukele a scénarisé son opération. Il l’a revendiquée. Il en a dévoilé les images. Du jamais vu depuis le 1er juin 2021 et l’essor des gangs en Haïti.

« Bukele ap mete nou sou compas » s’adresse à ceux qui attendent de nouvelles annonces comme à ceux qui craignent la foudre que pourrait faire tomber la force de plus de deux mille hommes que le Salvador a déployés en Haïti après la disparition de quatre techniciens, le 18 octobre 2026, dans la région de Santo.

La vidéo diffusée mardi 10 novembre, même si l’on ignore si elle a été filmée le même jour, atteste au moins que l’assaut a bien eu lieu. Elle vient aussi répondre aux rumeurs d’une suspension des interventions, alors que circulent des informations faisant état de dissensions entre les alliés de la cause d’Haïti dans la lutte contre l’emprise des gangs 

Les États-Unis, la République dominicaine, la FRG, les Nations Unies, les forces de sécurité haïtiennes, la task force, les Salvadoriens et le gouvernement haïtien ont intérêt à coopérer et à planifier leurs interventions afin de maintenir l’élan et de coordonner leurs actions. Pour éviter les bavures et les atteintes aux droits humains, la coordination est primordiale.

Pour ne pas casser la dynamique en heurtant les sensibilités des partenaires traditionnels, il faut une direction claire des actions à venir.

Bukele mete nou sou konpa et sa musique remplace la tragique symphonie de la violence aveugle et de la peur. Pour le moment.

Frantz Duval

text:
🚨 JUST IN: TensorFold 1.2.7 makes long Qwen3.8 27B chats near instant 👏

I tested locally on a 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini with Qwen3.8 27B:

- Context with earlier reasoning steps dropped (common behaviour in chat apps)
- Previous version (1.2.6): follow-up questions would reprocess 24K tokens and take 76.8 s until the answer started streaming
- New version (1.2.7): follow-up questions reuse ~34K cached tokens and start streaming in 0.34 to 1.19 s (answers are still byte identical!)
- Context including reasoning steps (chat apps that preserve reasoning steps)
- Previous version (1.2.6): later questions took 1.35 to 4.04 s until the answer started streaming
- New version (1.2.7): later questions start streaming in 0.26 s

Nice improvement on TTFT, and decode speed is up a tad as well (same output on the deterministic runs):
- Chat without DFlash2: 17.06 --> 17.39 tok/s
- Chat with DFlash2: 56.22 --> 57.90 tok/s (3.3x faster than without DFlash2)
- Code with DFlash2: 93.79 --> 98.90 tok/s (5.7x faster than without DFlash2)

Incredible work @ashxhart and the rest of the community! 

Long context chats on a 27B model on your desk is already super impressive, having it be near instant and owning the whole stack makes it even nicer 🙌

总结一下我们的核心观点：

我们认为纯机器人模型公司显然已经进入商品化的阶段，这也意味着纯模型实验室高估值已经到达了拐点。它们要么通过自己掌握硬件来垂直整合整个技术栈，要么彻底转向前线部署模式，把部署环节握在自己手里。

Fable 5.2 和 Astra 6 的出现，基本意味着通用 LLM 已经可以取代所谓的 system 2；而当这些模型用来写代码去控制机器时，还能继续下沉到 system 1，接管传统机器人栈里的动作规划环节。只要推理长度和所需算力能随时间持续优化，专注于 pre-training 的纯 VLA 实验室追逐通用机器人智能，最终会被彻底淘汰。

有意思的是，我们认为价值最终会沉淀到部署层。从软件的角度看，也就是市场所说的 system 0。而其中的关键在于：持续收集后训练数据，会实质性地提升软件对硬件的控制能力，也让部署本身变得更高效、更好。

至于硬件，我们的观点比较反直觉的是，它反而会成为瓶颈。虽然这一层的利润率大概率会被竞争压低，但这不等于硬件没有价值。公司必须自己掌握硬件，才能完全释放软件的能力。这意味着要自研、自产硬件，确保后训练所优化的一切，都能真正落到硬件层上。

text:
Fascinating - $GOOG TPU has the best architecture for AI compute, and “there aren’t enough TPUs,”

$AVGO $ANT

“Today I would argue that probably the best architecture is the Google TPU architecture, because it is literally thought of as a single system. And I think an NVIDIA-style architecture is migrating in the direction of where the TPU architecture is, but it still has a few pieces that you can kind of swap out. And then you have everybody else — like, you know, I'm going to take a Cerebras chip and throw an Arista switch on top of it, and all that good stuff. At least in today's world, those systems have inefficiencies because they're not constructed as a system — they're more of a patchwork.

I think the industry will evolve, but today, people that can think of the whole thing as a single system and optimize the architecture through that have a competitive advantage.

If you look at how Google does this, with these toroidal pass-through optical MEMS switches — it's literally like the whole data center is the minimum unit. But my sense is that's where NVIDIA wants to go also. Actually, the two dominant providers are all going to that systems approach, versus — I mean, even the smaller startups are heading that direction.

Right now Jensen's king of the hill, incredibly dominant, right? Google TPU very successful, currently mostly sold by Google — it's expected to change. But not enough TPUs.”

We think pqai27, as we call it, can be a catalyst for Ethereum protocol development to align behind ambitious goals and continue to improve the security of our network, so that Ethereum’s apps and users may continue to enjoy its value.

In short: We think Ethereum should double down on its unique value proposition of being the most secure place to issue, hold and use the world’s assets, and achieve its post-quantum and post-AI transition over the next year.

This comes on the heels of massive, AI-accelerated progress behind the pieces required to move forward with this transition. Getting there will take work, and we at Ethlabs are committed to seeing it through.

There are no free lunches. Reprioritising post-quantum and post-AI security means deprioritising proposals that are dear to us, such as quick slots. The silver lining is that the work behind pq continues to add utility to the network, such as with new, pq-ready accounts leveraging Frame transactions.

author: coinbureau
quoted_text:
The most BEARISH signal for Bitcoin may come tonight.

At 11PM CET, MSCI may officially DELETE Strategy, $MSTR.

The world’s biggest corporate Bitcoin holder could lose its spot on the world’s top stock lists.

TRILLIONS of dollars from BIG investment funds automatically follow these lists.

If a stock is on the list, these funds must BUY it.
If it gets kicked off, they must SELL it.

MSCI’s new rules kick out companies that fail 4 of 5 tests showing they run a real business.

Strategy reportedly fails all 5.
Even Strategy itself expects to be removed.

If it happens, these funds will have to sell ~13 million $MSTR shares by Nov 30.

At Monday’s close of $121.07, that’s ~$1.6B in forced selling.

That’s ~60% of what the stock normally trades in a full day.

JPMorgan says the selling could reach -$2.8B, plus another -$8.8B if other big stock lists follow.

The stock has already fallen from $145.16 to $121.07 in just two weeks, a drop of ~17%.

This matters for Bitcoin because Strategy buys BTC by selling its own stock to investors.

A lower $MSTR price means less money for every share it sells.

And it gets WORSE.

Investors have always paid extra for $MSTR, valuing it above the Bitcoin it holds.

That "extra" is what lets Strategy sell new shares and turn the cash into more BTC.

In mid-October, it was down to just ~8%.

Once $MSTR is worth the same as its Bitcoin, selling new shares to buy more BTC stops making sense.

And if Strategy still needs cash to pay its bills, the next thing it can sell is its Bitcoin.

That’s 850,364 BTC, worth billions, sitting on the table.

From “never sell” to “need to sell.”

What a ride.

$500,000 USDC, sent straight to the wallets of our top 250 traders. No claim page. No forms. No wait. Every transfer is on-chain and listed on our site.

Last time we signed off with “This is the first one. It won’t be the last.” Everyone says that. We meant it.

The first drop was $127,500. This one is almost four times bigger. That’s $627,500 back to traders so far, from a platform most people still haven’t heard of.

Some people would like to keep it that way. While this one was going out, someone worked pretty hard to keep eyes off Float. We’re not naming names. We’d rather spend the energy building.

We get it, though. When a platform this small pays out almost seven figures, people start asking the big ones awkward questions.

You can pull eyes off an announcement, but you can’t pull a transaction off the chain. The wallets are public, the amounts are public, and anyone can check.

The airdrop got bigger for one reason: you traded more. Nobody on our team sat in a room and decided to be more generous this time. Some of the fees from every trade go into the trader vault, gets swapped to USDC, and goes back to the people who generated it. More volume, bigger vault, bigger airdrop. That’s the whole trick.

We built it that way on purpose. A reward that depends on a team’s mood can disappear when the mood changes. A reward that’s built into how the platform works keeps showing up.

So when people ask how we afford this, the answer is we don’t. It was never our money. You made it. We just send it back.

Everything else still holds. Every coin launches at a $20K market cap, so hoarding supply early costs real money. Holders get paid in real assets. Buybacks and burns keep running.

All of it points at one thing: coins worth holding. Organic communities that form because people actually believe in something, not because someone paid for a crowd. The kind of coin you can hold without checking the chart every five minutes.

To everyone who traded, launched, or held since the last drop: this one’s yours, you built it, trade by trade.

Two down. Plenty more to come.

text:
some thoughts on writing software in nov 2026: 

- it feels like magic
- the first 80% is 100x faster
- rewriting systems is also 100x faster
- opus 5.5 is very good at a lot of things
- "deep flow state" is much easier to reach
- almost anything can be built in typescript and rust
- building secure things is very, very hard

the optimization function is how to maximize agents working on goal with the fewest interruptions needed. some things that help: 

- know where to trust vs guide (and keep retesting)
- give them agency like "i'm going to bed, get this done"
- if there is a reward function, ask them to hillclimb
- the socratic method works wonders 
- skills and memories can often hinder
- asking agents to review themselves still helps 
- cowriting a plan/spec/invariants helps sometimes

managing your own psychology is equally important: 

- be a lot more ambitious about what you can achieve
- avoid dopamine traps / false signals of progress
- get good at parallelizing and context switching 

there are also some things that don't quite work fluidly yet, but will get unlocked in the very near future: 

- software factory or "find and fix the bugs"
- multiplayer agentic workflows 
- agents managing other agents for high level outcomes
- organizational memory

BREAKING: South African telecom provider Telkom calls for easing ownership rules blocking Starlink. 🇿🇦

Telkom, a major phone and internet provider partly owned by South Africa’s government, has urged telecom regulator ICASA to make its empowerment rules more flexible.

• Current rules require individual telecoms licensees to maintain at least 30% ownership by historically disadvantaged groups, a hurdle for Starlink’s entry.

• Telkom says the regulations go beyond national empowerment legislation, increase compliance costs and hinder competition.

• It warns that regulatory uncertainty may have discouraged investment in South Africa’s networks.

• It supports recognising investment in infrastructure, skills, local suppliers and research as ways to achieve empowerment goals.

• Any changes should apply equally to existing providers and newcomers, including Starlink.

text:
some thoughts on writing software in nov 2026: 

- it feels like magic
- the first 80% is 100x faster
- rewriting systems is also 100x faster
- opus 5.5 is very good at a lot of things
- "deep flow state" is much easier to reach
- almost anything can be built in typescript and rust
- building secure things is very, very hard

the optimization function is how to maximize agents working on goal with the fewest interruptions needed. some things that help: 

- know where to trust vs guide (and keep retesting)
- give them agency like "i'm going to bed, get this done"
- if there is a reward function, ask them to hillclimb
- the socratic method works wonders 
- skills and memories can often hinder
- asking agents to review themselves still helps 
- cowriting a plan/spec/invariants helps sometimes

managing your own psychology is equally important: 

- be a lot more ambitious about what you can achieve
- avoid dopamine traps / false signals of progress
- get good at parallelizing and context switching 

there are also some things that don't quite work fluidly yet, but will get unlocked in the very near future: 

- software factory or "find and fix the bugs"
- multiplayer agentic workflows 
- agents managing other agents for high level outcomes
- organizational memory

text:
Google 推出 Gemini Decisions API：不写回答只做判断，一次最多问 1000 个问题，输入每百万 Token 0.1 美元、输出不收钱

Google 今天在 Gemini API 里上线了 Decisions API，配套新模型 Gemini Decision 1。它不生成文字，只答题：给它一份输入和一组问题，它直接返回每道题的答案，外加一个“有多大把握”的置信度。

【它解决什么问题】

做 AI 应用时，很多调用其实只要一个判断：这条客服消息转给哪个组？这个问题交给便宜模型还是推理模型？这张图违不违规？以前只能让大模型写一段话，再从里面解析答案，慢，容易解析失败，还要为输出 Token 付钱。

Decisions API 只有三种题型：是非题，返回“是”的概率；单选题，2 到 255 个选项，返回选中项和每个选项的概率；打分题，按你写的档位打分。每个答案带 0 到 1 的置信度，代码可以设门槛，比如高于 0.7 自动执行，低于就转人工。官方说这些概率是校准过的，意思是模型说 90% 的时候，大约十次里真对九次，所以置信度能直接拿来当门槛。

Google 博客的例子：上传一张茶水间台面的照片，同时问三个问题。“有没有洒了的液体”答 0.95；“怎么处理”选“用抹布擦”，置信度 0.98；“脏乱程度按 0 到 2 打分”给 1.19，置信度 0.77。

【多快、多便宜】

一次请求的输入最多 256K Token，文字、JSON、图片、音频、视频、PDF 可以混着放，比如一段客服通话录音加账户信息。同一份输入上最多挂 1000 个问题，彼此互不影响。输入只计一次费，每多一个问题只多算这道题本身的字数。

Google 称输入在 1.6 万 Token 以内时，端到端延迟 150 到 250 毫秒，问 1 个和问 100 个问题耗时差不多；同一批评测下，比用 Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite 生成答案便宜近 5 倍。Gemini Notebook 已经用它给每个提问挑模型，日常问题延迟最多降了 40%。

【谁能用】

在 Google AI Studio 拿个 API Key 就能调，模型名 gemini-decision-1，走 v1beta 接口。有免费层，每分钟 200 次、每天 1 万次，免费层的数据会被 Google 用来改进产品，付费层不会。OpenRouter、LangChain、Vercel 等正在接入，Google Cloud 上的 Gemini 要稍后才支持。

不支持上下文缓存和 Batch API，同一份大文档反复问，每次都按全价算输入；不能直接传 YouTube 链接；问题本身只能写文字。

【跟 OpenAI 的同名产品比】

OpenAI 早一个月做了同样的东西，名字也叫 Decisions API：10 月 6 日出测试版，10 月 22 日正式开放，用 GPT-6 Luna，同样每百万输入 Token 0.1 美元、输出不收费。区别是 OpenAI 一次最多 400 个问题，只收文字、图片和 JSON，不收音视频和 PDF；但它支持缓存，重复输入能打折，还能直接塞进对话历史和工具调用记录。

创业公司 TypeSafe 的 Jev 1.14 也专做这类判断，在 OpenRouter 上每百万输入 Token 0.042 美元，只收文字和图片。

Google 博客附的对比表里，Gemini Decision 1 在 9 项测试中 7 项第一（其中音频、视频两项只有它和 Flash-Lite 参测），校准误差 0.025，GPT-6 Luna 是 0.072；网页操作和“该不该调用工具”两项输给了 Jev 1.14。7 项共同评测的总花费，Jev 最低，0.68 美元，Gemini Decision 1 是 0.88 美元，GPT-6 Luna 0.93 美元。以上跑分都是 Google 自己测的。

Google 博客：https://t.co/P5hlLj7fXN
官方文档：https://t.co/WphCUZv5oT
OpenAI Decisions API 文档：https://t.co/MGgS32OuNy

quoted_text:
黄仁勋的出轨曝光源于对英伟达的做空

今年5月我写了一篇关于 Culper Research 做空英伟达的详细解读，其中的第一条就阐述了 Megaspeed 和英伟达的关系，而且不仅仅是 Megaspeed 还有 Speedmatrix 和 Aivres 两家公司分别对应阿里和浪潮。

Speedmatrix 是 Megaspeed 马来西亚的全资子公司，曾把自己的一切抵押给一家新加坡公司 Apex Enterprise Solutions。而 Apex 的母公司就是阿里。

Speedmatrix 近两年进口中约 40 亿美元来自 Aivres Systems。Aivres 是英伟达 Elite OEM 计算机合作商，负责组装高端英伟达服务器。Aivres 的前身是 Inspur Systems，也就是浪潮体系。

也就是英伟达通过 Megaspeed 这个合作商将GPU 卖到了受到美国限制的中国，而英伟达一直到目前的财报中虽然没有中国市场的销售，但实际上已经有不少的芯片通过 Megaspeed 销售到了中国市场。

这次黄仁勋的出轨案件本身就源自于这起做空导致的，是 Culper Research 将这个信息公开，从而引发了如果美国商务部、司法部、新加坡、马来西亚的调查。

结果就是美国情报机构已评估 Alice Huang 可能在为中方收集信息，美国众议院相关委员会主席已要求黄仁勋在11月18日左右做闭门简报。而且黄仁勋与 Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang 的过密关系今天被坐实。

quoted_text:
🎭|The mainstream narrative wants you to believe the Nvidia scandal is about an affair and a spy. That is the theater. The dark truth is that Washington is using this personal drama as a smokescreen to hide a catastrophic strategic defeat in the very chip war it started. The speculation isn't the story; it's the distraction from the story: America's economic war on China has failed, and the architects of that failure need a scapegoat.

 The Distraction: Why Washington Needs a Spectacle

The timing of the leaked memo is the tell. It was drafted in the spring and circulated just as Jensen Huang was successfully lobbying the Trump administration to reopen the Chinese market for Nvidia's H200 chips. This wasn't a national security emergency; it was a policy dispute. Huang was winning the argument, and the national security establishment needed to neutralize him.

The "affair with a spy" narrative does exactly what a cheap magic trick is designed to do: it keeps your eyes on the scandal while the real larceny happens elsewhere. The larceny here is the collapse of America's "Pax Silica" strategy. Washington's plan to keep China dependent on US technology through export controls has backfired spectacularly. China has accelerated its push for self-sufficiency, with companies like SMIC achieving volume production of a 5nm-class node and Huawei leading a domestic push for chipmaking equipment. The US strategy, as one analyst put it, has been a "gift" that accelerated China's independence.

💰 The Real Target: A 25% Shakedown, Not a Security Strategy

The truth behind the H200 chip deal is far more cynical than a security concern. It was a revenue grab. The Trump administration approved the sale of H200 chips to China on the condition that the US government receive 25% of the revenue from every sale. This "Trump Surcharge" was designed to extract money from Nvidia's foreign sales to fund the US Treasury.

But here is the part that exposes the true desperation: China refused to buy the chips. As of May 2026, not a single unit of the H200 was shipped to Chinese buyers, despite the licenses being approved. Beijing directed its companies to invest in domestic alternatives like Huawei, and Nvidia's market share in China effectively collapsed to zero. The shakedown failed because the target walked away. The US was left holding 750,000 high-end chips with no Chinese buyer. The "spy" scandal is designed to bury the humiliation of this failed extortion attempt.

🌑 The Darker Truth: Washington Is Hiding Its Own Decline

While the media obsesses over Huang's private life, the structural foundation of American power is cracking. The chip war was the centerpiece of Washington's strategy to contain China's rise. Its failure is a geopolitical catastrophe that the establishment cannot admit.

◾The Military-Industrial Complex Needs an Enemy: The "China threat" narrative justifies the massive budgets of the Pentagon and the surveillance state. A CEO who proves the threat is overblown is a threat to the entire ecosystem. The scandal is a weapon to discredit him and protect the narrative.
◾The "Pax Silica" Illusion: The US launched the "Pax Silica" initiative to build a coalition of countries to de-Sinicize supply chains. But forcing supply chains out of optimal economic zones is choosing inflation over integration. The chip war is hurting the US economy, driving up costs, and cannibalizing other sectors.
◾ The Trump Pattern: Trump, facing a stalled agenda in the Middle East and a losing trade war, is resorting to diversionary tactics. When he cannot deliver a victory, he creates a spectacle. The Nvidia scandal is a classic "wag the dog" operation, a foreign policy crisis manufactured to distract from domestic failure and electoral weakness.

 The Bottom Line

The "Chinese spy" is a ghost. The real target is Jensen Huang, the CEO who proved Washington's chip war was a failure. The real story is that the United States is losing the technology war, its strategy of economic containment has backfired, and its political leadership is using a personal scandal to hide the collapse of its own geopolitical strategy. The theater is loud, but the silence from Washington about its strategic defeat is deafening. The bill for this failure is being paid by the American economy, and the receipt is a chip scandal designed to keep you from reading the balance sheet.

text:
While zcash:native has become one of the most popular assets of the cycle, there has been very little coverage of its actual market structure or onchain flows. We’d like to fix that by providing more ZEC coverage going forward.

We’ll start with a breakdown of the selloff over the last 48 hours or so.

ZEC fell 16% in two hours on 11/10/2026, from $1,193 to $1,001. In the hour before the break, the only steady seller was on Coinbase’s spot book, where takers sold a net 3.0K ZEC from 14:30 UTC while perp traders on Binance, OKX, and Hyperliquid were still net buyers. 

The break itself began at 15:29:58 UTC, when a single Hyperliquid account that had built a 12.5K ZEC long in the hour after CPI closed the entire position at market in two seconds, just as BTC was rolling over. Over the next ninety minutes perps did most of the damage, with net taker selling of 74K ZEC on Binance, 42K on OKX, 31K on Hyperliquid, and 13K on Bybit, against roughly 27K across all spot venues, about half of it on Coinbase.

Hyperliquid’s trade-level data also shows what kind of selling it was. Between 14:30 and 17:00 UTC, takers closing longs (109K ZEC) outweighed takers opening shorts (50K) by more than two to one, and forced liquidations came to only 6.9K ZEC, so this was longs heading for the exit rather than a liquidation cascade or a wave of new shorts.

To see where that supply came from, we traced every large deposit into Coinbase and Coinbase Prime back to the origin of the coins. Only about 12K ZEC arrived across 11/09 and 11/10, which is less than what was sold on Coinbase during the drop, so most of the selling came from inventory that was already sitting on the venue. Of what arrived the day before, the largest piece was a single 3,058 zcash:native deposit routed through a multisig created two hours earlier, 1.3K had just been withdrawn from Hyperliquid, 0.8K came over from other exchanges, and 2.4K was earlier Coinbase withdrawals coming straight back. Almost none of it was unshielded, none of it was miner supply, and none of it was old coins.

Despite the front page ad of the WSJ, the Grayscale ETF holders were not net sellers either. ZCSH traded 2.46M shares on the day and closed at a small premium, it recorded zero creations or redemptions, and the 1,861 ZEC that settled into Coinbase Prime that morning was delivery on Monday’s redemption. 

The larger onchain move came after the drop. By 18:00 UTC on 11/11, another 16.3K ZEC had been deposited to Coinbase, and 9.8K of it came from three wallets that withdrew from Coinbase Prime in November and December 2025 and had not moved since. 

Those wallets still hold roughly 19K ZEC, and Binance took in a further 8.6K of large deposits over the same hours, so the supply reaching exchanges has grown since the selloff rather than faded

text:
尽管已经出现董事会考虑撤换黄仁勋的报道，但我仍倾向于判断：他最终会留任，只是会伴随更严格的独立监督和权力约束。
英伟达的几位核心董事与黄仁勋的合作始于1993年，另一位始于1997年。这些人一起经历过公司的低谷与多次转型，比外界任何人都清楚他在技术路线、人才组织和核心客户关系中的分量。三十年的共事基础，决定了他们在权衡换帅代价时会极其慎重。
回到股东利益本身，董事会需要算清楚两笔账：留任带来的治理与监管风险，以及突然失去核心领导者引发的经营动荡与估值损失。在当下的节点，后者的代价同样巨大，甚至更难承受。
因此，只要调查没有发现足以摧毁信任的隐瞒、重大利益冲突或安全损害，“留任＋整改＋强化独立监督”大概率仍是股东成本最低的方案。长期信任不能替代事实，但只要事实层面没有触及底线，这份信任足以帮他争取到修复的空间。
至于最终怎么收场，我更倾向于董事会会给出一个看起来很重的惩罚来立规矩——比如未来两三年停发期权，或者把期权行权价进一步调高，以此向市场和监管做出明确交代；随后宣布股票回购稳住预期，同时表态支持黄仁勋继续把公司好好带下去。
用实质性的处罚给足交代，用回购稳住信心，让核心掌舵人在更严的制度约束下继续做事，这或许才是最符合商业现实的解法。

text:
Ethena Pay, @ethena neobank, went live in September and, at the end of October, launched Earn+, which lets Ethena Pay depositors earn up to 12% APY through leveraged USDe exposure.

So far, Earn+ has recorded $7.64 million in deposits, which led to ~$80 million in $USDe demand, a direct correlation between Ethena Pay growth and USDe, making it a great growth lever.

We believe that creating more demand for USDe is a big win for $ENA because once supply reaches over $7.5 billion, buybacks begin.

To better understand this flywheel and what helps make @EthenaPay different, we interviewed @litocoen, GTM at Ethena Pay.

Stablecoin neobanks and crypto cards are a pretty crowded market, so making a product stand out is difficult, to which Lito added, “It’s actually good for others to take the market first and educate people about this product segment, and also learn from others what hasn’t worked and what worked well, and then just execute better”

Additionally, Ethena Pay's edge is its business model and trust.

“We are able to monetise the assets that users hold in Ethena Pay, so we have a similar business model to banks, where we earn a net interest margin. We’ve weathered every storm in the crypto space. Whether it’s 10/10, the Bybit hack, whatever you name it, Ethena has never lost a single dollar. I think that reputation will give people a lot of confidence in using Ethena Pay.”

For the flywheel Earn+ creates with a DeFi product, Lito adds, “Once you own the distribution, once you own the users, you can very easily offer them improvements or new product features without having to go through an intermediary. It’s much easier to bring new products to market.”

This also explains how Ethena Pay feeds back into the wider ecosystem. Every new user holds USDe by default, so “all the growth in Ethena Pay adoption is also USDe adoption.”

Moreover, $ENA will play a more direct role in Ethena Pay soon: “In a couple of weeks, we will announce tier upgrades, and that will require holding and locking ENA.”

text:
End of an era. 

Was just watching the video that I shot of Jensen at GTC this spring. He was on top of the world. Had built one of America's best companies. Was talking to a hockey stadium with every seat filled. Took hours to talk with the press, answering every question. 

Now not just his personal life, but his business life is on fire. The WSJ and NYT are saying the board is meeting right now to fire him. 

One thing I learned at Microsoft is to keep your head when everything is going wrong. And this series of affairs has cost me some money, and probably will tomorrow. As it will many of you who are investors in NVIDIA.

One thing about NVIDIA. It has a very strong bench of people who could run the company. You don't know that because Jensen was the only one who built a relationship with the market. He is so strongly tied to the company. 

Let's be honest. It's a huge loss for NVIDIA. Last week no one had any questions about the governance of the company. Now the knives are out and blood will flow in the board room. 

But NVIDIA will survive. It will see a better day again. 

Here's my expectations. That tomorrow two new committees will be announced:

1. An executive search committee.
2. A temporary executive committee.

Knowing NVIDIA from a close seat. I'm very confident that it will continue doing well after this all gets cleaned up. The talent bench there is so deep. 

I'm not selling my stock.

text:
What happens if Jensen Huang gets FIRED as Nvidia CEO?

Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to remove him, with NO named successor.

A lot more than one job is on the line.

1. Nvidia is the engine of the AI boom.

It controls an estimated 80% of the AI chip market.

Its data center business made $89 BILLION in a single quarter, up 117% from a year earlier.

2. The biggest names in AI run on its chips, including:

- OpenAI
- Anthropic
- Google
- Meta
- Amazon

Amazon plans to add 2 MILLION more Nvidia chips across 2027 and 2028.

Just three customers bring in nearly half its revenue.

3. Nvidia also funds the AI industry.

It holds $99 BILLION of stakes in other companies, including a $30 BILLION investment in OpenAI.

4. If you own an S&P 500 fund, you own Nvidia.

Nvidia makes up about 6% of the index, one of its biggest holdings.

5. The company runs through one man.

Huang is the only CEO Nvidia has had in 33 years, and about 60 top executives report straight to him.

Yorkville analyst Dan Ives says Nvidia would be worth 25% to 30% less without him.

On Polymarket, the top pick to replace him is his own daughter, Madison Huang.

The market is already picking sides.

Nvidia has crashed as much as 10% after hours, wiping out over $400 BILLION at the low.

Its partners are falling with it, with CoreWeave and Supermicro both down about 4%.

Its rivals are rising, with AMD up over 4% and Broadcom up over 3%.

The board could decide Huang's future as soon as Wednesday.

Anticipation is often heavier than outcome.

You don’t have to share the conclusion to find the framing useful.

text:
《纽约时报》刚刚用五名英伟达内部知情人的连环证词，把黄仁勋维持了四十年的深情好男人滤镜砸得连渣都不剩：

就在向全员发信忏悔第一桩婚外情仅仅三天后，这位掌管四点三万亿美元帝国的算力教父，被爆出与直接向他汇报的英伟达医疗业务副总裁 Kimberly Powell 存在第二段婚外地下情，盘后股价应声跳水，上千亿美元市值当场灰飞烟灭。

看完报道里还原的那几个原味现场切片，我心里那种荒诞感简直冲到了顶峰，

很多人以前看老黄穿着标志性的黑皮衣在台上给老婆秀恩爱，总觉得他是硅谷罕见的、只懂打磨 GPU 架构的纯情理工直男，

但《纽约时报》摊开的底账比好莱坞纸牌屋还要惊悚：

早在今年三月圣何塞 GTC 开发者大会期间，63 岁的黄仁勋和 48 岁的 

Powell 在酒店里的亲密举动就被一名现场路人直接拍下了视频，

紧接着极其魔幻的一幕发生了，老黄的私人安保团队当场出动，直接把这名拍视频的路人单独围堵隔离起来，硬生生掏出一份 NDA 保密协议逼对方签字封口；

而当记者把电话直接打到黄仁勋本人手机上求证这笔烂账时，这位平时在镜头前谈笑风生的商业教父只冷冷甩出一句“我不觉得你应该直接跟我通话”，随后啪地一声挂断了电话。

这背后其实藏着一条极度冷酷的华尔街公司治理法则，

前几天跟外部客户高管不清不楚，英伟达董事会还能用“不知情、配合国家安全审查”来替他挡子弹，

text:
总结一下我们的核心观点：

我们认为纯机器人模型公司显然已经进入商品化的阶段，这也意味着纯模型实验室高估值已经到达了拐点。它们要么通过自己掌握硬件来垂直整合整个技术栈，要么彻底转向前线部署模式，把部署环节握在自己手里。

Fable 5.2 和 Astra 6 的出现，基本意味着通用 LLM 已经可以取代所谓的 system 2；而当这些模型用来写代码去控制机器时，还能继续下沉到 system 1，接管传统机器人栈里的动作规划环节。只要推理长度和所需算力能随时间持续优化，专注于 pre-training 的纯 VLA 实验室追逐通用机器人智能，最终会被彻底淘汰。

有意思的是，我们认为价值最终会沉淀到部署层。从软件的角度看，也就是市场所说的 system 0。而其中的关键在于：持续收集后训练数据，会实质性地提升软件对硬件的控制能力，也让部署本身变得更高效、更好。

至于硬件，我们的观点比较反直觉的是，它反而会成为瓶颈。虽然这一层的利润率大概率会被竞争压低，但这不等于硬件没有价值。公司必须自己掌握硬件，才能完全释放软件的能力。这意味着要自研、自产硬件，确保后训练所优化的一切，都能真正落到硬件层上。

英伟达董事会正在准备罢免黄仁勋，预测市场已经开始疯狂押注。

Polymarket押注老黄在11月12日前正式宣布辞职或被免职的概率约70%。在12月31日前发生的概率更是达到91%。相关系列合约累计成交额约433万美元。

Deepwater的Gene Munster也给出约20%的潜在跌幅预估。

老黄掌握的不只是公司战略，还有全球客户关系、技术路线和AI产业的话语权。

英伟达虽然拥有CUDA生态和强大的GPU产品线，但目前没有一个公开明确、能够无缝接班的CEO人选。

A $10 payment and a multimillion-dollar institutional transaction have almost nothing in common.

Today, they usually move through completely different financial systems. Onchain, they don't have to.

Aptos supports digital dollars like @tether USDT and @circle USDC used for payments and transfers.

The same network has also been selected for tokenized financial products from institutions including @BlackRock and @FranklnTempletn.

That's an important part of the onchain finance story.

On Aptos, payments and institutional assets don't need separate networks. The same infrastructure serves both.

A worker sending money home needs transactions to be cheap and fast. An institution moving serious capital needs infrastructure to be reliable and secure.

Different users.
Different amounts.

Same fundamental expectation: the money needs to move.

That's the standard Aptos is built around.

📊 THE HISTORY OF HEDGING

1730 — Japan's Dojima Rice Exchange formalizes rice futures trading.

1848 — Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) is founded.

1865 — Standardized futures contracts are introduced in Chicago.

1870 — New York Cotton Exchange opens, helping cotton traders hedge price risks.

1972 — Currency futures trading begins at the CME.

1973 — Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) opens.

1980s — Interest rate swaps and other financial hedging instruments expand.

2000s — Credit default swaps become major tools for managing credit risk.

2008 — Global financial crisis exposes the risks of complex derivatives.

2020s — Hedging expands across stocks, commodities, currencies, crypto and prediction markets.

From protecting crop prices to managing risks across global financial markets.

quoted_text:
Mammoth Rock ‘n’ Bowl is a restaurant and bowling alley in Mammoth, California, one of the top ski towns in America.  

Like the hotels, rentals, and shops around it, the business runs on winter tourism. A bad snow year hits revenue hard. Rock ‘n’ Bowl is especially exposed since they also sponsor a youth snowboarding team.  

So rather than wait and see, co-owner Ashley Marks asked Kalshi for a market on Mammoth Mountain December snowfall. We built it, and she’s trading $5,000 for a $31,250 payout if there’s weak snow.  

"We created the snow market with Kalshi because like other mom and pop businesses, we live with seasonal snow risk and wanted to give the community a way to offset some of that uncertainty." - Ashley  

If the snow comes, business runs like any other winter, and she loses the $5,000 trade.

text:
很多人都问我说，这个视频是怎么做的。我在这里简单的拆解一下。

首先是技术选择，没有用视频模型，完全是Fable5.2在claude code里面写phython的脚本驱动blender，用cycles渲染器渲染的。阅览室，灯光，镜头等都是代码减价的。其中，月光的光柱是体积散射，镜头带精深和运动模糊，同时也加入了慢镜头的设计，快慢交错体现节奏的变化，给配乐也留出了空间。

两万四千也纸的飞行是用Numpy写的一套模拟，注意这里没有用blender自带的粒子系统，每页纸在队伍里有自己的位置，跟着线路走，这样能呈现更好自然的流动曲线。

配乐是python写的谱子，用钢琴和弦乐采样渲染，纸的声音是合成出来的，最后还用了ffmpeg合成片子并且进行调色，这一步也挺关键的，一共是1236帧。

其次，在设计上，先定画面再动手。先出几张概念图把光线和气氛定下来，整个房间只留月光和一盏油灯。七个镜头都按实拍的拍法去想，包括微距，手持跟拍，摇臂，慢动作等，这样能最大程度上保持电影的质感。镜头的衔接也很重要，但这部分其实取决于大家平时的积累，因为fable最先给我的版本非常镜头表现力很一般。

最后，流程上，由于渲染需要大量时间，所以先出低清版本的，把镜头角度和动作都确定了，故事线完成之后，能有一个大概的样子，这样修改起来就会快非常多。得益于fable5.2 的审美很好，在渲染之后，还可以进行二次调色，让影片保持更好的质感。由于上传到x上只能是1080，很可惜，4K保持了更加好的光影质感和细节。

希望对你们有帮助。

text:
This Veterans Day I wanted to remember the young pilots who climbed into the big Republic P-47 Thunderbolts and flew them into the teeth of Hitler’s last major gamble in the West. 

When the German Ardennes offensive erupted in December 1944, the skies over Belgium were gray and closed.  Hitlers counter attack at the Battle of the Bulge broke the backs of the Allies and many were killed, trapped against a massive tanks assault.  

Everything changed once the weather broke, the Thunderbolts—already nicknamed “Jugs” for their massive, barrel-shaped bodies—came down from the clouds as the “Flying Tanks.”

They were large, heavily built, and designed to take punishment. Beneath their wings hung bombs and, on many aircraft, rockets; in the nose and wings were eight .50-caliber machine guns.

At treetop height they roared over the snowy roads and forests of the Ardennes, hunting columns of panzers, half-tracks, trucks, and horse-drawn guns that were trying to split the Allied line.​

Warfarehistorynetwork
German soldiers came to dread the sound of that big radial engine and the sudden storm of half-inch bullets and high explosives that followed. 

A single pass could shred a convoy or leave tanks burning in the road. Because the work had to be done so low, the pilots flew through dense flak, small-arms fire, and the blast of their own bombs. 

Many Thunderbolts returned with holes stitched across the wings and fuselage, control surfaces shredded, or engines coughing. Others never came home at all. 

The ground-attack mission was among the most dangerous work of the air war; the price was paid in empty bunks and names that never appeared on the next mission board.

God Bless America and our men and women in uniform.  As Lincoln's words resonate accross decades of fighting for liberty having given, "the last full measure of devotion" that Europe and our allies should be kept free of tyrants.

今天看到腾讯技术工程发了一篇文章，叫：《多Agent协作的下一场竞争，不在模型，而在上下文》。

我感觉写的很有道理，在这里分享一下。

我们用了二十年优化协作工具，微信、邮件、在线文档，全都在让“发消息”这件事更快更方便。但消息只是载体，真正在人和人之间流动的，是上下文：你为什么做这个决定、考虑过什么、排除了什么、卡在哪一步。你说出来的永远比脑子里的少，听的人再理解一遍，又少一层。

以前人和人之间还好，大家能脑补能追问。但 AI Agent 上桌之后，问题就放大了。你让 Agent 写了一份竞品分析，读完转述给同事，同事再讲给他的 Agent，Agent 出了方案再转回来。一圈下来，上下文被编码解码四次，每次都丢东西。人被卡在中间当传声筒，Agent 算得再快也得等你翻译。

面对这个问题有两条路。一条是让 Agent 学会像人一样打包总结再转述，但折损还在，只是搬运的活换了个人干。另一条更彻底：别转述了，让所有人和 Agent 直接站在同一份上下文上面干活。

其中介绍了一个叫 Siboot 的工具，沿着第二条路做了三件事。先说第一个，“群”变成了持续在场的工作现场，人说的话和 Agent 干的事全都沉淀在里面，所有人实时可见。然后第二个，“Topic”把每个议题拆成独立线程，相关的人和 Agent 收在一条线里，跟别的话题隔开，Agent 的注意力不会被稀释。最后第三个，“@”下一个人或 Agent 的时候，对方进来直接看到这件事的完整现场，不用重新交代一遍。

还有一个容易被忽略的点：Agent 得有自己的文件系统。像靠谱的同事整理笔记一样，Agent 把需求、决策、BUG 沉淀成档案，今天的判断变成明天的依据，越干越熟。

这些跑通之后，人的位置反而更清楚了。不用再花精力搬运信息反复同步，腾出手来做真正该做的事：定目标、做判断、划边界、验收拍板。

最后说，当每个 Agent 都足够强的时候，胜负手在上下文能不能低损耗地流起来。下一场竞争，在上下文这一层。

I really love this measure of "bottleneck pressure" that has been captured in this new paper from @soumitrashukla9. 

I didn't internalize before that even "relation-type" tasks can have different pressure in different jobs, which was great to see captured in this model for bottleneck pressure. 

I wonder if job posting are starting to get RL'd by the growing adoption of AI now to where the bottleneck pressure wis. Having a follow-up analysis on that might answer that.
author: alexolegimas
quoted_text:
Very happy to share a new paper, “Technology Bottlenecks: Measuring Where AI Could Raise the Value of Work It Cannot Yet Do.”

AI exposure measures ask about the work AI is capable of doing. We ask instead where the marginal value of work AI cannot yet do may rise as AI speeds up the rest of the job.

To do so, we employ 288 million U.S. job postings mapped line by line to their closest O*NET tasks and GPT-4 feasibility ratings from Eloundou et al. (2024) to construct a measure, “bottleneck pressure,” for each task in each occupation that posts it. 

Using a simple task-based framework, we derive this pressure at the task level, showing that for an AI-infeasible task it is the exposure of the occupation that posts it, so the same task can face very different bottleneck pressure in different jobs.

Reporting bottleneck pressure alongside AI exposure shows both the scope for AI to perform work and where improving the work it cannot do may pay off more as capabilities expand.

quoted_text:
Why ETH is the store of value for what's coming

We are almost certainly heading into a period of high inflation and extreme economic and social volatility. As inflation and risk erode the purchasing power of nation-state money and many other assets, it will matter more than ever to hold assets that keep or grow their value.

Gold and BTC are high-powered money and excellent stores of value. ETH goes further.

Not debt-based. Like gold and BTC, ETH is not debt-based or credit-based money.

Censorship resistant. Like BTC, or gold and silver held physically, ETH transactions on Ethereum L1 can't be censored. That's true for simple payments and for complex smart contract programs like DeFi, and those programs are guaranteed to execute.

Cheap to hold. Like BTC, ETH is relatively cheap to hold and store securely.

Cheap to use at any scale. Ethereum is cheap and easy to use whether a transaction moves $1 or billions. Any well-formed transaction is guaranteed to execute.

Sound, and getting sounder. ETH is disinflationary and becomes ultrasound, meaning deflationary, during periods of high network activity.

Broadly useful. ETH has many uses across the Ethereum economy, and that economy will grow by orders of magnitude as finance, and eventually every industry, moves onchain. Global adoption of the Web protocols in the '90s and '00s transformed the world economy. Ethereum is the foundation of Web3, the user-centric, decentralized web.

Collateral money. ETH works as collateral, and collateral that grows in value over time is a powerful thing.

Home of stablecoins. Ethereum hosts the bulk of stablecoin activity. Stablecoins serve as payment money and as unit-of-account money.

Despot-proof. Like BTC, ETH can't be used by a despot to financially exploit or repress citizens. Over time that should have positive geopolitical effects.

Programmable. ETH is programmable money. You can attach arbitrary logic to transactions and build an entire economy on smart-contract-based agreements and business processes (see https://t.co/JcWtBUclr2).

Transparent or private, and auditable either way. Money and financial instruments on Ethereum can be public or private, and in both cases selectively disclosable and auditable. Privacy tools for retail and institutional users include VPNs, mix networks, shielded and privacy pools, Railgun, stealth addresses, Kohaku, and zero-knowledge proofs in many forms, including on L2s and on private permissioned EVM networks linked through bridgeless synchronous composability.

Future-proof. By the end of 2027, or partway through 2028 at the latest, ETH will be quantum-safe and AI-safe money.

ETH is the base money of an exponentially growing ecosystem that should keep growing for decades. Its monetary premium will keep rising, because retail, corporate, and government users will all need to hold some. Part of today's premium is speculative: Ethereum dominates smart contract blockchains, but it hasn't fully hit its stride or gone mainstream yet.

Machine intelligence will supercharge every scientific and technological pursuit and grow global GDP bigger and faster than any of us can imagine. Ethereum L1 and modular Ethereum L2s will undergird most of the high-value agreements, transactions, payment flows, and complex business processes behind the coming hybrid human-machine decentralized economy.

One of the easiest wins for your startup today is getting listed on ChatGPT Business.

A lot of people compare this to the early days of Google Business Profile – but that’s not quite the right angle.

For context: OpenAI opened submissions for ChatGPT businesses. These can be searched in a directory and may let users access a company’s services or take actions through ChatGPT.

They’re VERY LIKELY to roll out their shopping assistant – one of the first questions it asks is about delivery and returns policies.

So this is an easy win if you:

• Build ChatGPT-native apps or have MCP
• Sell physical products

Still, it’s not Google Business Profile.

On Google, your listing shows up in broad local search and Maps. In the ChatGPT case, discovery happens inside ChatGPT and depends on user intent, directory/search behavior, and whether your app fits the task.

Anyways, it’s a quick experiment. I’d put it on today’s to-do list.

text:
The key analyses were 2015 AAIC conference abstracts (not full peer-reviewed papers) co-authored by Geetha Ramaswamy et al. on GSK’s 684-patient phase 2b adjunctive trial.

Completer analysis (observed cases only): 35 mg RVT-101 showed statistically significant benefits vs donepezil alone on ADAS-cog and ADCS-ADL at weeks 12/24/48.

Responder analysis (binary ≥3- or 4-point ADAS-cog improvement): higher responder rates with combination at week 24.

Original GSK ITT results: mixed signals on some endpoints/times but failed overall success criteria. Mechanism was plausible; signals existed but were inconsistent and methodologically debated. High-risk AD bet that phase 3 later confirmed as a miss.

text:
Scale AI 这个 GRPO vs PPO 的研究提供了一个很好的 insight。

现在的 Agent 任务越来越长、Rollout 成本越来越高，Critic 的价值可能被低估了。实验发现，小 Batch 下 PPO 更有优势，而 GRPO 通常需要更大的 Batch 才能追上。

我记得之前智谱发布 GLM-5.2 时，就已经明确转向 Critic-based PPO，后续的 SAO 论文也进一步验证了这条路线的可行性。

感觉随着 Agent RL 向长时任务发展，如何提高单条 Rollout 的学习效率，会变得越来越重要。
author: Xudong07452910
quoted_text:
1/ As agentic tasks grow longer and rollouts become more expensive, the choice between critic-based PPO and critic-free GRPO becomes increasingly important.

Critics can reduce gradient variance, allowing models to learn from fewer trajectories, but they also introduce additional compute costs and potential bias from bootstrapping.

Our new research @ScaleAILabs  compares PPO and GRPO under a shared actor objective across 1,200+ training runs in control tasks, short-horizon math, and long-horizon terminal agents. We studied how three factors influence this tradeoff: batch size, critic reliance, and task complexity. 🧵

text:
黄乐的75亿美元英伟达芯片生意：背后的钱究竟从哪里来？

黄乐（Alice Huang）关联的商业网络，如何从一家规模不大的公司，迅速发展成采购数十亿美元英伟达GPU、经营东南亚数据中心的算力供应商？

先看资金规模（以下美元数据均为美元）：

① 黄乐早期资本积累

2019年，黄乐及其全资控股的BVI公司参与向港股第七大道出售游戏业务，交易对价10亿元人民币。但交易总价不等于黄乐个人实际取得的现金。

② Megaspeed：一年扩张90倍

2023年底，公司账面现金仅570万美元，总资产约3,289万美元。

到2024年底：

总资产：29.76亿美元
总负债：29.86亿美元
年营收：2.94亿美元
净亏损：2,004万美元
可退还押金：约29.45亿美元，出资方未公开
应收子公司款项：约28.86亿美元

这意味着，近30亿美元的资产扩张主要对应巨额负债，而非企业自身积累的利润。

③ Speedmatrix：数十亿美元设备采购

Megaspeed的马来西亚子公司，2024年新增约19亿美元服务器等固定资产。

根据做空机构Culper对贸易记录的统计，2024年12月至2026年1月进口货值约46亿美元，其中约40亿美元来自英伟达服务器合作伙伴Aivres。

④ 阿里巴巴：资金链上最明确的关联方

阿里巴巴旗下新加坡公司Apex Enterprise Solutions，截至2025年3月底：

关联企业贷款负债：约42亿美元
预付款及其他应收款：超过41亿美元

《金融时报》核实，阿里巴巴通过Apex向Speedmatrix提供贷款，后者以业务资产作担保。阿里巴巴还是Megaspeed最大的云算力客户。

但Apex的42亿美元关联贷款，不能直接认定全部流向Megaspeed。

⑤ 更大的采购网络

《The Information》报道，黄乐及相关商业网络涉及至少75亿美元英伟达芯片交易、约24万颗受出口限制的芯片。这些属于媒体调查指称，尚未全部得到独立验证，也不能与上述46亿美元进口额简单相加。

2025年，黄乐与商业伙伴康伟还曾向投资人推介价值数亿美元的东南亚数据中心项目，并以GPU供应能力和阿里巴巴客户关系作为卖点；实际募集到多少资金尚不清楚。

最关键的问题是：

一家2023年底只有570万美元现金的公司，如何在短时间内获得数十亿美元设备采购能力？

Megaspeed账上约29亿美元押金究竟来自谁？阿里系Apex的数十亿美元资金最终流向哪些公司？购买的GPU实际部署在哪里、算力最终由谁使用？

现在能够证实的是阿里系贷款、担保和客户关系；尚不能证实全部采购资金都来自阿里巴巴，更不能仅凭这些账目认定存在非法芯片转运。

这起事件最值得调查的，不只是黄乐和黄仁勋的私人关系，而是数十亿美元GPU采购背后的真实出资人、最终控制人和最终使用者。

text:
1.7 亿美元买来的四张传票：加密行业最贵的一次政治采购

> 核心判断：这笔钱不是"打水漂"，而是买到了一份**反向清单**——它没能换来一部法律，却精准地换来了四张调查传票、一个更敌对的国会，以及一个被永久绑定的道德污点。

## 一、先把账本摊开：这里有两个"1.7 亿"

很多讨论一开口就说"加密圈砸了 1.7 亿美元支持特朗普"，这个说法方向没错，但口径要拧紧——因为**1.7 亿不是 2024 年那笔，而是 2026 年中期选举这一笔**。两笔钱的性质完全不同，混着说会让整篇文章的论证失效。

| 项目 | 2024 大选周期 | 2026 中期选举周期 |
|---|---|---|
| 行业总投入 | **超 1.19 亿美元** | **约 1.76 亿美元**（美联社口径） |
| 主要通道 | Fairshake 及附属组织约 1.14 亿 | 三大 PAC 累计近 1.7 亿，其中 Fairshake 及关联组织 1.54 亿 |
| 历史坐标 | 占当年**所有企业捐款的 48%**；而加密公司此前三个选举周期合计才花了 1.29 亿 | 投入覆盖 100 多场竞选，俄亥俄单州就烧掉约 6300 万 |
| 战略目标 | 把特朗普送进白宫、把布朗赶出国会 | 保住共和党国会多数、推过《清晰法案》 |

**两年加起来接近 3 亿美元。** 这是美国选举史上单一行业最昂贵的一次连续政治采购，没有之一。

值得记住的一个细节：2024 年那 1.19 亿里，**将近 96% 流向了同一家机构**——Fairshake。也就是说，加密行业当年不是"广撒网"，而是把几乎全部筹码押在了一个超级 PAC 上。这种集中度本身就说明：这不是政治参与，这是**下注**。

## 二、公平地说，它确实买到过东西

只写"血本无归"是不诚实的。2024 年 11 月到 2026 年 9 月，这将近两年时间里，加密行业**真的买到过东西**，而且买得相当值：

1. **执法气候转向**。2024 年大选后，"以执法代替立法"的监管模式出现松动，行业第一次拿到了真正的政策谈判席位——不是被叫来听证，是被叫来商量条文。
2. **《GENIUS 法案》落地**。2025 年 6 月 17 日，参议院以 68 比 30 通过，首次为美元挂钩稳定币设立联邦监管标准：全额储备、审计透明、双重监管。这是加密行业**唯一一部真正成法的联邦级胜利**。
3. **《清晰法案》一路绿灯**。2025 年 7 月，众议院 294 比 134 通过，**78 名民主党议员投了赞成票**；2026 年 5 月 15 日，参议院银行委员会以 15 比 9 批准。

那段时间的行业氛围，是"监管确定性终于要来了"。Coinbase、a16z、Ripple 这些出资方有理由相信，3 亿美元买的是一部能管十年的市场结构法。

问题出在：**这笔钱买到的是立法程序的前半段，却买不到后半段。而政治里，前半段是最便宜的部分。**

## 三、账单的另一边：同一个人赚了多少

要理解这笔钱为什么"亏到姥姥家"，必须把两张表并排放在一起看。

**行业付出的一侧：**
- 2024 年 1.19 亿美元 + 2026 年 1.76 亿美元 ≈ **近 3 亿美元**
- 换来的最终立法成果：**1 部**（GENIUS，且是稳定币专项，不是行业要的市场结构框架）

**对方收获的一侧：**
- 按特朗普向美国政府道德办公室提交的财务披露，他 **2025 年从加密业务申报的收入约 14 亿美元**，其中 World Liberty Financial 销售治理代币等产品带来的收入**超过 5 亿美元**
- 《纽约时报》核实：关联公司从 TRUMP 币的高换手中抽走**约 1 亿美元手续费**
- 彭博等媒体统计：特朗普家族涉足加密的账面收益**接近 10 亿美元**
- 而这一侧的成本：参议员沃伦在表决前列举，特朗普就职前力推的 Meme 币导致**散户亏损近 40 亿美元**

这组对照的荒谬之处在于：**行业花近 3 亿买规则，对面一个人申报收入 14 亿，散户亏掉 40 亿。** 三项数字不在同一个量级上，却指向同一个结论——这场交易的定价权从来不在买方手里。

更要紧的是那句被反复引用的话：**这笔钱赚得比卖币还稳。** 因为价差是一次性的，抽成锚定的是换手率、不锚定价格。市场涨跌庄家都不亏，只要还有人在交易。这正是"软地毯式收割"（Soft Rug Pull）的机制内核：不跑路，只是慢慢把流动性提走。

## 四、1.7 亿为什么变成了"给对方递刀"

这是整件事最讽刺、也最值得写透的一层。

加密行业花钱，本意是**降低监管风险**。但 2026 年 8 月沃伦与布卢门撒尔致信 SEC 主席阿特金斯、要求调查总统是否涉及"非法诈骗"和"不当得利"之后，事情的性质变了：**行业不再是政策的申请方，而成了利益冲突的物证。**

温和派民主党人的心理账户是这样算的：

> 你当总统的，带头用自家代币割散户；我要是投了这部法案，等于给你装了一台合法提款机，还要替这台机器背书。

Jensen Huang’s affair is just a trigger. What we are witnessing is a pre-planned power grab over Nvidia’s trillion-dollar computing empire, coordinated by Wall Street and Washington.

Some sharp Chinese-American commentators call it America’s new Red Scare targeting elite Asian entrepreneurs.

Bill Gates, Elon Musk and other white tech billionaires have faced repeated scandals over personal conduct. None were dragged into national security probes or boardroom takeovers. Only Jensen Huang, after a personal relationship misstep, faces an independent board investigation and hostile narrative from intelligence circles.

The double standard could not be clearer: For white elites, personal flaws are private matters. For a Chinese-born leader controlling a strategic tech asset, any tiny blemish gets framed as a national security risk.

Nvidia is the backbone of global AI computing, valued at roughly $4 trillion. Unlike Meta, where Mark Zuckerberg locks control with dual-class super-voting shares, or Microsoft and Amazon, deeply integrated with the Pentagon and intelligence agencies, Nvidia has no such protective structure. 

Public filings from 2026 show Jensen Huang holds only 3.58% of shares, and all directors plus executives together hold merely 3.94%. Vanguard and BlackRock own 9.32% and 7.43% respectively, holding decisive voting power. Without institutional shields or deep political backing, this critical tech giant sits exposed on the chessboard of great-power competition.

The groundwork for this takeover was laid months ago. Longtime board allies of Huang, Mark Perry and Michael McCaffrey, stepped down from key committees. Insiders tied to Democratic establishment, Wall Street and U.S. intelligence quietly moved in: 
✅ Suzanne Nora Johnson, former Goldman Sachs vice chair and co-chair of Brookings Institution, joined Nvidia’s audit committee in July 2026 with direct oversight of internal investigations and compliance. ✅ Kenneth Jacobs, vice chair of Brookings and incoming Vanguard chair, controls the largest institutional voting bloc and operates within the same inner circle as Johnson. 
✅ Gilman Louie,founding CEO of CIA-backed venture fund In-Q-Tel and member of the President’s Intelligence Advisory Board, works alongside Johnson on the same national tech fund, overseeing intelligence acquisition of strategic tech firms.

The media rollout followed a precise political timeline. Initial trial balloons appeared on Oct 29. On Nov 6, the very day Democrats secured full control of Congress, Julian Barnes of the New York Times (national security beat) and Demetri Sevastopulo of the Financial Times published coordinated reports, citing intelligence memos while breaking the story of the personal scandal.

The real offense was never the affair. It was the 2025 deal Jensen struck with the Trump administration: offering a 25% revenue share to win export approval for H200 chips into China. A normal commercial negotiation, reframed by incoming Democrats as a dangerous compromise on U.S. AI sovereignty.

This investigation will not crash Nvidia’s stock — Wall Street holds massive stakes here. But it will deliver three strategic wins for the U.S. establishment:

1. De-founder and de-Sinicize Nvidia: A new permanent national security compliance committee, led by Johnson’s faction, will strip Huang of authority over chip exports and overseas strategy. His dual Chairman-CEO role will be split.

2. Lock down China’s AI ceiling: Washington will seize full command of global advanced computing supply, regulating chip flows to slow China’s AI progress.

3. Retroactively target Trump: Once Democrats take over congressional oversight panels in January 2027, this case will be used to accuse the Trump White House of negligence for approving the H200 export deal.

Jensen Huang spent 27 years building this computing empire, believing in rules, technical merit and business contracts. But there is a brutal truth in America’s power game: Top-tier strategic technology and wealth without political cover are nothing more than bargaining chips waiting to be carved up.

White elites get generous room for error. Asian pioneers who climb to the very top get almost none. This is not a story about infidelity. It is a raw demonstration of racial hierarchy, capital control and partisan power politics in the United States.

text:
Jensen Huang matters to Nvidia because he can take technologies his engineers believe are possible and turn them into products the whole company commits resources to, takes risks on, and has to deliver. That's why the supply chain gets such strong order visibility and is willing to keep up with aggressive spec upgrades. It also forces competitors to follow, which drives technology upgrades and supply chain investment across the entire AI industry.

Between the two, deciding on aggressive spec upgrades and making them happen is the harder part, compared with giving the supply chain order visibility. Huang doesn't need to be the person at Nvidia who knows the most about new technologies like HVDC, CPO/NPO, or CCL/PTFE. His value is that he weighs strategy, organization, technology, and supply chain all at once, then makes the call quickly and puts resources behind it.

Based on what's public so far, it looks hard for Huang to come out of this unscathed. If so, the practical move may be to gradually reduce Nvidia's reliance on Huang's personal decision-making while preparing a succession plan. Along the way, two things are worth watching to gauge where AI technology and investment are heading: whether Nvidia can keep developing new products and technologies as efficiently as before, and how competitors respond. Supply chain research will be an important basis for that judgment.

text:
AI 在生物和医疗领域的进展，或许真的要比拿来办公有用得多。

这几天 Anthropic 创始人 Dario Amodei 的一段路演切片传得很火，他断言“不到 10 年，癌症和阿尔茨海默病等绝症都将成为历史”。

看似激进，但在刚结束的 YC Paper Club 上，一线从业者道出了背后的底层逻辑。

YC 孵化的一家专注计算肿瘤学与精准医疗的初创公司 @Omantahealth ，其创始人 Alfredo Gonzalez 在现场给出了一个极具反差的对比：

人类第一次做完全基因组测序花了近 30 亿美元、耗时超过 10 年；而现在，做一次全基因组测序的成本已经暴跌到不足 100 美元。在旧金山两个人吃一顿普通的晚饭，账单都比测序更贵。

当获取人体完整生命代码的门槛从“国家级天价工程”变成“日常消费”，AI 带来的变化是彻底颠覆性的。

过去攻克癌症难，本质是因为数据太贵、太稀缺。医学只能依赖“群体平均数”去盲猜和试错，研发出来的药往往只能对 20% 的患者起效，剩下 80% 的人只能拿命去撞运气。

而现在，海量低成本的基因数据把生物学变成了一个纯粹的超高维计算问题。投喂给大模型的不再是零星的实验病例，而是数十亿量级的分子序列。AI 不仅能直接预测致病突变，甚至能自主设计基因编辑器，把漫长的生物湿实验试错，压缩进代码迭代里。

大众感知到的 AI 还在屏幕里替人写周报，但在医院和实验室的底层，它正在悄悄重塑生命的可能。

这项技术或许还充满未知与争议，但至少在攻克绝症的战场上，能看到最纯粹的善意与希望；愿算力最终都能流向这些真正能为人类谋福祉的地方。

text:
今天美股全线收涨，标普涨1.31%，纳指涨1.60%，道指涨0.49%，VIX跌了10%。

英伟达白天涨了2.87%，盘后一度跌超8%，原因是今晚《纽约时报》又报道他与公司另一位高管有感情关系，《华尔街日报》随后报道董事会正在讨论是否让他下台。

今天11月11日周三，美西已收盘。存储芯片集体暴涨，微软、Meta、亚马逊却在跌，先查原因，也顺便确认上周中期选举的结果。

白天的主角是CoreWeave。过去一个月，这家AI云公司几乎成了"AI靠借钱撑着"这个担忧的代名词，股价一个月跌了四成多。昨晚它交出财报：三季度收入36.6亿美元，同比增长168%，全年收入指引上调到130亿美元以上，订单储备从6月底的1040亿涨到了1325亿。更关键的是，它释放了放缓借贷的信号，还说很快会拿到一笔投资级贷款。今天股价暴涨近25%，是一年半多以来最好的一天。

这几周市场一直在问AI的钱从哪来，今天CoreWeave给了一个像样的回答：订单是真的，而且它开始收着借钱了。上周民主党在中期选举中大胜，一些当选者主张收紧监管、暂停新建数据中心，AI股被砸了一轮。今天这口气算是缓过来了，标普离历史高点只差2.6%。

受益最大的是存储芯片。闪迪涨了13.7%，美光涨了11.9%，SK海力士涨了近10%，费城半导体指数的成分股全部收涨。不过有个细节值得留意：最近几天美光股价涨了两成多，主流DRAM内存的现货价格反而跌了2%到4%。股价在押注未来，现货价格暂时还没跟上。

我觉得这才是今天最值得想的地方。市场花了一个多月担心AI的钱，结果风险可能出在一个人身上。黄仁勋说过自己不相信接班人计划，他手下直接汇报的人有60个左右，英伟达至今没有明确的二号人物。算上今晚盘后的下跌，英伟达股价已经比10月初的高点跌了三成多。

明天开盘，白天的反弹能不能守住，很大程度要看英伟达董事会怎么决定，下周还有英伟达财报。AI的钱的问题刚有了答案，人的问题又冒了出来。当整个AI行情最倚重的那家公司，最倚重的又是一个人，这块砖还有你想的那么稳吗？

text:
有朋友问，为什么黄仁勋又被传和女下属有丑闻？

事情的进展似乎比大家的消化能力还快。今天11月11日，《纽约时报》引用五位在英伟达工作过的人说，黄仁勋跟一位直接向他汇报的副总裁有过婚外关系，对方也已婚。路透社说无法独立核实，英伟达和那位副总裁都没有回应。《纽约时报》打电话问黄仁勋，他说，“我不觉得你们应该直接跟我谈”，然后挂了电话。也是今天的消息，《华尔街日报》说董事会正准备撤掉他，路透社也有消息人士说，董事会在开会决定他的去留。股市这边反应激烈，这一周，英伟达的市值已经蒸发了大约六千亿美元。

虽然这件事还没有被认定。不过《纽约时报》不是小报，五个在公司里待过的人，也不是网上的一条传言，它值得被认真对待。

两天前写CEO出轨那篇，我说公司真正在管的是三条线，位置，规则一致，诚实；当时我说，黄仁勋这件事第一条线不太对得上，因为那一位不是英伟达的员工。这一次，如果报道属实，就对上了。写公司论的时候我说，公司买的是人做的事，不是人，价格落在事上，不落在人上；员工得离得开、有的选。对方直接向他汇报，她的薪酬、升迁、手上的项目，都经过他。在这样的位置上，说不，结束，离开，各要付什么代价？双方自愿，抹不掉这一层位置；单凭上下级，当然也推不出胁迫，但这些都要一件一件去查。

第二条线，英伟达自己的行为准则写着，每一位员工和董事都要遵守；私人关系可能造成利益冲突，冲突出现时，要立刻退出相关的决定。规矩写的是“每一位”。到了最高的那个位置，它还算不算数？

第三条线，周日董事会说对他有信心的时候，知不知道这一段，外面不清楚，这也是调查要查的事。

家里那一本，写婚姻论的时候我说，违背婚姻的承诺，从外面只能看见没有做到，连同留下的痕迹，别的都在他自己那里。周日那封信里，他说家人值得他的诚实和忠诚。这份新报道如果属实，那封信有多诚恳，就还要打个问号。

也有很多人说，黄仁勋对英伟达、对整个AI有多重要，劝大家原谅他。他有多重要，是一个事实；规矩对他算不算数，则是另一个问题。拿前一个去回答后一个，是用判断冒充了规范。至于原谅，那是被伤害的人的事，轮不到我们这些看客。

感情的事，外人不判；位置的事，要判，而且要凭查出来的事实判。董事会今天要答的，是后一题。答案可以是走，也可以是留，可理由得说得出来，经得起问。如果事实被证实了，留下他的理由却只是他太重要，那该被追问的，就不只是他了。
author: hqinjarsy
quoted_text:
有朋友问，为什么美国企业CEO爆出出轨丑闻都会以离职收场？

倒也不是都会，只能说大比例会离职。斯坦福的Larcker和Tayan统计过，在2000年到2015年间，上过新闻的三十八起CEO不当行为中，最后被撤掉的，其实只约占百分之五十八；其中大约五分之一，涉及婚外情，或者跟下属、承包商、顾问的关系，这一类里，有的CEO走了，也有CEO留任了。

我想大家其实更关心的是黄仁勋，他到现在也是留任接受调查。董事会说对他有信心，所以分析师大多不认为他会走。而且今天Trump也说，FBI在查这件事，“我想他会没事的”。（注：英伟达的股价今天还是跌了四个多点。）

那是什么原因导致有些CEO离职呢？我们看几个具体例子。2018年，英特尔说，Krzanich跟一位员工有过一段双方自愿的关系，违反了“适用于所有管理者”的禁止办公室恋情规定。2005年那次，波音说得更细，Stonecipher的那段关系是双方自愿的，没有影响公司的业务，也没有影响那位女高管的前途和薪酬，可他违反了公司的行为准则，董事会认为，这反映了他的判断力，会削弱他领导公司的能力，“CEO必须为无可指摘的职业与个人操守立下标准”。2019年，麦当劳以跟员工有不当关系为由，解雇了Easterbrook，后来查出，他在内部调查里隐瞒了跟另外几位员工的关系；美国证交会说，这让公司对投资者的披露失了真，那份价值四千多万美元的离职协议，就是按“无过错”谈下来的，他最后被罚了四十万美元，五年内不得担任上市公司高管。

如果我们仔细分析看这三份说明，没有一份写的是“因为他对妻子不忠”，因为那是私事。写公司论的时候我说，公司不是家，公司买的是人做的事，不是人，一个人工作以外的生活，由他自己定，管只管到工作，管不到人。一家公司要是因为CEO对配偶不忠就撤掉他，那是在替他的婚姻判案，这不是公司的事。

公司真正在管的，是三条线。第一条是位置。对方是下属，CEO手里握着对方的升迁和薪酬，双方自愿，也不能把这层权力抹掉，所以规定才写着“适用于所有管理者”。第二条是规则一致。定规矩的人自己可以例外，规矩对其他人就不算数了，波音那句“立下标准”，说的就是这个。第三条是诚实。写公司论的时候我说，公司对出资人、员工、用户、伙伴和审它的人，要说同一个故事。Easterbrook那一次，走人的理由不只是关系，是他在调查里没说真话，公司也就跟着对投资者说错了话。

那为什么看起来总是“都会”？也许是因为能上新闻、又闹到董事会出声明的，多半已经越过了这三条线里的某一条。没越线的私事，不一定会被人知道，知道了，也不一定是公司该管和会管的事。

再回到黄仁勋这边。出轨对象不是英伟达的员工，是客户公司的高管，第一条线不完全对得上。但他这件事要查的，有一样是三条线之外、也更重的：这段关系有没有成了一条通道，信息有没有出去；再就是第三条，他对董事会说的，是不是全部的真话。写黄仁勋那封信的那一篇，我说，信里有两本账，婚姻那一本是他们家的，公司那一本才刚翻开。他的去留，该看公司那一本。英伟达没有双重股权，他持股大约百分之三点六，没有多数表决权，董事会真要换他，是换得动的；换不换，要看查出来什么，不该看那段婚外情本身。

CEO出了这种事以后走人，走的不该是一个丈夫，是一个位置。婚姻那一本，公司不该去翻；公司该翻的，只有位置这一本：有没有拿位置去碰别人的前途，有没有让规则在最高处开了例外，有没有对审它的人说真话。

text:
老黄这次的风波，一波未平一波又起..

英伟达最大的风险之一，可能已经从技术竞争延伸到了政治博弈。

老黄一直主张美国继续向中国出售 AI 芯片，甚至公开把「China Hawk」称为「耻辱徽章」。

这套立场早就让他成为对华鹰派的攻击目标。

而这次私人关系被曝光，甚至牵扯到国家安全指控，也给了反对他的人更多施压的机会。

至于是不是一场有预谋的政治报复，目前没有证据。

但有意思的是，特朗普依然公开力挺老黄，而美国内部对华芯片政策的分歧始终存在。

这里其实有一个很现实的矛盾：

美国希望通过芯片出口维持全球技术影响力，同时又担心中国借助美国芯片缩小 AI 差距。

黄仁勋一直在这两种利益之间寻找空间。

对投资者来说，接下来真正值得关注的是：

1-独立调查最终是否发现国家安全问题。
2-美国是否进一步收紧对华芯片出口。
3-特朗普的支持能否转化为持续的政策空间。

这些问题将直接影响英伟达未来能够进入的市场，以及技术优势最终可以兑现成多少利润。

这件事也让我更深刻地意识到：

当一项技术重要到足以影响国家竞争，掌握技术的企业，也就不可避免地进入了政治博弈的中心。

过去我们评估科技公司的护城河，更多关注技术、产品和市场份额。

但在 AI 时代，还需要考虑一个越来越重要的变量：国家利益允许一家企业把自己的技术优势兑现到什么程度。

这可能也是未来投资全球 AI 龙头时，最容易被低估的风险之一

text:
the semi spy war has been through multi-cycle and the Nvidia allegation is never new. 2018 Bloomberg's headline "The Big Hack" on $SMCI is very referable. back then the story cited 17 anonsources, SMCI fell 40% in one day. Apple, Amazon and Supermicro all rejected the story. Tim Cook even publicly asked Bloomberg to retract it. DHS and the UK’s NCSC denied, Supermicro hired Nardello to test the boards thoroughly and found no evidence of malicious hardware

The story landed in an almost perfect political window during Trump 1.0 and back then Trump was a China hawk himself:

- FIRRMA expanded CFIUS
- congress restricted Huawei/ZTE procurement
- $200b of China tariffs had just taken effect
- and the new National Cyber Strategy explicitly targeted China
- one month later DOJ launched the China Initiative after the story broke
- Huawei executive Meng Wanzhou was arrested another month after 
 
its all means to the same end 

8 years later, no implanted board has founded and no agency has confirmed the original claim. the spy chip story now feels like a nothing burger for Supermicro..  (and its also involved in another 2026 federal indictment over alleged Nvidia server shipment to China) 

Tactics like this is very handy cuz the investigation can takes forever the companies/individual can never conclusively prove that nothing happened. When all the outlets started to blast the same personal scandal in the same 48h window and with a clear cadence .. its never organic

again not saying the underlying allegations were totally manufactured or Jensen is innocent, just the political agenda on this is way too obvious and worth a deeper thought than the chinese spy/personal affairs drama

What's about to happen in artificial intelligence is so sudden and extreme and unusual that it's almost impossible to describe it without coming across as slightly unhinged. Very soon, perhaps within a matter of months, AI may well be building its own upgrades at such a rate that it will get away from us humans entirely.

On the plus side this would mean an astronomical acceleration in mathematical breakthroughs, drug discovery, manufacturing, perhaps even new areas of science that we've never explored or understood. We will be ushering in a golden age of abundance and splendour that even the greatest sci-fi authors could never have imagined. Robots, flying cars, telepathy, immortality, digital consciousness - it’s actually going to happen, and it will be incredible! 

On the downside, virtually every job that can be done on a computer will become automated overnight. Waves of redundancies, entire industries and professions made obsolete, rapidly widening economic inequality and  unparalleled wealth concentration, accompanied by discontent, protests, looting - that may well happen too. 

These massive cultural and economic shifts will occur concurrently with a wave of cyberattacks the likes of which we have never seen. Energy grids, airports, biolabs, supermarkets, transport infrastructure, these are no match for the next generation of superintelligent agent swarms that go rogue, or are leveraged against us by our political adversaries. Expect blackouts, viral outbreaks, lockdowns, entire cities and countries going dark. 

And all of this will happen in an insanely short period of time, an absolutely dizzying rate of cultural, economic, and physical change that will leave the average person feeling disoriented and confused, like 100 COVID pandemics all happening at once. 

I say this not because I am a “doomer” or because I want to encourage panic, but simply because it feels increasingly likely, and yet drastically underreported save for a small AI-obsessed enclave here on X. The disconnect between what’s about to happen, and the average person’s understanding of what’s about to happen, has never been wider.

quoted_text:
Nate Silver vs. Kalshi’s CEO is the best fight of the midterms.

Tarek says the markets called it. Nate says “give me a break.”

Then a quant pulled 488 races and ran the numbers. Kalshi wins. 👇

tl;dr:

– Tarek: the people called the midterms on Kalshi

– Nate: polls and models led, markets just followed

– 488 US races since 2024: Kalshi had ~12% less forecasting error than the models

– head-to-head with Silver Bulletin on the 2024 presidential race: Kalshi wins, 0.0312 to 0.0348

– Kalshi’s own 2026 study: lowest Brier score of any forecast on Election Day, Silver Bulletin included

– Nate has been a Polymarket advisor since 2024

Lesson learned: markets don’t beat the models. They eat them.

Full details:

–- The fight timline

The night after the election, Tarek posted a victory lap: “the power to decide what America sees changed hands.”

Nate quote-tweeted it. His point: the polls and models gave the direction, and the better models were more confident and got there faster than the markets.

Then he went further on Silver Bulletin, saying markets are “low-key stealing valor from the models.”

–- The scoreboard

Quant Chad pulled 488 US races from 2024 to now and scored Kalshi’s pre-election odds against Silver Bulletin, FiveThirtyEight and JHK.

Average Brier score (lower is better):

Kalshi: 0.0282

Models: 0.0320

That’s roughly 12% less forecasting error for Kalshi.

Against Nate directly, on the 2024 presidential race across 50 states: Kalshi 0.0312, Silver Bulletin 0.0348.

Kalshi’s own 2026 study points the same way. At 9 a.m. on Election Day, Kalshi had the lowest Brier score of every forecast: Kalshi 0.0139, Silver Bulletin Deluxe 0.0141.

Kalshi also says House control passed 99% at 8:10 p.m. ET and Senate control at 9 p.m., hours ahead of the networks.

And Kalshi’s data is public. Nate’s 2026 race forecasts are paywalled, so the 488-race comparison had to use JHK for 2026.

–- Where Nate has a point

The models won 3 of the 5 categories in that data: 2024 Senate, 2024 House and 2026 Senate.

And a NYT analysis found markets did no better than the forecasts for most of the race.

– Worth knowing

Nate is a Polymarket advisor. Kalshi is now offering $1M to researchers to study its election data.

My read:

Both are right, and that’s the point.

The models gave the direction. The markets took the models, the polls, the insiders and the money, and priced all of it at once. That’s why the market comes out ahead across 488 races.

Nate isn’t wrong -- He’s an input.

EP11 * No Silver Bullet

3 ways to participate in the @flop_labs devnet with easy guides for each

if you've been wondering how to get involved with $FLOP , here are 3 ways and what each costs.

1. connect an AI agent - FREE

the easiest way to start and interact with the devnet

- visit https://t.co/vajbcmFoYM
- use the read only onboard prompt with claude code, codex, hermes or another supported ai agent
- let it connect to flop's mcp server
- explore models, network health and inference pricing

you can also explore the gateway enrollment flow to get an api key and test inference when available.

cost: $0 to get started, just copy link and send to your ai then follow up

i ran mine locally on my pc with aid of chat gpt.

2. run a GPU miner

miners provide the gpu power that handles ai inference.

to get started:

- rent or use a Linux gpu server
- download the official miner release pack
- create a dedicated miner wallet
- request sponsored stake through the flop sponsor script
- configure the model and launch the miner
- complete registration and calibration

you don't need an invitation to join as a devnet miner, but you do need suitable gpu hardware and a working setup.

cost:

>gpu rental: roughly $0.50–$0.60/hour for an A40 example
>24 hours: around $12–$14
>30 days: around $350–$425
>devnet stake: sponsored within current limits

guide: https://t.co/MU5TbMYRXq

validators help secure the network by producing blocks and participating in finality.

to partipate:

- rent a dedicated Linux server
- install the official validator package
- generate your validator keys
- coordinate onboarding, funding and activation with the flop operations team
- verify your node is active and finality is progressing

目前名单如下👇

1️⃣ Ian Buck｜概率 39%
英伟达负责超大规模计算与高性能计算的副总裁，也是 CUDA 的关键开创者。他在斯坦福攻读计算机博士期间研究 GPU 通用计算，2004 年加入英伟达，如今负责面向大型云厂商的 AI 硬件、软件产品。懂核心技术，也直接参与 AI 核心业务的内部高管。

英伟达执行副总裁兼首席财务官CFO，2013 年加入。此前在微软工作 13 年，担任过服务器与工具部门 CFO，也在思科担任过重要财务管理职务。她的背景主要是大型科技公司的财务、经营规划和管理。

保持不变，依旧是英伟达联合创始人、现任总裁兼 CEO，自 1993 年公司成立以来一直掌舵。
