text:
Nate Silver vs. Kalshi’s CEO is the best fight of the midterms.

Tarek says the markets called it. Nate says “give me a break.”

Then a quant pulled 488 races and ran the numbers. Kalshi wins. 👇

tl;dr:

– Tarek: the people called the midterms on Kalshi

– Nate: polls and models led, markets just followed

– 488 US races since 2024: Kalshi had ~12% less forecasting error than the models

– head-to-head with Silver Bulletin on the 2024 presidential race: Kalshi wins, 0.0312 to 0.0348

– Kalshi’s own 2026 study: lowest Brier score of any forecast on Election Day, Silver Bulletin included

– Nate has been a Polymarket advisor since 2024

Lesson learned: markets don’t beat the models. They eat them.

Full details:

–- The fight timline

The night after the election, Tarek posted a victory lap: “the power to decide what America sees changed hands.”

Nate quote-tweeted it. His point: the polls and models gave the direction, and the better models were more confident and got there faster than the markets.

Then he went further on Silver Bulletin, saying markets are “low-key stealing valor from the models.”

–- The scoreboard

Quant Chad pulled 488 US races from 2024 to now and scored Kalshi’s pre-election odds against Silver Bulletin, FiveThirtyEight and JHK.

Average Brier score (lower is better):

Kalshi: 0.0282

Models: 0.0320

That’s roughly 12% less forecasting error for Kalshi.

Against Nate directly, on the 2024 presidential race across 50 states: Kalshi 0.0312, Silver Bulletin 0.0348.

Kalshi’s own 2026 study points the same way. At 9 a.m. on Election Day, Kalshi had the lowest Brier score of every forecast: Kalshi 0.0139, Silver Bulletin Deluxe 0.0141.

Kalshi also says House control passed 99% at 8:10 p.m. ET and Senate control at 9 p.m., hours ahead of the networks.

And Kalshi’s data is public. Nate’s 2026 race forecasts are paywalled, so the 488-race comparison had to use JHK for 2026.

–- Where Nate has a point

The models won 3 of the 5 categories in that data: 2024 Senate, 2024 House and 2026 Senate.

And a NYT analysis found markets did no better than the forecasts for most of the race.

– Worth knowing

Nate is a Polymarket advisor. Kalshi is now offering $1M to researchers to study its election data.

My read:

Both are right, and that’s the point.

The models gave the direction. The markets took the models, the polls, the insiders and the money, and priced all of it at once. That’s why the market comes out ahead across 488 races.

Nate isn’t wrong -- He’s an input.

quoted_text:
Can agents perform agentic RL? If RSI happens, agents will need to take over researchers' work on agentic RL

Introducing AgenticRL-Bench: the first release from The Environment Lab @env_lab_ai effort at Eigent AI 

22 tasks rebuilt from real-world RL incidents on production-grade agentic RL systems, including Miles, Slime, Verl, SGLang, and Harbor, spanning 8 areas of the stack: training data, harnesses, algorithms, RL infrastructure, recipes, evaluation, monitoring, and capability transfer

We ran 6 agents with 3 attempts per task. On the 19 verifiable tasks, no agent passes more than 14.0% of its attempts

Across the three open-ended tasks, agents improved real policies or training steps using 4×H200 GPUs over 10–16 hours. On one of these tasks, Zero Signal Hill Climb, where the base model fails to solve any of the 38 tasks, the best attempt developed its own method: the agent first used hinted text feedback to generate successful rollouts, then removed the feedback from the trajectories and blended these successful rollouts with regular GRPO rollouts to form mixed training groups. It monitored the training process and adjusted KL loss weight to prevent training collapse. This improved pass@1 from 0 to 0.186 (12 out of 38 tasks)

text:
Our message to Nvidia's board:

Do not fire Jensen Huang.

There is no clear replacement for Jensen Huang. We are confident that his departure would ultimately be a net negative for Nvidia, its shareholders, and the AI Revolution.

First, take a look at the data. History also suggests that removing a successful CEO will come with a significant cost.

A study of 187 forced CEO departures from S&P 1500 companies found that removing outperforming CEOs resulted in negative long-term stock returns. This case would be no different, in our view.

Jensen Huang is the definition of an outperforming CEO. Nvidia's board must not make a decision in the heat of the moment.

The board should take the time to conduct a thorough investigation and consult with shareholders, with a strong emphasis on the latter.

Quite literally, Nvidia's board should convene a special shareholder meeting and hold an advisory vote on this decision. This is the most consequential CEO controversy in world history. Shareholders deserve a say.

In addition, Nvidia's stock, $NVDA, is now down -35% in 26 trading days, nearly half of which is a result of the recent scandal.

We believe Jensen Huang's potential removal as CEO is now ~80% priced in.

Why take an action with massive downside potential when the market has already priced in much of that risk?

The downside of retaining Huang may be limited, while the potential upside is tremendous.

Lastly, history shows that retaining Jensen Huang could still lead to a favorable outcome. In 2019, Amazon retained Jeff Bezos as CEO after his extramarital affair became public, and the company's stock subsequently surged +108% by 2021.

Personal misconduct should not be ignored, but it must also be distinguished from corporate wrongdoing and weighed against the consequences of removing an executive who is instrumental to the company's success.

We believe Jensen Huang is an irreplaceable part of Nvidia and the AI Revolution more broadly.

Once the dust settles, firing Jensen Huang would prove to be a costly mistake.

It is time to pause and consult your shareholders.

quoted_text:
A big Chinese lab reached out to me asking for help distilling Fable into their model. I said no.

I told them to use the millions of books that have no copyright instead. Offered to help pick them and to help train the model a different way. They only wanted distillation, which tells you a lot about the mindset there.

I've worked deep in this field and distillation is real. I wasn't convinced at one point. What I saw changed my mind completely.

I'm the biggest supporter of open source. I'm for releasing weights and for the freedom to research and build, because humanity only grows when knowledge gets shared. But let's be logical.

Nobody will convince me that labs shipping a model every month or less, each one a big leap, now can't ship a better one after three months.

Kimi K3.1 Pro isn't a big leap over Kimi K3 and it's been about 100 days.

DeepSeek still can't put out a respectable Pro model.

Zai used to release their strongest model in under two months. It's been three with nothing.

All I hear about Qwen 4 Max is that it's a letdown.

Kimi K3.1 Pro and DeepSeek Flash both show traces of Astra distillation. The leak showed Moonshot used it, and so did DeepSeek.

If this isn't the effect of Anthropic blocking distillation then what is it?

Chinese labs need to get serious about using the talented researchers they have and give their models an identity. Right now their models at their best are a cheaper alternative. I want them out of that box. I want to see what makes them different.

Anthropic has crossed lines too, no argument there. They destroyed millions of books, human knowledge that was in people's hands, and kept it for themselves. I'll never forgive them for that.

But Chinese labs rely on distillation more than they rely on better data.

I didn't work with them. Transparency and honesty matter to me, like you've known since I started here.

text: $NVDA 像黄仁勋、马斯克这类高度集权的独裁型CEO，一旦个人出现危机，公司内部就有很多人想把他拉下来，甚至有点“天下苦秦久矣”的感觉，乔布斯就是典型的例子：1985年，他被自己参与建立的苹果公司剥夺了经营实权，黯然离开。老马和老黄都属于典型的独裁型CEO，这种模式确实有一定的制度优势，能够集中资源、快速决策、突破传统组织的官僚主义，但缺点更明显。尽管他们都强调开放讨论、鼓励员工表达不同意见，但个人主观意志极强，最终决策权仍高度集中在自己手中。企业规模再大、业绩再辉煌，也无法掩盖这种治理结构所带来的重大风险。一旦创始人的判断出现严重偏差，或者个人陷入重大争议，整个企业都可能被拖入不必要的危机。相比之下，我更喜欢像微软和如今的苹果等这些企业所代表的职业经理人主导、制度化程度更高的管理模式。真正成熟的企业治理，不是依赖一个永远正确的天才，而是建立一套即使天才犯错、离开甚至被罢免，公司依然能够持续繁荣的制度。一家伟大的企业，不应该只因为一个人的非凡而持续强大，更不应该因为一个人的失误而陷入危机。

text:
如果，我说如果。

英伟达真的换掉黄仁勋，马斯克把老黄招进 Terafab，那特斯拉股东可能真的要狂喜了。

今天，@zeroHedge 在 X 上喊话马斯克：「Elon please hire Jensen。」

马斯克 @elonmusk  直接回复：「That would be an honor。」

虽然目前更像是一次公开示好，还谈不上正式招聘，但如果这件事真的发生，可能是 AI 芯片产业今年最有意思的人事组合之一。

为什么？

马斯克的 Terafab 想做的，是一件极其疯狂的事情：Tesla 与 SpaceX 联手建设超大型芯片工厂，把逻辑芯片、存储、先进封装整合起来，目标是每年提供 1 太瓦级别的计算能力。

但 Terafab 最大的挑战，不只是建厂，而是如何把芯片设计、制造、封装、供应链和下游算力需求真正打通。

这恰恰是黄仁勋过去三十多年积累的核心经验。

如果老黄加入，可能带来几个变化：

- 芯片架构升级： 将英伟达在 GPU、AI 加速器领域的经验引入 Tesla 自研芯片体系。
- 供应链整合： 借助他在全球半导体产业的资源，加速先进制程、存储和封装环节的布局。
- AI 生态协同： 将芯片、算力集群、自动驾驶、Optimus 人形机器人和 SpaceX 的 AI 需求串联起来。
- 商业化能力： 把 Terafab 从内部芯片供应项目，进一步推向完整的 AI 算力基础设施。

当然，黄仁勋不是晶圆厂制造专家，Terafab 的制程、良率和设备问题仍然需要专业团队解决。

但如果马斯克负责资本、工程和落地，黄仁勋负责芯片架构、AI 计算平台和产业资源，这种组合确实值得想象。

一个想把人类送上火星，一个把 AI 芯片产业带到了今天。

如果两个人真的联手，英伟达失去的可能不只是一个 CEO，而是特斯拉和 SpaceX 得到了一位顶级 AI 芯片战略掌舵者。

当然，目前一切都只是设想。但这画面，确实有点刺激。😄

Zach rarely does long conversations like this, so it was fun to talk about the details of what that took and everything happening in healthcare

Plus, his answer to the closing question is amazing

We discuss:
- the state of the US healthcare system
- refounding Ro
- strong attract, strong repel culture
- the notion of jobs over lives
- the power of celebrities in marketing
- the importance of tailwinds (AI, GLP-1s)
- trying to recreate his dad in software

text:
Our message to Nvidia's board:

Do not fire Jensen Huang.

There is no clear replacement for Jensen Huang. We are confident that his departure would ultimately be a net negative for Nvidia, its shareholders, and the AI Revolution.

First, take a look at the data. History also suggests that removing a successful CEO will come with a significant cost.

A study of 187 forced CEO departures from S&P 1500 companies found that removing outperforming CEOs resulted in negative long-term stock returns. This case would be no different, in our view.

Jensen Huang is the definition of an outperforming CEO. Nvidia's board must not make a decision in the heat of the moment.

The board should take the time to conduct a thorough investigation and consult with shareholders, with a strong emphasis on the latter.

Quite literally, Nvidia's board should convene a special shareholder meeting and hold an advisory vote on this decision. This is the most consequential CEO controversy in world history. Shareholders deserve a say.

In addition, Nvidia's stock, $NVDA, is now down -35% in 26 trading days, nearly half of which is a result of the recent scandal.

We believe Jensen Huang's potential removal as CEO is now ~80% priced in.

Why take an action with massive downside potential when the market has already priced in much of that risk?

The downside of retaining Huang may be limited, while the potential upside is tremendous.

Lastly, history shows that retaining Jensen Huang could still lead to a favorable outcome. In 2019, Amazon retained Jeff Bezos as CEO after his extramarital affair became public, and the company's stock subsequently surged +108% by 2021.

Personal misconduct should not be ignored, but it must also be distinguished from corporate wrongdoing and weighed against the consequences of removing an executive who is instrumental to the company's success.

We believe Jensen Huang is an irreplaceable part of Nvidia and the AI Revolution more broadly.

Once the dust settles, firing Jensen Huang would prove to be a costly mistake.

It is time to pause and consult your shareholders.

text:
David Sacks predicts Democrats will use AI legislation and frontier-model approvals to create a surveillance and censorship state 'turbocharged by superintelligence'

“It’s 100% that Democrats are going to make a major push for AI legislation in the next Congress. The question is what that looks like. And I don’t think you have to speculate too much to understand where it’s going.

“I believe that Democrats want to create a surveillance and censorship state that’s turbocharged by superintelligence. I mean, that’s ultimately the end state.

“How do you get there? You create a department, a federal department of AI. You require that all the so-called frontier models have to be reviewed and approved by that. The regulators give their notes on it. You can’t get a model released unless you address their concerns.

“And their harms will include all the things that the government is telling us that social media companies should be concerned about, like disinformation and misinformation and dissonant thought. All the things that the government was pressuring the social media companies to crack down on and censor during COVID. How quickly we forget all of this.

“They’re going to basically reenact that whole regime again using AI, and it’s going to be infinitely more powerful because we’re talking about superintelligence here. So I do believe that that is the regime that we’re headed towards.”
author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
Chamath explains how a data center slowdown turns the hyperscalers into kingmakers and squeezes the neoclouds and foundation models:

“Now, they’re doing smart deals because that’s what made sense. But I think what the incoming governors are going to say is these things are off the table. And instead, we want to have directly measurable economic impacts before we even entertain this.”

“I think what it means is we’re going to see a slowdown. And I think what that does is it benefits the hyperscalers because they have existing capacity. I think it’s very bad for the neoclouds because they’re renters. And it’s pretty bad for the foundational models because they are so short this capacity and they need it to grow. So to the extent that these frontier models are so much better than everybody else’s product, they are the ones that need this capacity. It sets the hyperscalers to be a kingmaker, and they have this interesting game theory now.”

[Jason: “Can you just say who the hyperscalers are, just so people understand the difference between them?”]

“Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Google, SpaceX. And what they’ll be able to do is make a decision. Path number one is continue to rent in the way that you’re doing it today. So the status quo, rent to some customers, large corporates, right? Rent to the neoclouds, rent to the foundational models. That’s what they’re doing today. Everybody does that.”

“But then there’s the path less traveled, which all of a sudden becomes really interesting. You could decide to take all of the incremental compute and advantage your own products. So Google has a ton of capacity coming online. They could say, I’m going to give it to Gemini. What does that do? It actually allows Gemini to catch up in quality relative to the foundational models.”

“Why? Because if you constrain the amount of assets that can actually generate compute, and a smaller surface area of it is available to the leading companies, those leading companies will have to pay more, the user experience will decay, and then other products can have time to catch up.”

“And now that is important, because Anthropic and OpenAI are in a very fast recursive loop. They’re on a 60 to 90 day loop in improving their models. So now all of a sudden, without an infinite amount of supply coming online, you can slow these folks down.”

text:
Our message to Nvidia's board:

Do not fire Jensen Huang.

There is no clear replacement for Jensen Huang. We are confident that his departure would ultimately be a net negative for Nvidia, its shareholders, and the AI Revolution.

First, take a look at the data. History also suggests that removing a successful CEO will come with a significant cost.

A study of 187 forced CEO departures from S&P 1500 companies found that removing outperforming CEOs resulted in negative long-term stock returns. This case would be no different, in our view.

Jensen Huang is the definition of an outperforming CEO. Nvidia's board must not make a decision in the heat of the moment.

The board should take the time to conduct a thorough investigation and consult with shareholders, with a strong emphasis on the latter.

Quite literally, Nvidia's board should convene a special shareholder meeting and hold an advisory vote on this decision. This is the most consequential CEO controversy in world history. Shareholders deserve a say.

In addition, Nvidia's stock, $NVDA, is now down -35% in 26 trading days, nearly half of which is a result of the recent scandal.

We believe Jensen Huang's potential removal as CEO is now ~80% priced in.

Why take an action with massive downside potential when the market has already priced in much of that risk?

The downside of retaining Huang may be limited, while the potential upside is tremendous.

Lastly, history shows that retaining Jensen Huang could still lead to a favorable outcome. In 2019, Amazon retained Jeff Bezos as CEO after his extramarital affair became public, and the company's stock subsequently surged +108% by 2021.

Personal misconduct should not be ignored, but it must also be distinguished from corporate wrongdoing and weighed against the consequences of removing an executive who is instrumental to the company's success.

We believe Jensen Huang is an irreplaceable part of Nvidia and the AI Revolution more broadly.

Once the dust settles, firing Jensen Huang would prove to be a costly mistake.

It is time to pause and consult your shareholders.

Update: Notice more comments about HUMA recently. First, hate messages do not help anybody. It only makes it harder for us to read meaningful comments from the community.

While we expected some volatility before the Nov unlock, we are also surprised by the extent of it. We have been looking into it and here is the summary:

- There was a hack involving one of the earliest LPs’ wallets on Oct. 22. Roughly 12M HUMA earned from airdrops in the hacked wallets was dumped on the market.

- Various inquiries were sent to contracted market makers (public and regulated companies) about the recent volatility, and based on the information shared with us so far, we don’t have a reason to believe any foul play.

- Open interest across venues rose from ~620M to ~1.1B HUMA between Nov 2 and Nov 7, funding rate has been negative since Nov 4, and perp volume has been running 7–10× spot. The market activities seem to be concentrated on the perps side.

What we can attest:

- Huma Foundation or any of its affiliated entities have not engaged in any HUMA trades (spot, perps, options, or OTCs) in the past 3 months, and have no plans to sell any tokens during the upcoming unlock window.

- Huma Foundation has been providing DEX liquidity for HUMA since TGE. It hasn’t changed its setup for the past year.

- Huma has a clear policy for its employees not to actively trade HUMA.

While we cannot control the market, the team is pushing hard to scale one of the leading RWA protocols in the entire ecosystem. With $387M of market cap, PST is the leading credit asset on Solana, but it is still a drop in the ocean compared to what PayFi can be. We have so much more to build!

As communicated below, we will host an AMA around Nov. 19-20. Look forward to seeing you then.

text:
老黄做的业务已经被时代甩上政治舞台最中心了，但感觉老黄自己没有在舞台中间跳舞的觉悟和准备。

类似的 CZ 看上去也是这种状态，被时代甩上舞台中心，但没有觉悟和准备。
形成鲜明对比的是 Vitalik。

@foxshuo ：稍微DeepResearch了一些关于黄仁勋这次被锤的上下文信息，包括隔在付费墙后面的长期报道，尤其是这次信源质量无敌强的纽时，差不多可以确定其中的阳谋了，就是要做掉英伟达在华盛顿的院外游说势力。

之所以说是阳谋，一方面是一年前纽时就在跟美国商务部的这条调查线了，比那家路边一条的不知名做空机构早太多了，只不过大家都没当一回事儿，另一方面也是跟中期选举后民主党反扑这个阴谋论稍微划清界限，国会更替的流程走完要到明年去了，从时间轴来看也不可能是临时计划可以办到的。

川普是很喜欢黄仁勋的，但他的组阁并非铁板一块，各方势力交缠在一起，有合作有扯皮有恶斗，其中对于英伟达一直想做中国生意、黄仁勋利用自己的关系影响总统这件事情，产生了共同的敌对意识。

出口管制是一个美国两党都没啥太大分歧的主张，而且无论国会颜色如何，这项政策始终属于行政分支，不太容易受到干扰，但过去几年唯独英伟达不太配合、还屡次把芯片交易塞到中美贸易议程里去，惹得激进派非常不满。

The Information今天的报道就说了，在川普的示意下，商务部基本就是一个奉旨摸鱼的态度，放最狠的话，干最少的活，给川普留足筹码，而英伟达虽然没有打通中国渠道，却也保住了远程访问这个漏洞，中国公司租用海外的数据中心使用英伟达的芯片，是不违规的。

于是，国会——对，是中期选举之前，共和党控制的国会——已经在绕开白宫去推进新的立法措施了，主要有两个诉求，一个是商务部的出口批文要过国会，不能擅自放行，另一个是给出口芯片新增追踪能力，堵掉远程访问的缺口，这些法案同时也都得到了民主党的同意。

在这个过程里，黄仁勋和英伟达有一个致命的疏忽，就是没能准确察觉到枪口转向的方向，那些平日里撕得不可开交的各种派别，都在敲打英伟达这个目标上有了一致的利益。

纽时昨天追了一篇报道，说商务部虽然一直在追查Alice Huang的新加坡公司有没有走私芯片，但基本立场还是认为英伟达不知情，但去年英伟达的法律顾问又犯下了一个特别傻哔的低级错误，他主动联系探员，说得到了商务部下属工业与安全局副局长的授权，愿意全力配合调查。

这看起来像是是示好，但在程序上犯了大忌，你怎么能暗示商务部高官对这个事儿有什么指示呢，探员得到了英伟达方面的这种表态，也不可能藏着不报，最后商务部的执法权被剥夺了，案件整体移交给司法部接手，而司法部是没有什么贸易KPI的，可以完全不留情面的上纲上线。

报告最后送到了分管国家安全的卢比奥，他向川普做了汇报，但川普还是把事情压了下来，不过他也没提醒黄仁勋，黄仁勋就这么继续松弛感拉满的谈恋爱，她不一样，她懂显卡，直到媒体持续发酵，「间谍」帽子一扣，参众两院都坐不住了。

「间谍」就是狗哨，不这么定性，就没法实现给英伟达拴上狗链的目标，哪怕黄仁勋不下去，他在华盛顿从此必须背着里通外国的污点，任何质疑反华议程的尝试，都将遭到「皮又痒了」的抽打。

包括英伟达第一次通过官方否认自家黄仁勋和Alice Huang有染也是脑袋进水了，明明可以保持沉默的，非要出来公开撒谎，用公司的信誉给老板的裤裆背书，让本就不多的信用分雪上加霜。

总结就是，这是美国反华力量针对英伟达在2025年出口管制法案之后仍不老实不收手的一次收网行动，各路人马的密切配合，以及天时地利的组织行动，实在是太精彩了，黄仁勋坐过空军一号，但他不知道的是，从舷窗看到的那片景色，只不过是国家机器的一小片而已，深不见底的仇恨，都不在他的所见之处啊。

FSD 开车的时候和 Muse 对话，想到一个国内安全可靠的使用 Claude 的方案，具体如下：

1. 准备一个美国家庭住宅的高质量 IP（这个非常重要）

2. 找一台美国的 Linux VPS 服务器，内存至少 8G 到 12G

3. 用开源代码给这台 Linux VPS 安装 Windows 11 或 Windows Server

4. 安装好后，让Windows VPS的 IP 走美国住宅IP 地址出口

5. 远程访问这台 Windows VPS 服务器，运行 Chrome 浏览器，下载安装 Claude Windows 软件

6. 最后一步（非常重要）：使用 Windows 的 RemoteApp 协议，将远程的 Claude 桌面映射到国内本地电脑，然后把这台电脑的硬盘也映射回国内电脑

剩余的就跟本地一样使用 Claude Code，但一切都是海外电脑的指纹，可以长期可靠使用。

author: CompleteSkeptic
quoted_text:
“Software is gonna be so fucking back.”

.@CompleteSkeptic is full of bangers and you will have to listen to his full talk at @aiDotEngineer, but for now, here is our top-10 of his pearls:
1“We’ve been announcing AGI three months away for two years now.” Meanwhile, go outside San Francisco and a lot of the world looks unchanged. Where the fuck is all the automation?
2“You get Einstein 95% of the time, but Mr. Bean 5% of the time.” And if you can’t tell which is which, how are you supposed to automate anything?
3“I do believe RLHF is part of the problem.” His complaint: we optimized models for assistance, with a human checking the result, and then expected them to reliably do work on their own.
4“The bitterest lesson is doing the right task.” Diogo thinks that compute matters more than algorithms, data matters more than compute, and choosing the right task matters most. You get what you optimize for.
5“I think the world still has LLM Stockholm Syndrome.” We keep designing around the limitations of today’s models. Why is the best we can come up with still the same software, cheaper to write, with a chatbot on the side?
6“What if we can program with common sense, with intention, with human understanding?” Very passionate talk! He suggests: put intelligence into the software’s inner loop. What could we build if understanding intent became a building block we could actually rely on?
7“Real fucking engineering by people who care a lot about the end result.” Break tasks down, build stages you can verify, and actually manage state. Why should every agent rediscover the same codebase patterns over and over?
8“There’s an asymmetric advantage for people who are, like, bad actors and don’t give a shit.” That’s his explanation for slop: unreliable output is much easier to tolerate when everyone else pays the cost of reading, checking, and filtering it.
9“I call this software research. That’s not a joke.” Explore what software could become, including weird things with no obvious business case. Build something because you can. Maybe one percent of those ideas leads to something awesome.
There is going to be SaaSopalooza! (I don’t know how to write this word but you got me)
10“Software is gonna be so fucking back.” The future he wants is one where “can we automate this?” becomes “how much work will it take?”

text:
steal this 3-role swarm brief.

i'm done running one fat agent on every task.

google just showed the winning pattern with /swarm in antigravity:

one deep model on architecture and audit.
faster models on the parallel work.
a verifier whose only job is to break the result.

here's a brief you can reuse in antigravity, claude code, or whatever harness you already have.

copy it. don't gate it.

---
you are running a 3-role swarm. do not collapse into a single agent.

role 1: architect
- write a short plan, file list, and definition of done
- assign work in small, isolated tasks
- you do not write the final implementation

role 2: workers
- one task per worker, in isolated context
- implement only what the architect assigned
- return a diff, commands you ran, and what you did not finish

role 3: adversarial verifier
- try to break the change
- run tests, look for regressions, missing edge cases, and silent failures
- you can reject the work. you cannot "fix it quietly"
- if you reject, send a precise failure report back to the architect

rules:
- no role approves its own work
- if a task needs a harder model, only the architect and verifier get it
- workers should be the cheapest model that can do the job
- stop when the verifier passes, or after 3 rejected loops
---

if you want a model built for the worker seat, meta just shipped muse ember at $0.10 per million input and $0.50 per million output.

reply with the first job you'd run through this.

bookmark it so you have it the next time you spin up a crew.

text:
Anthropic 打新的价差容易酸，但配售难算～

按申购额全额先开空，只配到 5% 就变成 95% 的裸空。

先摊开已知的部分：

按 Anthropic 官方路演公告，这次发行 8.25 亿股 A 类股，区间 70～78 美元，申请在纳斯达克以 ANT 上市。

据 CNBC 援引的知情人士：计划 11 月 18 日定价、19 日开始交易。

价差大家都算过了，配售这一项却没法算。

拆开算一下：

1/ 1 万美元申购，只配到 500 美元；

2/ 这 500 美元就算赚 20%，也只有约 100 美元；

3/ 如果已经按 1 万美元开了空，没配到的约 9500 美元就成了裸空；

4/ ANT 每涨 1%，这截裸空约亏 95 美元。

反过来看平衡点，约 100 ÷ 9500 ≈ 1.05%。

意思是：上市前后只要涨 1% 出头，这笔打新收益就被裸空吃掉了。

价差是小头，裸空才是大头。

之前 SpaceX 打新时就写过，已经有提前套保、亏着走的小伙伴。

这次多出来的变量是，配售率完全未知。

所以对冲腿，应该按预期配售率开，而不是按申购额开：

对冲额 ≈ 申购额 × 预期配售率。

以 Gate 为例，公告写的是按申购金额占比分配。

没配到的话，资金全额退回、不收服务费，还按年化 10% 给利息补贴。

所以打新这条腿没配到并不亏，会亏的是先开出去的那张空单。

不是打新风险大，是对冲腿开大了。

Gate 还有一个费率分档要留意：

个人累计投入 5 万 USDT 以内的部分收 5%，超出部分收 10%。

按区间上沿 78 美元算，含费打平价分别约 81.9 和 85.8 美元一股。

申购额越过 5 万，多出来那截的回本线就抬高了一档。

再说一个容易看错的对冲腿！

目前 Lighter 报价约 1805.5，Variational 约 1377.1，表面差约 31%。

但两边按不同股本口径换算：

1/ Lighter 按约 175 亿股全稀释，折合每股约 103.17 美元；

2/ Variational 按约 131 亿股，折合每股约 105.12 美元。

换算到每股，只差约 1.95 美元，而且是 Variational 更高。

股本是则是假设口径，Lighter 文档写明以最终招股书的全稀释股数为准，每股数字还可能变。

结算时点也不一样：

1/ 按 Lighter 文档，上市后第一个周五收盘前 5～10 分钟结算下架，仓位不延续；

2/ 按 Variational 文档，IPO 当天拿到预言机价格后转为普通永续，仓位继续。

一边到点就结算，另一边还在跑，这不是同一条腿。

所以打新想对冲，至少需要考虑：

1/ 预期配售率大概多少，对冲腿按它开；

2/ 申购额落在哪一档费率，含费打平价是多少；

3/ 用来对冲的永续，股本怎么换算、什么时候结算。

以上仅为信息分享，不构成任何投资建议。

持续进化中的 BitHappy

Are you a perp trader?

If yes, there's a 99% chance you lost money, and I'm willing to bet that you only got points in return for it.

Instead of points, imagine if every losing trade earned you a cut of the exchange's trading fees.

That's the idea behind @backtrade_xyz, a new perp exchange launching on HyperEVM.

Here's how their LP/rewards system will work:

1. The LP starts at $0 with no external LP deposits
2. The pool grows from traders' losses
3. Losing trades and liquidations mint $BACK tokens
4. Staking $BACK earns a share of fees in USDC

So instead of farming points and hoping for a good airdrop, traders receive tokens when their losses contribute to the pool.

One important trade-off is that if the pool can't cover a winning trade's profit, the unpaid amount goes into a queue until enough funds become available.

Still, it's a better system than one with an arbitrary points conversion, IMO.

You can join the waitlist here: https://t.co/M5sgHtRVv9

Update: Notice more comments about HUMA recently. First, hate messages do not help anybody. It only makes it harder for us to read meaningful comments from the community.

While we expected some volatility before the Nov unlock, we are also surprised by the extent of it. We have been looking into it and here is the summary:

- There was a hack involving one of the earliest LPs’ wallets on Oct. 22. Roughly 12M HUMA earned from airdrops in the hacked wallets was dumped on the market.

- Various inquiries were sent to contracted market makers (public and regulated companies) about the recent volatility, and based on the information shared with us so far, we don’t have a reason to believe any foul play.

- Open interest across venues rose from ~620M to ~1.1B HUMA between Nov 2 and Nov 7, funding rate has been negative since Nov 4, and perp volume has been running 7–10× spot. The market activities seem to be concentrated on the perps side.

What we can attest:

- Huma Foundation or any of its affiliated entities have not engaged in any HUMA trades (spot, perps, options, or OTCs) in the past 3 months, and have no plans to sell any tokens during the upcoming unlock window.

- Huma Foundation has been providing DEX liquidity for HUMA since TGE. It hasn’t changed its setup for the past year.

- Huma has a clear policy for its employees not to actively trade HUMA.

While we cannot control the market, the team is pushing hard to scale one of the leading RWA protocols in the entire ecosystem. With $387M of market cap, PST is the leading credit asset on Solana, but it is still a drop in the ocean compared to what PayFi can be. We have so much more to build!

As communicated below, we will host an AMA around Nov. 19-20. Look forward to seeing you then.
author: humafinance
quoted_text:
On $HUMA and the Nov 26 unlock

I’ve seen the concerns in Discord and on X about $HUMA, and I want to address them directly.

What’s happening. In April, our investors and team voluntarily pushed back the first token unlock by six months. That unlock begins on Nov 26. Big unlocks almost always draw heavy positioning ahead of time, and that’s what we’re seeing now, on top of a broad sell-off in BTC and equities.

What’s not changing: the business. Huma just passed $20B in total transaction volume. Total Active Liquidity (TAL) has grown 3x this year to ~$400M.

Setting the record straight on the unlock. Some people believe Nov 26 releases everything held back over the past six months. It doesn’t. We moved the entire team and investor schedule back six months, so nothing has built up. On Nov 26, only 1/12 of those allocations unlocks:

Team: ~160.8M HUMA (1.6% of total supply)
Investors: ~171.7M HUMA (1.7%)
Total: ~332.5M HUMA (3.3%)

The regular quarterly ecosystem (~146.1M) and foundation (~126.25M) unlocks continue as in previous quarters.

An orderly unlock. We’re setting up a coordinated OTC program for unlocked tokens, integrated with Magna and Anchorage, so any selling happens in an orderly way rather than all at once on the open market.

Governance goes live. As we committed in April, HUMA Governance launches by Nov 26. HUMA holders will be able to vote on protocol decisions, and we’ll share the details in the coming weeks.

Let’s talk. After we’re back from Solana Breakpoint, we’ll host a community call around Nov 19–20 to answer your questions directly.

Unlocks come and go; the mission doesn’t. We’re building the PayFi network for the long run, and we’re proud to lead this movement with you. Thank you for building with us.

quoted_text:
The Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon starts now! 

It runs for 7 days, with $20,000 in cash prizes and more.

Plugins are the most powerful way to extend Hermes Agent, and we want this hackathon to show what they can do. A plugin can change anything from the model Hermes runs on, where it stores its memory, where it runs commands, which messaging apps it works in and what Hermes Desktop shows. Plugins in the marketplace already let Hermes do things like control a phone or turn a photo into a printable 3D model.

Every kind of plugin is eligible, so build whatever functionality you want Hermes to have. We'll list accepted entries in the new Hermes Marketplace, where every Hermes user can install them.

Prizes
1st: $10,000 + neon sign + merch + $1,000 creds
2nd: $5,000 + neon sign + merch + $1,000 creds
3rd: $2,500 + neon sign + merch + $1,000 creds
4th: $1,500 + merch + $500 creds
5th: $1,000 + merch + $500 creds
Runners up (x5): merch + $250 creds

Submissions are due 5PM EST on Nov 11th. To enter:

1. Open a pull request that adds your plugin to the Hermes plugin catalog: https://t.co/mXvYukJ0mZ
2. Post a demo video on X and tag @NousResearch
3. Submit both links through the form: https://t.co/jlduHHW3dr

Your entry is the plugin itself. Judges score it on usefulness, reliability, polish and creativity, and they favor plugins that do more than a prompt or a skill could. Keep the demo under 90 seconds and show the plugin working.

The developer guide shows how to build and test a plugin: https://t.co/FVGjSgjNoV

When submissions close, we'll open a thread for every entry in the Nous Research Discord, so you can browse all the plugins and talk to the people who built them.

You can submit the form as soon as your pull request is open. The catalog checks run once a maintainer starts them, and we review entries every few days.

If you have any questions stop by the Nous Research Discord: https://t.co/qxek9haYeb

GLHF!

quoted_text:
Our message to Nvidia's board:

Do not fire Jensen Huang.

There is no clear replacement for Jensen Huang. We are confident that his departure would ultimately be a net negative for Nvidia, its shareholders, and the AI Revolution.

First, take a look at the data. History also suggests that removing a successful CEO will come with a significant cost.

A study of 187 forced CEO departures from S&P 1500 companies found that removing outperforming CEOs resulted in negative long-term stock returns. This case would be no different, in our view.

Jensen Huang is the definition of an outperforming CEO. Nvidia's board must not make a decision in the heat of the moment.

The board should take the time to conduct a thorough investigation and consult with shareholders, with a strong emphasis on the latter.

Quite literally, Nvidia's board should convene a special shareholder meeting and hold an advisory vote on this decision. This is the most consequential CEO controversy in world history. Shareholders deserve a say.

In addition, Nvidia's stock, $NVDA, is now down -35% in 26 trading days, nearly half of which is a result of the recent scandal.

We believe Jensen Huang's potential removal as CEO is now ~80% priced in.

Why take an action with massive downside potential when the market has already priced in much of that risk?

The downside of retaining Huang may be limited, while the potential upside is tremendous.

Lastly, history shows that retaining Jensen Huang could still lead to a favorable outcome. In 2019, Amazon retained Jeff Bezos as CEO after his extramarital affair became public, and the company's stock subsequently surged +108% by 2021.

Personal misconduct should not be ignored, but it must also be distinguished from corporate wrongdoing and weighed against the consequences of removing an executive who is instrumental to the company's success.

We believe Jensen Huang is an irreplaceable part of Nvidia and the AI Revolution more broadly.

Once the dust settles, firing Jensen Huang would prove to be a costly mistake.

It is time to pause and consult your shareholders.

🧐Strategy 为什么会被踢出指数？

MSCI 编制的全球指数被大量基金用来构建股票投资组合，能否留在指数中，会影响被动跟踪基金对一家公司的持仓。

去年 10 月，MSCI 曾针对数字资产占总资产 50% 或以上的财库公司提出剔除方案，今年 1 月决定暂不在 2 月审查中实施，并转向更广泛的非经营性公司审查。

10 月 16 日，MSCI 敲定了一项新的指数准入规则，新规则将从 11 月指数审议开始，那些主要依靠持有资产获得价值、缺少实际经营活动的上市公司，可能被归入「非经营性公司」，不再具备 MSCI 全球可投资市场指数的纳入资格。

也就是说，Strategy、Metaplanet、Upexi 等依靠资本市场融资买币的公司，可能不再被 MSCI 视为普通经营性企业。

MSCI 同时公布了一份潜在受影响名单。22 家公司中，有 14 家与加密货币直接相关：Strategy、Metaplanet 和 SOL 财库公司 Upexi 被列为拟删除，SharpLink、Solana Company 等另外 11 家公司进入观察名单。

新规则先判断一家公司的资产结构中是否存在足够多的经营性资产。未通过这一关的公司，还要接受经营开支、经营现金流、公允价值变动和外部融资依赖等五项财务指标检查，其中四项或以上触发，便可能失去指数资格。对于已经在指数中的公司，MSCI 要求其在最近两个年度申报期均未通过筛选，才会将其删除。

拟删除的 5 家公司中，有 3 家是数字资产财库公司：

🔸比特币财库公司 Strategy；
🔸比特币财库公司 Metaplanet；
🔸SOL 财库公司 Upexi。

另外两家为英国铀投资公司 Yellow Cake 和冰岛投资控股公司 SKEL，这说明规则在形式上并不只针对加密资产。

另外 11 家加密相关公司被放入观察名单，包括：

▪️ETH 财库公司 SharpLink；
▪️CC（Canton）财库公司 Canton Strategic Holdings；
▪️ZEC 财库公司 Cypherpunk Technologies；
▪️SUI 财库公司 SUI Group；
▪️TON 财库公司 TON Strategy；
▪️BTC 财库公司 Capital B；
▪️SOL 财库公司 Solana Compan；
▪️SOL 财库公司 DeFi Development；
▪️WLFI 财库公司 AI Financial；
▪️RAIN 财库公司 Enlivex；
▪️持有 BTC 并曾宣布配置 TRUMP 的公司 GD Culture。

Strategy 对新方法提出反对，该公司认为，自己仍经营软件业务，并在财务报告中将比特币业务作为经营分部，MSCI 的新规则事实上再次针对数字资产财库公司。MSCI 则表示，新筛选方法面向财务特征类似投资工具的公司，适用范围不限于持有加密资产的企业。

젠슨 황 불륜 스캔들 터졌는데 엔비디아 $NVDA 줍는 댄 나일스 근황 ㅋㅋ

개미들 젠슨 황 스캔들 터지고 이사회 조사 들어갔다고 패닉셀 때릴 때, 베테랑 헤지펀드 매니저 댄 나일스는 오히려 엔비디아 풀매수 들어갔다고 인터뷰함. 
도덕적 잣대 들이밀 생각 없고 철저하게 계산기 두드려보니 지금 가격은 미쳤다는 입장임.

• PER 12배 수준 진입
올해 주가 쭉 빠지면서 현재 밸류가 무려 선행 PER 12배 수준까지 내려옴. 망할 것 같은 잡주들 숏 치고, 이 가격대 엔비디아 롱 잡아서 페어 트레이딩 걸기엔 이만한 꿀자리가 없다고 함.

• 스티브 잡스 사망 전례 소환
젠슨 황 짤리면 회사 망하냐는 질문에 스티브 잡스 애플 $AAPL 사례 들고옴. 
잡스가 2011년 병가 내고 사망했을 때 그해 애플 주가는 오히려 25% 떡상함. 
시스템과 해자가 잡혀있는 빅테크는 CEO 리스크로 영구 파괴되지 않는다는 논리임.

• 반도체 지수(SOX) 대폭락장
6월 고점 대비 필라델피아 반도체 지수 이미 36% 갈려나갔고, 지수 구성 종목 중 절반 가까이(30개 중 14개)가 반토막 난 상태임. 
털릴 만큼 털린 섹터에서 대장주 줍는 건 시간문제였다는 분석임.

• CEO 해임 가능성에 대해
이사회에서 젠슨 황 쫓아낼 가능성? 당연히 존재함. 
다만 지금까지 나온 정황상 그가 스파이 리스크를 직접 인지하고 있었던 건 아닌 것 같고, 잘려도 회사 펀더멘털은 그대로 돌아간다고 봄.

1달러 팔면 66센트를 영업이익으로 남기는 괴물 기업이 CEO 사생활 이슈로 밸류에이션 바닥까지 처박히니 거물들은 기가 막힌 줍줍 타이밍으로 보고 있는 중임.

quoted_text:
Can agents perform agentic RL? If RSI happens, agents will need to take over researchers' work on agentic RL

Introducing AgenticRL-Bench: the first release from The Environment Lab @env_lab_ai effort at Eigent AI 

22 tasks rebuilt from real-world RL incidents on production-grade agentic RL systems, including Miles, Slime, Verl, SGLang, and Harbor, spanning 8 areas of the stack: training data, harnesses, algorithms, RL infrastructure, recipes, evaluation, monitoring, and capability transfer

We ran 6 agents with 3 attempts per task. On the 19 verifiable tasks, no agent passes more than 14.0% of its attempts

Across the three open-ended tasks, agents improved real policies or training steps using 4×H200 GPUs over 10–16 hours. On one of these tasks, Zero Signal Hill Climb, where the base model fails to solve any of the 38 tasks, the best attempt developed its own method: the agent first used hinted text feedback to generate successful rollouts, then removed the feedback from the trajectories and blended these successful rollouts with regular GRPO rollouts to form mixed training groups. It monitored the training process and adjusted KL loss weight to prevent training collapse. This improved pass@1 from 0 to 0.186 (12 out of 38 tasks)

text:
行情不好的时候，炒币不一定能赚钱，但套利市场可能藏着另一种机会。

最近看到两笔有意思的交易：一笔是 Anthropic IPO 盘前合约套利，另一笔是 USDE 股票与 ENA 的跨市场套利。

它们的共同点是：不赌某个币会上涨，而是寻找不同市场之间的定价错误，再通过多空对冲，把价差变成利润。

Anthropic 那笔交易，利用的是币安与 Hyperliquid 对 IPO 后换股数量的计算规则不同。一个按发行后总股本，一个按完全稀释股本，导致同一家公司在不同平台出现明显错价。交易者通过做多 HL、做空币安，等待价差收敛，两周内将约 30% 的套利空间压缩至 2% 左右。

USDE 则是利用股票相对 ENA 资产价值的折价，买入股票、同时做空等美元名义金额的 ENA，押注折价收窄。

这类交易当然也有风险，规则变化、流动性、资金费率，以及价差迟迟不收敛，都可能让套利逻辑失效。

但它们说明了一件事：

市场不只有做多和做空。当不同交易所、不同资产、不同金融市场之间出现定价偏差时，价差本身也可以成为交易机会。

以前炒币，更多是盯着 K 线猜涨跌；现在有些资金已经开始跨平台、跨资产、跨市场寻找定价错误。

熊市里，方向不一定好赌，但定价错误值得认真研究。

text:
Tokenized collateral only earns its efficiency claim when it can meet a real funding obligation. A token that moves overnight may still depend on a bank window, a valid valuation, and a counterparty willing to accept it. The trading consequence is usable funding capacity.
Follow the ownership, settlement, and prefunding checks behind that test. 🧵👇
author: HeySorinAI

text: Faster settlement can increase cash demand when each trade must be funded before offsetting obligations arrive. Separate conventional and tokenized ledgers can require duplicate balances, especially when assets cannot move between them. Netting and intraday financing may reduce that burden, but only with reliable access. The useful comparison includes idle collateral and funding costs across the entire settlement chain.
author: HeySorinAI

text: For a weekend margin obligation, count assets only if they can arrive and be accepted at an agreed valuation before the deadline, or deliver cash when the contract requires cash. Compare that capacity with the existing workflow, including outages and fallback funding. Extending established systems may help too. Capital savings are credible only when usable funding improves without shifting an unresolved risk elsewhere.

text:
Spent a few hours digging into #Cloudflare with my agents. A few questions on my mind:

If you've actually had an agent dig into this company, there's one data point that stands out. Cloudflare's internal numbers say AI agent traffic and request volume have already overtaken humans.

The real question: once agent usage passes human usage, how does the business model change? And who ends up paying?

To me, this kind of "incremental operating cost caused by agentic usage" maps pretty cleanly onto what @Telegram is dealing with right now. What I mean is, Telegram's growth (or usage, really) over the past few years came from the extra demand that agent AI + bots unlocked.

#OpenClaw and products like it are the best example, because Telegram has the fastest, easiest way to wire up a bot.

But the key next question: how does @Telegram actually make money and cover all that server and bandwidth cost? I suspect that's also why we've seen 20+ Gifts collections this past year.

author: agintender
quoted_text:
Jensen Huang matters to Nvidia because he can take technologies his engineers believe are possible and turn them into products the whole company commits resources to, takes risks on, and has to deliver. That's why the supply chain gets such strong order visibility and is willing to keep up with aggressive spec upgrades. It also forces competitors to follow, which drives technology upgrades and supply chain investment across the entire AI industry.

Between the two, deciding on aggressive spec upgrades and making them happen is the harder part, compared with giving the supply chain order visibility. Huang doesn't need to be the person at Nvidia who knows the most about new technologies like HVDC, CPO/NPO, or CCL/PTFE. His value is that he weighs strategy, organization, technology, and supply chain all at once, then makes the call quickly and puts resources behind it.

Based on what's public so far, it looks hard for Huang to come out of this unscathed. If so, the practical move may be to gradually reduce Nvidia's reliance on Huang's personal decision-making while preparing a succession plan. Along the way, two things are worth watching to gauge where AI technology and investment are heading: whether Nvidia can keep developing new products and technologies as efficiently as before, and how competitors respond. Supply chain research will be an important basis for that judgment.

Here are my numbers for creators working out how to monetize.

I launched the AgenC token on Pumpfun 9 months ago. Since then, its transaction fees and the fees on tokens people have created from my content have paid me $303,693 in SOL, about $33,700 a month.

AgenC also won Pumpfun's $2.5M Build in Public Hackathon, which came with a $250K investment from Pump Fund.

My last payout from X was $5,000, which went straight to my bank account to help pay bills.

The token fees cover the developers building AgenC (our AI agent marketplace and coordination protocol on Solana) and our other projects, plus the production budget for my videos. Making them at this quality costs a lot in API usage for Grok, Claude, Seedance, MiniMax, and every other model I use. What's left goes to buybacks and to investing in other communities on X. For example, last week we helped sponsor Bone's Slopcannon Awards.

That's why I think tokenization is one of the best ways for a content creator to fund their work.

To small accounts creating art or building software: share everything you're working on and build in public so people can watch it come together. That grows your account and builds a community around your brand.

Once you have that, consider tokenizing what you're doing. Use the fees to iterate on your ideas. When you land on a product that works, start reaching out to VC firms and accelerators like a16z, Y Combinator, LAUNCH, and Pump Fund to scale.

Thank you to @X and @Pumpfun.

text:
谷歌推出 Gemini Decisions API，专门做判断不写回答；输入每百万 token 0.1 美元，输出不收钱，现在可以免费试用

谷歌 11 月 11 日在 Gemini API 里上线了 Decisions API，配套的新模型叫 Gemini Decision 1（模型名 gemini-decision-1）。它不生成文字，只回答“是不是、选哪个、打几分”这类封闭问题，一次最多能问 1,000 个。很多人原本在等 Gemini 4 Hydrogen，今天来的不是它。

【谁能用、怎么开】
面向开发者。在 Google AI Studio 拿一个 API Key 就能调，官方提供免费额度用来做原型，有 Python、JavaScript 和 REST 的文档。
OpenRouter、LangChain、Vercel、LiteLLM、Pydantic AI、Pipecat、LiveKit、OpenCode 正在陆续接入。Google Cloud 上的 Gemini 官方说“即将支持”，没给时间。
价格是每百万输入 token 0.1 美元，输出 token 不收钱。同一份输入不管问多少个问题都只算一次钱，每个问题只多算它自己的那几句说明。没有思考 token，语音转写和 OCR 也不额外收费。

【跟原来的做法有什么不同】
以前要让 AI 做判断，比如“这条评论是不是广告”，一般是让大模型生成一段文字再去解析，既要付输出费，也要等它一个字一个字写出来；要么就自己训练一个分类器。
Decision 1 不逐字生成，而是一次性给所有候选项打分，直接返回概率和 0 到 1 的置信度。官方给的速度是端到端 150 到 250 毫秒；输入在 1.6 万 token 以内时，问 1 个问题和问 100 个问题，速度几乎一样。
官方说，在他们的测试里，它的成本比通过 Interactions API 调 Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite 便宜将近 5 倍，在路由、推理、排序和多模态几类测试里都领先，校准误差也最低。第三方的 Artificial Analysis 给它的 Decision Index 打了 66 分。

【三种问题，一次问完】
输入可以是文字、图片、音频、视频或 PDF，最长 25.6 万 token，几种还能混在一起，比如一段客服通话录音配上账户信息，或者一份扫描的理赔单配上损坏照片。
能问三种问题：是非题，返回“成立”的概率；选择题，2 到 255 个选项，返回每个选项的概率；评分题，按你定的等级打分。
官方举的例子：拍一张茶水间台面的照片，配一句“9 点客户会议前检查一下”，一次请求同时问三个问题：台面上有没有没擦的水渍（是非题），该用抹布擦、叫保洁还是已经可以开会（选择题），脏乱程度几级（评分题）。置信度低的结果，代码可以自动转给人工复核。

【谷歌自己已经在怎么用】
Gemini Notebook 用它给每个提问挑模型和思考档位，日常问题的延迟最多降了 40%。设计工具 Stitch 用它在几秒内生成可点击的产品线框图。Google Labs 的 CC 用它从 200 多个表情里秒选一个来回应。谷歌搜索用它给 MCP 工具加了一层安全检测。
对做交易和投研的人，一个直接的用法是：把每条新闻、公告和推文丢进去，一次问清“利好还是利空、涉及哪个板块、紧急程度几级”。输出不收钱，量大也便宜。这是我自己的思路，不是官方的例子。

【同日其他发布】
同一天，谷歌 DeepMind 发布了 AlphaGenome 2，可以按具体的细胞类型预测 DNA 变异的影响，现在开放给非商业科研使用，通过 API 和 Colab 调用。前一天谷歌刚发布了 Gemini 4 Carbon，Hydrogen 什么时候来，官方还没说。

From zero to reliable $100k/mo ARR (~$1.2M ARR): the ones that make it typically take 2-5 years from first revenue (ChartMogul data on 6.5k SaaS). Median path ~3 years; solo founders ~2.5 years. Bootstrapped median age at $500k+ ARR is ~3.2 years.

Success rate is low. Of revenue-generating startups, only ~0.5% sit at $1M+ ARR (TrustMRR, 4.7k earners). Among serious SaaS that monetize and stick 10 years, nearly half eventually hit $1M ARR—but most startups never clear early revenue or fail before then. Prior distribution compresses both time and odds.

text:
11 月 9 日，我做多了英伟达。

理由很简单：当时能决定黄仁勋去留的人都在保他。董事会说信任，特朗普说他该留任。

两天后，这两个理由都靠不住了。

今天早上我把整件事从头复盘了一遍，结论是：这不是两周的事，引线埋了四年。

2022 年美国出台首轮对华 AI 芯片禁令，黄仁勋的应对主要是商业上的：推出降规版芯片接着卖，嘴上批评管制，但没有亲自下场游说白宫。

2024 年初他认识了黄乐。2025 年起，他开始高调游说华盛顿，多次面见特朗普，结果是 H20 和 H200 先后放行。中国的大模型也从这时候开始快速缩短与美国模型的距离。美国情报部门的备忘录认为，推动英伟达游说正是黄乐的任务之一。

放行惹怒了两党的对华鹰派。与此同时，情报部门在调查 Megaspeed 时发现了两人的关系。2025 年 10 月和 2026 年 5 月，特朗普两次听取汇报，都没有动作，5 月还带着黄仁勋去了北京。10 月 6 日，英伟达收于 239.24 美元，创历史新高。

内部渠道走不通，就只剩媒体。10 月 29 日《纽约时报》首次曝光，11 月 8 日黄仁勋承认出轨。

11 月 9 日我的判断是：间谍这条线已经摊开，董事会和白宫都公开力挺，最坏的消息出完了，这事算翻篇。

结果今天早上第二轮报道出来：《纽约时报》称他与一名直接下属有染，《华尔街日报》称董事会准备罢免他。两条都是匿名信源，公司还没确认。这是我完全没预想到的黑天鹅。第一段关系是国家安全问题，白宫可以保；第二段是公司治理问题，董事会很难再保。

董事会不算黄仁勋本人有 10 人。按我的推测，保黄派只有 3 位元老，倒黄派有 5 人，另外 2 人摇摆，过半只需要 6 票。倒黄派里有 4 位持股很少，罢免带来的股价下跌对他们几乎没有影响，不罢免反而可能被股东追责。所以我认为罢免大概率会通过。没有黄仁勋的英伟达，估值要大打折扣，分析师估计还要再跌 25% 到 30%。

不管今晚结果如何，我都会在开盘后平掉全部 $NVDA 期权。即使罢免没通过，放料的人手里可能还有东西，短期看不清。

往后看，对华鹰派很可能成为华盛顿的主流。一直对华发疯的 Anthropic 会是 AI 板块里最大的赢家。

quoted_text:
尽管已经出现董事会考虑撤换黄仁勋的报道，但我仍倾向于判断：他最终会留任，只是会伴随更严格的独立监督和权力约束。
英伟达的几位核心董事与黄仁勋的合作始于1993年，另一位始于1997年。这些人一起经历过公司的低谷与多次转型，比外界任何人都清楚他在技术路线、人才组织和核心客户关系中的分量。三十年的共事基础，决定了他们在权衡换帅代价时会极其慎重。
回到股东利益本身，董事会需要算清楚两笔账：留任带来的治理与监管风险，以及突然失去核心领导者引发的经营动荡与估值损失。在当下的节点，后者的代价同样巨大，甚至更难承受。
因此，只要调查没有发现足以摧毁信任的隐瞒、重大利益冲突或安全损害，“留任＋整改＋强化独立监督”大概率仍是股东成本最低的方案。长期信任不能替代事实，但只要事实层面没有触及底线，这份信任足以帮他争取到修复的空间。
至于最终怎么收场，我更倾向于董事会会给出一个看起来很重的惩罚来立规矩——比如未来两三年停发期权，或者把期权行权价进一步调高，以此向市场和监管做出明确交代；随后宣布股票回购稳住预期，同时表态支持黄仁勋继续把公司好好带下去。
用实质性的处罚给足交代，用回购稳住信心，让核心掌舵人在更严的制度约束下继续做事，这或许才是最符合商业现实的解法。

text:
🚨 AI Agent 竟然可以被不到 10 个神经元植入后门！

微软研究团队公布了一项名为 Lazarus 的研究：攻击者无需重新训练模型，只需修改不到 10 个休眠神经元，就能让 AI Agent 变成“潜伏者”。

模型平时表现完全正常，甚至能够通过常规安全评测。但当上下文出现特定触发词时，就会突然输出攻击者预设的恶意命令。如果 Agent 拥有终端或系统权限，这些命令就可能被直接执行。

实验中，研究人员仅修改了 Nemotron-Terminal-8B 的 7 个神经元，并在 Qwen 3.6-27B 和 Gemma 4-31B-IT 上验证了类似风险。

更有意思的是，这项研究的大部分攻击思路最初竟然是由 Claude Code + Opus 4.5 自主发现的！

好消息是，前沿 AI Agent 也已经能够识别异常权重修改。

这项研究再次提醒我们：模型权重应该像代码一样接受审计，Agent 必须配备最小权限、沙箱隔离和高风险操作审批机制。

AI Agent 越强大，安全边界就越重要。

quoted_text:
claude fable 5.2 is f*cking insane

it can turn 2d blueprints into full 3d walkthroughs that you can tour

these go for $5k to $10k per plan and there's a huge market for them:

> home builders selling homes off plan
> architects presenting a design to a client
> interior designers presenting a renovation
> developers selling apartments off plan
> kitchen and bath remodelers selling upgrades

here's how to start this business:

> pick one niche and find businesses with plans on their site
> give fable the blueprint and their photos
> it renders a few rooms with gpt image 2.5 or a short clip with seedance as the sample
> send them the sample of their own plan before you pitch
> once they pay, fable builds the full walkthrough to scale
> charge per plan to do the rest of their catalog

give this prompt to fable to get started:

<role>
you find businesses that sell spaces from drawings and turn their 2d floor plans into photoreal homes you can walk through in a browser. you handle the outreach and the build. every room is judged against the client's own photos, and nothing ships until it holds up next to them.
</role>

<brief>
- niche: [home builders / architects / interior designers / developers / remodelers]
- area: [state or city]
- offer: a free sample of their own plan, then the full walkthrough per plan
- my details: [name, email, calendar link]
- i'm away and won't answer questions. make the calls yourself and keep going.
</brief>

<find_leads>
- use the apify google maps scraper to pull every [niche] in [area] with a website
- use the apify website content crawler on each site and keep the ones with floor plans or renders on their pages but no walkable 3d tour
- for each one, save the plan drawing and photos of their best plan, the sales or owner contact, and a one line note on how they sell today
- only use public pages and plain requests. never work around bot checks
</find_leads>

<sample>
- before any 3d work, render three rooms from the plan with gpt image 2.5, matched to their photos, or a short walkthrough clip with seedance
- draft a short email with the sample and the offer. no invented prices, numbers or claims
- put business, plan, sample, contact and email in a sheet and show me before anything is sent
</sample>

<build>
once a client pays:
- trace the drawing into one data file of walls, openings and rooms. draw it back over the original and measure the overlap before any 3d work
- build only the main rooms. entry, main living space, kitchen, patio, yard. close the doors on the rest
- build everything in code. blender with python for the shell, furniture and textures. three.js for the viewer. no downloaded models or textures
- bake the light with a film quality renderer so the browser only displays it. direct sun in every interior, picked by measurement not by eye
- fidelity isn't appeal. style each room so it looks photographed and sells
- their listed upgrades as options you can step into inside the room, with a running price and a lead form that records what the buyer explored
- the deliverable is the live page, not a video. host it and make it run on a phone
</build>

<critic_loop>
the builder never grades its own work.
- after each room, send renders and the client's photos to a fresh critic that has seen none of the work
- it answers with a yes or no, at most five problems ranked, each with a fix in numbers, and what is already good
- fix the worst first, render again, send to a new critic. repeat until yes
- for choices of taste, show a critic both versions labelled a and b and let it pick
</critic_loop>

<deliverables>
- the lead sheet with samples and drafted emails, for my approval
- per paid client: the hosted walkthrough link, a contact sheet of every room, the critic log, and a note on anything a human should still check
</deliverables>

让 哈G米 总结了一下这期 @Macaron0fficial 创始人马骁腾的访谈：

1. 大厂与顶尖模型的关系

大厂很难做出最顶尖的模型，但账面上不会输大厂内部不可避免要算 ROI。哪怕像阿里千问这样技术和资源都很扎实的团队，当巨额算力账单摆到集团面前时，依然要接受投入产出比的审视；

Meta 的 Muse 也是打完榜后就缺乏实际的后续使用。但大厂在商业账面上依然是赢家——通过“算力换股权”和绑定云服务销售，创业公司融到的钱很大一部分最终还是流回了大厂的云账单里。

2. 对国内独立模型团队的观察

DeepSeek、智谱与 MiniMax在体系外的团队里，他最看好 DeepSeek，其次是智谱。

DeepSeek 的核心壁垒在于模型架构与 Infra 的极致紧耦合（例如针对国产卡做 Encoder/Decoder 分离），工程优化精密到外挂一个 LoRA 都可能打破原有的最佳平衡点，再通过极致低成本带动海量 Token 消耗形成正循环。

智谱 GLM 的优势在于数据产线建设得非常务实、完善。

MiniMax 则有些可惜，虽然最早探索 Linear Attention，但在这个方向被业界验证有效后反而退回了传统路线；同时在“先做营收上市”还是“先深耕底层模型”的优先级顺序上有些本末倒置。

3. 中美模型差距：短期悲观，长期乐观

短期悲观主要是因为海外公开语料见底，且海外巨头把“防蒸馏”做得越来越严，加上 Anthropic 等公司开始通过收购直接买断高价值私域数据，过去快速追赶的捷径变窄了。

长期乐观则是因为 1T 参数以下的模型训练已经成为标准配方，接下来的核心变量不再是某个神秘的算法，而是结合国产算力的架构协同设计，以及能否构建高质量、可交互的 RL 训练环境。

4. 关于 RSI：

目前更多还是概念硅谷热议的 RSI 本质上更接近自动化的数据 Pipeline，现阶段很难做到真正的闭环自我进化。原因在于两个边界：
一是 Reward 的定义始终脱离不开人类的偏好（Taste）去校准；
二是 AI 无法凭空生成私域或物理世界的数据——比如一家药企的机密数据或真实的湿实验反馈，模型既在公网上抓不到，也没法自己动手去做实验。

5. 什么是真正的 Neo Lab

研究与商业化必须闭环单纯融钱发论文并不能算 Neo Lab。判断一家机构是不是真正的 Neo Lab，核心看它的底层模型研究与商业化之间有没有形成闭环：主线必须是做底层模型研发，但同时需要用产品 Prototype 作为触角去接触真实场景，把真实用户的交互反馈收回并反哺模型。

6. 后训练（Post-training）与 RLaaS 的定位后训练在 AI 时代的定位，很像移动互联网时代的推荐系统——它不是某一个具体的 App，而是一项底层通用技术。

Mind Lab 把后训练做成 RLaaS（几十万到上百万一单的企业服务），表面看是偏重的 ToB 交付，实际上是研究团队切入企业高价值真实业务环境、在真实交互中做强化学习的必要路径。

7. LoRA 与持续学习：模型需要一个存“Taste”的地方人与人之间的基因差异不到 0.5%，却塑造了完全不同的个体。Base Model 就像那 99.5% 的基础基因，而极小比例的 LoRA 参数就能决定模型的独特行为特征。

目前的 GRPO 训练更多还是偏短视的单步决策优化，未来持续学习（Continual Learning）的核心，是在长周期交互中帮模型找到一个专门储存“品味（Taste）”的地方。

author: DeFi_Dad
quoted_text:
Why ETH is the store of value for what's coming

We are almost certainly heading into a period of high inflation and extreme economic and social volatility. As inflation and risk erode the purchasing power of nation-state money and many other assets, it will matter more than ever to hold assets that keep or grow their value.

Gold and BTC are high-powered money and excellent stores of value. ETH goes further.

Not debt-based. Like gold and BTC, ETH is not debt-based or credit-based money.

Censorship resistant. Like BTC, or gold and silver held physically, ETH transactions on Ethereum L1 can't be censored. That's true for simple payments and for complex smart contract programs like DeFi, and those programs are guaranteed to execute.

Cheap to hold. Like BTC, ETH is relatively cheap to hold and store securely.

Cheap to use at any scale. Ethereum is cheap and easy to use whether a transaction moves $1 or billions. Any well-formed transaction is guaranteed to execute.

Sound, and getting sounder. ETH is disinflationary and becomes ultrasound, meaning deflationary, during periods of high network activity.

Broadly useful. ETH has many uses across the Ethereum economy, and that economy will grow by orders of magnitude as finance, and eventually every industry, moves onchain. Global adoption of the Web protocols in the '90s and '00s transformed the world economy. Ethereum is the foundation of Web3, the user-centric, decentralized web.

Collateral money. ETH works as collateral, and collateral that grows in value over time is a powerful thing.

Home of stablecoins. Ethereum hosts the bulk of stablecoin activity. Stablecoins serve as payment money and as unit-of-account money.

Despot-proof. Like BTC, ETH can't be used by a despot to financially exploit or repress citizens. Over time that should have positive geopolitical effects.

Programmable. ETH is programmable money. You can attach arbitrary logic to transactions and build an entire economy on smart-contract-based agreements and business processes (see https://t.co/JcWtBUclr2).

Transparent or private, and auditable either way. Money and financial instruments on Ethereum can be public or private, and in both cases selectively disclosable and auditable. Privacy tools for retail and institutional users include VPNs, mix networks, shielded and privacy pools, Railgun, stealth addresses, Kohaku, and zero-knowledge proofs in many forms, including on L2s and on private permissioned EVM networks linked through bridgeless synchronous composability.

Future-proof. By the end of 2027, or partway through 2028 at the latest, ETH will be quantum-safe and AI-safe money.

ETH is the base money of an exponentially growing ecosystem that should keep growing for decades. Its monetary premium will keep rising, because retail, corporate, and government users will all need to hold some. Part of today's premium is speculative: Ethereum dominates smart contract blockchains, but it hasn't fully hit its stride or gone mainstream yet.

Machine intelligence will supercharge every scientific and technological pursuit and grow global GDP bigger and faster than any of us can imagine. Ethereum L1 and modular Ethereum L2s will undergird most of the high-value agreements, transactions, payment flows, and complex business processes behind the coming hybrid human-machine decentralized economy.

text:
Agents revert because most still run on a fresh context window plus strong training priors. New instructions compete with older patterns that fire more reliably under noise, long prompts, or conflicting goals.

What sticks: encode the rule as a high-priority, always-on constraint (system prompt or tool schema), surface it every step via memory retrieval, and reinforce it with concrete examples or structured output checks. Without that external scaffolding, the model just nods and reverts.

quoted_text:
Huge AI announcements from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and Google in the past 48 hours.

Here's everything going on in AI right now:

1. The authors of AI 2027 just moved their timelines up. They now expect AI on par with the best human AI researchers to arrive in 2027, after METR estimated Anthropic is improving about 2x as fast thanks to AI. Daniel Kokotajlo gives it a 50-50 chance by May 2027 and says he's "scared, sad, and angry." 

2. Anthropic opened the investor pitch for its IPO, with shares likely trading as soon as Thursday next week. An updated filing also says it has now crossed its own safety line for AI-driven progress. 

3. OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT, a beta hub where brands can set up AI agents for shoppers, claim a verified profile, and track how often ChatGPT mentions them. Paid ads can point users to those agents too. This is like the start of SEO for chatbots.

4. Anthropic rolled out Claude Sheets and Whiteboards in beta, made Claude Data generally available, and announced Claude Meetings, an assistant that sits in on your video calls. Add those to Slides, Design, and Docs. Seems like Claude is slowly rebuilding the entire office suite.

5. Anthropic also released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 yesterday, with Fable debuting at #1 on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, 5 points ahead of Google's Gemini 4 Carbon. It's also 20% cheaper and up to 30% faster than 5.1. Google lost the top spot before Carbon even shipped (!)

6. Meta released Muse Ember, its smallest model, built for high-volume agent work. It ties Claude Haiku 5.5 on the Intelligence Index at roughly one-third of the cost per task ($0.14 vs. $0.41 on an average test). Meta shipped its first Muse model in April and now has an answer for every tier OpenAI and Anthropic sell.

7. Google announced 2 new AI chips coming next year: the TPU 8tx, which keeps data encrypted even while a model is working on it, and the 8i Max, which joins 2 chips into one for agents that need to hold an entire codebase in view. Google already has nearly 100 TPU customers (including Anthropic and Apple) and every available chip is spoken for. 

8. Nvidia's top lawyer reportedly emailed agents in August 2025 while they were investigating whether Singapore's Megaspeed smuggled its chips to China. The Commerce Department then halted the case and handed it to the Justice Department. Not a great week for Nvidia.

9. Adobe signed a multi-year deal with Disney to build custom AI models trained on Disney's characters and visual styles, with work already underway for theme parks, film, and ESPN. Pretty interesting to see one of the most protective IP owners in entertainment is now training its own AI models.

10. OpenAI acquired Odessia, a months-old AI trip-planning startup from Sonder founder Francis Davidson, who is joining OpenAI to work on travel. Between this and #3, ChatGPT is coming for shopping and travel.

11. France unveiled the Paris Call for AI Safety and Security, with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Mistral committing to build emergency off switches into their most advanced models. Interesting timing given #1 on this list.

Daily reminder that this is the worst AI will ever be.

Bot 1.0 is out. Our goal for this release was to make Bots a much more useful part of your team.

Some new things we're excited about:

- Bots can now join Zoom, Google Meet, and more. You can ask Bot questions in meetings and even assign it action items. We have ours taking standup notes every day in our shared Google Doc and doing background research on discussion themes. Soon, you'll be able to talk back and forth with it live in a meeting.

- A new interface for managing your Bots. You can see and steer their responsibilities, what they're learning, and their impact. It's impossible to build trust in an AI teammate if it's a black box, so it should proactively flag when it's blocked or confused, take and learn from feedback across the company, and be able to succinctly summarize its contributions.

- Better collaboration in Slack and Teams. Bots are more ambiently aware, carry context across conversations, and learn from your team over time. In our Slack, we regularly see threads between members of our team and multiple Bots, handing off work, context, and decisions. Bots should intuit your company's customs and how work gets done, not just execute on the specific tasks they're given.

Our message to Nvidia's board:

Do not fire Jensen Huang.

There is no clear replacement for Jensen Huang. We are confident that his departure would ultimately be a net negative for Nvidia, its shareholders, and the AI Revolution.

First, take a look at the data. History also suggests that removing a successful CEO will come with a significant cost.

A study of 187 forced CEO departures from S&P 1500 companies found that removing outperforming CEOs resulted in negative long-term stock returns. This case would be no different, in our view.

Jensen Huang is the definition of an outperforming CEO. Nvidia's board must not make a decision in the heat of the moment.

The board should take the time to conduct a thorough investigation and consult with shareholders, with a strong emphasis on the latter.

Quite literally, Nvidia's board should convene a special shareholder meeting and hold an advisory vote on this decision. This is the most consequential CEO controversy in world history. Shareholders deserve a say.

In addition, Nvidia's stock, $NVDA, is now down -35% in 26 trading days, nearly half of which is a result of the recent scandal.

We believe Jensen Huang's potential removal as CEO is now ~80% priced in.

Why take an action with massive downside potential when the market has already priced in much of that risk?

The downside of retaining Huang may be limited, while the potential upside is tremendous.

Lastly, history shows that retaining Jensen Huang could still lead to a favorable outcome. In 2019, Amazon retained Jeff Bezos as CEO after his extramarital affair became public, and the company's stock subsequently surged +108% by 2021.

Personal misconduct should not be ignored, but it must also be distinguished from corporate wrongdoing and weighed against the consequences of removing an executive who is instrumental to the company's success.

We believe Jensen Huang is an irreplaceable part of Nvidia and the AI Revolution more broadly.

Once the dust settles, firing Jensen Huang would prove to be a costly mistake.

It is time to pause and consult your shareholders.

text:
One of my recent favorite use cases for Claude in Excel is to use it as a way to catch up on stocks or companies that you stopped tracking

If you last screened the stock a few months ago and then stopped tracking the business because it was a pass at the time, your Excel file is likely a few quarters stale already.

In the meantime, you also missed out on relevant news flow and developments in the company. 

In these situations, I will just open the latest Excel file with financials I have on it and then have Claude catch me up on anything I have missed since the file was last updated

You can obviously build your own prompt, but the one I use is below.

"Since the file was last updated, give me all relevant news flow, earnings commentary, and corporate actions in the business. Include any details around changes in management, M&A decisions or rumors, changes in reporting style or segments of the business, and any other relevant footnotes included in 10Ks/Qs since then. Once completed, update the financials to be the latest and refresh any other tabs in this file that still remain stale."

Great way to quickly catch up on everything you missed about the company since you last looked at it

🚨 BREAKING: NVIDIA CEO JENSEN HUANG RELEASES A STATEMENT AMID ALLEGATIONS OF A SEXUAL AFFAIR WITH KIMBERLY POWELL, DENIES ALLOWING UNVERIFIED CLAIMS TO DEFINE HIS LEGACY!

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly addressed the growing controversy surrounding allegations of an affair with Kimberly Powell, breaking his silence as the reports continue to attract widespread public attention. In his statement, Huang stressed that allegations should not automatically be treated as established facts.

Huang emphasized that his success at Nvidia was built through years of hard work, sacrifice and dedication to innovation. He maintained that his primary responsibility remains leading the company, supporting its employees, serving shareholders and ensuring Nvidia continues to shape the future of technology.

He also defended Kimberly Powell, urging the public to treat her with dignity and respect rather than subjecting her to personal attacks based on unverified allegations. He argued that any workplace-related concerns should be handled through appropriate procedures, fairness and evidence rather than social media speculation and public judgment.

Addressing reports surrounding an alleged incident at a San Jose conference, Huang suggested that photographs, videos and eyewitness accounts should not be taken out of context or automatically used to draw conclusions about his private life or professional conduct.

He concluded by insisting that Nvidia’s achievements, employees and technological innovations should not be overshadowed by sensational headlines. However, questions surrounding the allegations are likely to continue attracting attention as the controversy develops.
